docs.title: Components
docs.text:
StatsComponent(nlp, name)

The base of the components of spaCy that put the statistics of a text into an extension of Doc: a component registers the extension when added to a pipeline and puts the statistics of every document into doc._.<name>. Writing components in general is described in the documentation of spaCy.

The components of ruTS are subclasses of the StatsComponent of the anyTS core, one for every class of statistics.

Note

The examples below use the ru_core_news_sm model, which is installed separately: python -m spacy download ru_core_news_sm (see installation).

CodeResult 
import ruts
import spacy

nlp = spacy.load("ru_core_news_sm")
nlp.add_pipe("ruts_basic", name="basic")
nlp("мама мыла раму")._.basic.c_letters
nlp("?!")._.basic is None

{4: 3}
True

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description nlp Language - Pipeline the component is added to name str - Name of the component in the pipeline and of the extension

spaCy sets both at nlp.add_pipe(factory, name=...); the other parameters of a component are passed in the config dictionary of the same call.

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
The factories carry the prefix of the library: ruts_basic, ruts_readability, ruts_unadapted_readability, ruts_diversity, ruts_morph, ruts_syntax, ruts_cohesion, ruts_lexical, ruts_style, ruts_phon, ruts_verse, and the component of sentence boundaries ruts_blank_lines. They are declared as entry points of spacy_factories, so a pipeline saved with these components (nlp.to_disk(path)) loads with spacy.load(path) without import ruts. import ruts does not load the components while spaCy is not loaded - the entry points find them; from the sources without an installed package, import ruts.components comes before add_pipe.

The name of the pipe is the name of the extension: nlp.add_pipe(factory, name="basic") puts the statistics into doc._.basic. Without name both take the name of the factory. The extension follows the pipe when the pipeline renames it (nlp.rename_pipe). A name taken by an extension of another package raises ParameterError instead of replacing it: at add_pipe, or at the first document after rename_pipe, which renames the pipe before the component learns its name. A component taken from another pipeline (add_pipe(name, source=other)) is the same object in both, so under a new name it writes to that extension in the other pipeline too; a separate component comes from the factory, add_pipe(factory, name=...). The same component can be added twice under different names, with different parameters. A document with no words - an empty string, whitespace, punctuation alone - passes through a component untouched, its extension left at None.

In ruts_lexical a document of numbers alone passes untouched as well, and in ruts_verse a document without letters.

Serialization

A component keeps an object of statistics in doc._.<name>, and spaCy cannot serialize it: Doc.to_bytes(), DocBin(store_user_data=True) and nlp.pipe(..., n_process>1) fail with these components in the pipeline. To save a document, leave the user data out (doc.to_bytes(exclude=["user_data"])) or keep doc._.<name>.get_stats() separately; for multiprocessing compute the statistics in the main process after nlp.pipe, without the components.

Adding a component extends the tokenizer of its pipeline with the rules for the dialogue dashes glued to words (ruts.utils.add_dash_rules), so that a Doc is split into words the same way as a string; for your own pipeline without ruTS components call this function yourself.

ruTS removes stress marks from the words of a Doc, but the parts of speech, features and dependencies come from the model, which sees a word with a mark as unknown and tags it worse: on a text after accentuate the ru_core_news_sm model changes the part of speech of over half of the words. Pass a text with stresses to the pipeline without them - nlp(ruts.utils.strip_marks(text)).

docs.title: Basic statistics
docs.text:
BasicStatsComponent(nlp, name)

BasicStatsComponent puts the basic statistics of a document into its extension.

docs.title: Morphological statistics
docs.text:
MorphStatsComponent(nlp, name)

MorphStatsComponent puts the morphological statistics into the extension; by default they need the parts of speech before it.

In ruTS the parts of speech and the features are taken from the model annotation (token.pos_, token.morph), and in a pipeline without morphologizer from pymorphy3.

CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ruts_morph", name="morph")
nlp("мама мыла раму")._.morph.case

('Nom', None, 'Acc')

docs.title: Readability metrics
docs.text:
ReadabilityStatsComponent(nlp, name, preset=None, basic=None)

ReadabilityStatsComponent puts the readability metrics into the extension, computed from the document or, with basic, from the basic statistics another component put into it. A library sets basic_factory, the factory of its component of the basic statistics, which the error names when that extension holds none.

Parameter Type Default Description preset str None Preset of the coefficients, one of the presets of the class; the default of the class if None basic str None Extension of a component of the basic statistics to reuse instead of computing them again

With preset left at None the config of a saved pipeline holds no preset, and the pipeline takes the default of the class when it is loaded; a library that wants its default written into the config gives it in the signature of its subclass.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - a stats_class that is not concrete, a preset that is not a string or not one of the class, an extension not named by a string;
  • SourceTypeError - a class without basic_stats_class and no basic;
  • SourceError - a document whose extension basic holds no basic statistics of the class.

The presets of ruTS are plainrussian, fiction and academic, the preset of the class plainrussian. In ruTS the class of statistics and its basic_stats_class are set, so the errors of stats_class and SourceTypeError do not occur; the message of SourceError names the component ruts_basic (basic_factory) to add before it.

CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ruts_readability", name="readability")
config = {"preset": "fiction", "basic": "basic"}
nlp.add_pipe("ruts_readability", name="readability_fiction", config=config)
doc = nlp("Кот сидел на окне и смотрел на птиц, которые летали над крышами домов.")

docs.title: Formulas of other languages
docs.text:
UnadaptedReadabilityStatsComponent(nlp, name, basic=None)

UnadaptedReadabilityStatsComponent puts the readability formulas of other languages into the extension, computed from the document or, with basic, from the basic statistics another component put into it. A library sets basic_factory, as for ReadabilityStatsComponent.

Parameter Type Default Description basic str None Extension of a component of the basic statistics to reuse instead of computing them again

Raises:

  • ParameterError - a stats_class that is not concrete, an extension not named by a string;
  • SourceTypeError - a class without basic_stats_class and no basic;
  • SourceError - a document whose extension basic holds no basic statistics of the class.

The formulas are those of UnadaptedReadabilityStats, with their original coefficients and without a calibration for Russian. As for ReadabilityStatsComponent, the errors of stats_class and SourceTypeError do not occur in ruTS, and the message of SourceError names the component ruts_basic to add before it.

CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ruts_unadapted_readability", name="unadapted", config={"basic": "basic"})
doc = nlp("Кот сидел на окне и смотрел на птиц, которые летали над крышами домов.")
doc._.unadapted.gulpease, doc._.unadapted.forcast
doc._.unadapted.bs is doc._.basic

(69.0, 13.076923076923077)
True

docs.title: Lexical diversity metrics
docs.text:
DiversityStatsComponent(nlp, name, window_len=50, mtld_threshold=0.72, mtld_min_len=10, hdd_sample_size=42, log_base=10)

DiversityStatsComponent puts the lexical diversity metrics into the extension, by a class of the library that reads a Doc. Its parameters are those of DiversityStats, with the same defaults.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - a wrong parameter (check_params of the diversity).
Parameter Type Default Description window_len int 50 Window size for MATTR and segment size for MSTTR mtld_threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for MTLD, MA-MTLD and MTLD-W mtld_min_len int 10 Minimum factor length for MTLD, MA-MTLD and MTLD-W hdd_sample_size int 42 Sample size for HD-D log_base float 10 Logarithm base for the Summer, Maas and Dugast metrics CodeResult 
config = {"window_len": 100, "log_base": 2.718281828459045}
nlp.add_pipe("ruts_diversity", name="diversity", config=config)
nlp("мама мыла раму")._.diversity.rttr

1.7320508075688774

docs.title: SEO style metrics
docs.text:
StyleStatsComponent(nlp, name, stopwords=None, top_n=10, nausea_stopwords=None, cliches=None)

StyleStatsComponent puts the style metrics into the extension.

Parameter Type Default Description stopwords list[str] None Stopwords of the water content; those of the class if None top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words of the academic nausea and of the naturalness by Zipf's law (NAUSEA_TOP_N) nausea_stopwords list[str] None Words left out of the most frequent words of the academic nausea; those of the class if None cliches list[str] None Cliches; those of the class (cliches_list) if None

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - stopwords, nausea stopwords or cliches that are not a list of strings;
  • ParameterError - a top_n that is not an integer of at least one.

Without the lists the water words and the stopwords of the nausea are determined by the pymorphy3 tags, and the cliches come from OFFICIALESE_CLICHES; NAUSEA_TOP_N is a constant of anyts.constants.

CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ruts_style", name="style", config={"stopwords": ["и", "в", "не"], "top_n": 5})
nlp("мама мыла раму")._.style.water
nlp.add_pipe("ruts_style", name="style_cliches", config={"cliches": ["в целях", "в рамках"]})
nlp("В целях экономии в рамках проекта мы закрыли склад.")._.style_cliches.cliches

0.0
22.22222222222222

PhonStatsComponent(nlp, name, window_len=3)

PhonStatsComponent puts the phonetic statistics into the extension; window_len (PHON_WINDOW_LEN by default) is the window in words of the alliteration and the assonance.

Raises:

nlp.add_pipe("ruts_phon", name="phon", config={"window_len": 5})
nlp("мама мыла раму")._.phon.p_open_syllables

docs.title: Syntactic statistics
docs.text:
SyntaxStatsComponent(nlp, name)

SyntaxStatsComponent puts the syntactic statistics into the extension; they need a parser and the parts of speech before it.

The ru_core_news_sm, ru_core_news_md and ru_core_news_lg models have a parser and the parts of speech.

Raises:

  • SourceError - a document without a dependency parse or parts of speech, in a pipeline without a parser or morphologizer.
CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ruts_syntax", name="syntax")
nlp("Дом, построенный рабочими в прошлом году, был продан")._.syntax.tree_depth

4.0

docs.title: Cohesion statistics
docs.text:
CohesionStatsComponent(nlp, name)

CohesionStatsComponent puts the cohesion statistics into the extension. It needs no parser, and a Doc without sentence boundaries is split into sentences by the Russian SentsExtractor; when annotation is present, parts of speech are taken from it, lemmas - from pymorphy3 by the token's part of speech, without annotation - from the first pymorphy3 analysis.

CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ruts_cohesion", name="cohesion")
doc = nlp("Кот сидел на окне. Он смотрел на птиц. Птицы улетели, и кот уснул.")
doc._.cohesion.noun_overlap_adjacent

0.5

docs.title: Lexical sophistication statistics
docs.text:
LexicalStatsComponent(nlp, name, data_dir=None)

LexicalStatsComponent puts the lexical sophistication statistics into the extension. The frequency dictionary metrics require a downloaded FreqDict; the bands and lexical density are computed without it.

Parameter Type Default Description data_dir str None Path to the frequency dictionary directory; if not given, the default directory is used

Raises:

  • DatasetNotFoundError - the frequency dictionary metrics and get_stats() when FreqDict is not downloaded.
CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ruts_lexical", name="lexical")
nlp("Кот сидел на окне и смотрел на птиц")._.lexical.p_top1000

0.75

docs.title: Verse statistics
docs.text:
VerseStatsComponent(nlp, name, data_dir=None)

VerseStatsComponent puts the verse statistics into the extension; it requires a downloaded StressDict stress dictionary. The component works on the Doc text with line breaks, so pass the poem text to nlp as is, without joining the lines. A text with letters but without Russian words gives empty statistics, like VerseStats, so nlp.pipe over a corpus does not stop on it.

Parameter Type Default Description data_dir str None Path to the stress dictionary directory; if not given, the default directory is used

Raises:

  • DatasetNotFoundError - the stress dictionary is not downloaded; the first document with letters raises it.
CodeResult 
nlp.add_pipe("ruts_verse", name="verse")
poem = (
    "Буря мглою небо кроет,\nВихри снежные крутя;\n"
    "То, как зверь, она завоет,\nТо заплачет, как дитя"
)
doc = nlp(poem)
doc._.verse.meter, doc._.verse.n_feet

('хорей', 4)

docs.title: Sentences after blank lines
docs.text:
start_sents_after_blank_lines(doc)

A component that starts a sentence at the first token after a blank line - a line break, optional whitespace and another line break - so that a heading, a list item or a paragraph without a final mark is a sentence of its own, as in the sentence extractor. It goes before the parser, senter or sentencizer, which keeps its starts and places the others. The whitespace before such a start stays with the sentence before it, and the marks that open a paragraph (a dash of a dialogue, ¡, «) stay with its first word. Alone, the component leaves the sentences within a paragraph unsplit and sets partial boundaries (has_sents), so the statistics take the sentences of such a document from its text. A parsed document, such as one passed through the pipeline again, passes untouched, since spaCy keeps its sentences. A language library registers the component under its prefix, Language.component("<prefix>_blank_lines", func=start_sents_after_blank_lines).

Parameter Type Default Description doc Doc - Doc object

In ruTS the component is registered as ruts_blank_lines. Without it the ru_core_news_sm model glues a paragraph without a final mark to the next sentence, and the statistics of a Doc differ from those of the same string.

CodeResult 
nlp = spacy.load("ru_core_news_sm")
nlp.add_pipe("ruts_blank_lines", before="parser")
[sent.text.strip() for sent in nlp("Что нового\n\nБыстрый импорт. Меньше ошибок").sents]

['Что нового', 'Быстрый импорт.', 'Меньше ошибок']

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Jupyter notebooks in the examples/ directory of the repository. Each opens in Google Colab with a button and installs the library and the spaCy model itself; the outputs of all cells are stored in the files, so the notebooks can be read without running.

docs.title: Text walkthrough
docs.text: 01_text_walkthrough.ipynb - Chekhov's short story "The Death of a Government Clerk" through every tool of the library in turn: sentence and word extraction, basic statistics, readability with coefficient presets, lexical diversity and windowed computation, morphology, SEO style metrics on fiction and on officialese, phonostatistics, syntax and cohesion from the spaCy parse, lexical sophistication by the frequency dictionary, highlighting, Zipf's law and the sentence length curve. At the end all statistics are attached as spaCy components, and a single nlp.pipe pass over the TextsByGrade dataset yields a table of statistics by text grade. The notebook is in Russian.

docs.title: Text complexity by school grade
docs.text: 02_text_complexity_by_grade.ipynb - the 68 TextsByGrade texts labelled with grades 1 to 17 as a single complexity axis onto which every group of statistics is laid in turn: Spearman correlation of the eleven readability formulas with the label and their error in grades, three coefficient presets, lexical diversity (unrelated to grade) versus lexical sophistication by the frequency dictionary, syntax and morphology (nominal load, tree depth, passive, share of verbs), cohesion, distributions by school stage and a check on the independent first-grade reader SovChLit. The notebook is in Russian.

docs.title: Pairwise comparison of prose writers
docs.text: 03_prose_authors.ipynb - ten prose writers of RussianLiterature, up to 200 windows of 1000 words per writer, the text_features and Cliff's delta for 45 pairs: the three strongest features of every pair, a detailed look at Tolstoy and Dostoevsky (compare_features, feature distributions, keywords - speech against narration), the number of large-effect features as a distance (from 4 for Turgenev-Chekhov to 59 for Herzen-Chekhov), edition features (quotes, the letter ё) that must be excluded, universal discriminators (semicolons, ellipses, commas, windowed diversity measures), dendrogram and multidimensional scaling by features and by Burrows's delta with a Mantel test, authorship attribution of 1000-word windows with held-out works (delta variants, number of frequent words, word forms against character trigrams, text features as a classifier, confusion matrix, Zeta markers). The notebook is in Russian.

docs.title: Stalin's language over half a century
docs.text: 04_stalin_corpus.ipynb - corpus measures as tools of diachrony on StalinWorks (1243 texts from 1901 to 1952, four periods): keywords against the frequency dictionary and lemmatization artefacts when comparing with an external dictionary, keywords of the periods and keyness_plot of the two extreme periods, collocates of the words «враг» (enemy) and «партия» (party) by period via collocations with node, dispersion of words over the volumes and dispersion_plot as a timeline, the kwic concordance by lemma, Zipf's law and windowed MTLD for every period. The notebook is in Russian.

docs.title: Verse and sound
docs.text: 05_poetry.ipynb - verse statistics and phonostatistics on PoetryCorpus (16,694 poems, 18th-20th centuries): the Onegin stanza through VerseStats (stresses, cC patterns, ABABCCDDEFFEGG, line endings, stress profile), meters by era and the number of feet in iambs (the alexandrine of the 18th century, the peak of iamb under Pushkin, ternary meters from the 1840s, dolniks and accentual verse of the 20th century as meter None), the stress profile of the iambic tetrameter of Lomonosov, Pushkin and Blok against Taranovsky's manual counts, meters by author, quatrain rhyme schemes and line endings by era, blank and free verse, stressed vowels and textbook sound painting, alliteration indices and "hardness" by author, alliteration highlighting, a check of stresses and rhymes on the RIFMA dataset. The notebook is in Russian.

docs.title: Running locally
docs.text:
uv sync --group examples
uv run jupyter lab examples/

make notebooks executes all notebooks, writes the outputs into the files and strips the execution metadata; the examples.yml workflow runs the notebooks on a schedule and on demand.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
All library exceptions inherit the base class RutsError and one of the built-in Python classes, so they can be caught both by their ruTS name and by the familiar built-in type - existing code with except ValueError keeps working.

Exception Built-in class When raised RutsError Exception Base class, never raised itself SourceTypeError TypeError The data source is neither a string nor a Doc, the frequency counter is not a Counter, the list of texts is not a list of lists, the path is neither a string nor a Path, the tokenizer is not callable SourceError ValueError The source has no words, sentences, texts or collocations, lacks a dependency parse, has fewer texts than the measure needs, or nothing is left after culling ParameterError ValueError A threshold, window, segment size or number of items is out of range; an unknown measure, variant, preset, layer, stage or dataset category UnknownStatError ParameterError, KeyError An unknown statistic is requested by name (describe of the statistics classes, get_stats, print_stats and explain_text of MorphStats, DiversityStats.windowed, describe_level_norm) DatasetNotFoundError OSError The dataset is not downloaded; the message shows the download command DataFileError ValueError A dataset file is corrupted, has an unexpected format or cannot be decoded DownloadError RuntimeError The file could not be downloaded or failed the checksum verification

The classes are available from ruts and from ruts.exceptions. They are the classes of the anyTS core under the same names, RutsError being its anyts.exceptions.AnyTSError: aliases, not subclasses, so except RutsError catches the errors raised by the code of the core too, and a traceback shows anyts.exceptions.SourceError. The messages of ruTS are in Russian, the messages of the statistics classes, the extractors, the components and the highlighting built on the core included (ruts.constants.CORE_MESSAGES). English remain the checks of the types of arguments in the code of the core (a string instead of a number and the like) and some functions of the core.

CodeResult 
from ruts import BasicStats, RutsError, SourceError
from ruts.datasets import PoetryCorpus

try:
    BasicStats("...")
except SourceError as e:
    print(e)

try:
    list(PoetryCorpus(data_dir="/nowhere").get_texts(limit=1))
except RutsError as e:
    print(type(e).__name__)

В источнике данных отсутствуют слова
DatasetNotFoundError

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
The library prints nothing on its own: the anyTS core sends messages about downloading and extracting datasets (the download() methods) to the anyts logger at the INFO level. The logger has a NullHandler by default, so the messages are silent; to see them, configure logging in your application:

CodeResult 
import logging

from ruts.datasets import SovChLit

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(name)s: %(message)s")
SovChLit(data_dir="/tmp/ruts_data").download()

anyts.datasets: Downloading the file https://github.com/SergeyShk/ruTS/raw/master/ruts/datasets/data/sov_chrest_lit_v1.tar.xz
anyts.datasets: The file is downloaded: /tmp/ruts_data/sov_chrest_lit_v1.tar.xz
anyts.datasets: Extracting the archive /tmp/ruts_data/sov_chrest_lit_v1.tar.xz

The print_stats() methods of the statistics classes and print_kwic() write to standard output by design; logging does not affect them.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: The library can be installed with pip or by cloning the project repository with git.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
ruTS relies on the following third-party libraries:

  • python - 3.11 or newer
  • anyts - 0.3.6 or newer within 0.3, the language-independent core ruTS is built on
  • pymorphy3 with the Russian dictionaries pymorphy3-dicts-ru
  • razdel
  • scipy
  • spaCy - 3.8.15 or newer
  • numpy
  • pandas
  • matplotlib
  • graphviz

docs.title: Installing with pip
docs.text:
Run in the command line:

pip install ruts

This installs the release version of the library with all dependencies.

Graphviz

The graphviz package among the dependencies is only a wrapper: rendering the word tree and the collocation network requires the Graphviz executables (brew install graphviz, apt install graphviz, conda install graphviz), otherwise render() and displaying the graph in Jupyter fail with ExecutableNotFound. Nothing else needs them.

Fast morphological analysis

For corpora, install the library with the fast extra:

pip install "ruts[fast]"

It adds the DAWG2 C extension for pymorphy3 (CPython only, wheels are available for Linux, macOS and Windows): word form analysis gets about 5x faster (175 vs 34 thousand word forms per second), MorphStats on a 70-thousand-word text about a third faster, because analyses are cached per word form and the rest of the time goes into counting. Without the extra the library works the same, just slower.

import ruts loads neither spaCy nor matplotlib nor pandas: spaCy comes with a Doc object or a component, and the plots and the corpus functions on first use. The statistics of a string work without them.

spaCy model

The spaCy components, the syntactic statistics and the examples that start with spacy.load("ru_core_news_sm") need the Russian-language model; without it spacy.load fails with OSError: [E050]. The model is installed separately:

python -m spacy download ru_core_news_sm

The larger models ru_core_news_md and ru_core_news_lg make no sense for ruTS statistics: in our measurements on the gold Universal Dependencies annotation (Taiga and GSD) they are less than one UAS point more accurate than sm, the text-level statistics of the three models coincide (correlation above 0.95 for 40 of 53), and they weigh 93 and 670 MB against 47.

Datasets

The datasets are downloaded by default into the ruts_data directory next to the package (DEFAULT_DATA_DIR in ruts.constants): for an installation from a wheel that is site-packages/ruts_data, where writing may be forbidden for a system Python. In that case pass your own directory in the data_dir argument when creating a dataset or set the environment variable RUTS_DATA_DIR before the package is imported:

export RUTS_DATA_DIR=~/ruts_data

Note

A detailed guide to the pip package manager is available on its website.

docs.title: Installing with git
docs.text:
This way you get the latest version of the library straight from the project repository. Run the following commands:

  1. Clone the repository into a local directory:

    git clone https://github.com/SergeyShk/ruTS.git

  2. Change into it:

    cd ruTS

  3. Install the library into the current environment:

    pip install .

    For development it is more convenient to use uv, which creates an isolated environment and installs all dependencies, including the development tools:

    uv sync --all-groups --no-group examples

    The examples group with Jupyter is needed only for the example notebooks.

Note

A detailed guide to the git version control system is available on its website.

docs.title: Syllables and stress
docs.text: The ruts.syllables module divides a Russian word into syllables and finds its stressed syllable: syllables by rules, the stress by the StressDict dictionary. The basic, phonetic and verse statistics and the readability formulas are built on these functions. Stress marks and soft hyphens are removed from the word (ruts.utils.strip_marks), and a stress given by a mark (за́мок, замо́к) overrides the dictionary.

docs.title: Syllabification
docs.text:
syllabify(word)

Division of a word into syllables by the rising sonority rule (Avanesov): there are as many syllables as vowels, a word without vowels (в, к, с) has none. The syllable boundary follows these rules:

Rule Example a single consonant between vowels goes to the next syllable ко-ро-ва, ра-йон a cluster of obstruents, or an obstruent followed by a sonorant, goes to the next syllable ко-шка, се-стра, о-ткрыть, по-зна-ко-мить a sonorant before an obstruent goes to the previous syllable кар-та, пол-ка the boundary goes between two sonorants вол-на, кар-ман й before a consonant goes to the previous syllable май-ка, вой-на ь and ъ go with the preceding letter боль-шой, по-дъезд every vowel of a hiatus forms its own syllable а-э-ро-порт, а-ист

The division is orthographic, by letters, as in school phonetics; a compound word is divided part by part (со-рок-во-ро-вка).

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a word that is not a string.
CodeResult 
from ruts.syllables import syllabify

syllabify("здравствуйте")

['здра', 'вствуй', 'те']

docs.title: Syllable count
docs.text:
count_syllables(word)

The number of syllables of a word - the number of vowel letters.

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a word that is not a string.
CodeResult 
from ruts.syllables import count_syllables

count_syllables("здравствуйте")

3

docs.title: Stressed syllable
docs.text:
word_stress(word, stress_dict=None)

The number of the stressed syllable of a word, counting from zero: by the letter ё, the only syllable of a monosyllable, otherwise by the dictionary (step 1 of the algorithm of the verse statistics); for a compound word, the last of the stresses of word_stresses.

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word stress_dict StressDict None Stress dictionary; StressDict() by default

Returns None if the word is not found or has no vowels.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a word that is not a string, a stress dictionary of another type;
  • DatasetNotFoundError - the stress dictionary is not downloaded.
CodeResult 
from ruts.syllables import syllabify, word_stress

word_stress("корова"), word_stress("ещё"), word_stress("желанье"), word_stress("кто-нибудь")
word_stress("за́мок"), word_stress("замо́к"), word_stress("сорок-воровка")
word_stress("хмурота"), word_stress("в")
syllabify("корова")[word_stress("корова")]

(1, 1, 1, 0)
(0, 1, 3)
(None, None)
'ро'

docs.title: All stresses
docs.text:
word_stresses(word, stress_dict=None)

All stressed syllables of a word in ascending order. A hyphenated compound that the dictionary lacks as a whole gets the stress of every content part (со-рок-во-ро-вка - 0 and 3), the particles (-то, -либо, -нибудь and others) are unstressed.

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word stress_dict StressDict None Stress dictionary; StressDict() by default

Returns an empty list if the word is not found or has no vowels.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a word that is not a string, a stress dictionary of another type;
  • DatasetNotFoundError - the stress dictionary is not downloaded.
CodeResult 
from ruts.syllables import word_stresses

word_stresses("сорок-воровка"), word_stresses("северо-западный"), word_stresses("кто-нибудь")

([0, 3], [3], [0])

docs.title: Ending type
docs.text:
stress_type(word, stress_dict=None)

The type of the ending of a word by the position of its main stress. The names are those of verse clausulas (VERSE_CLAUSULAS):

Type Stress Example мужская (masculine) on the last syllable зем-ля женская (feminine) on the penultimate syllable ко-ро-ва дактилическая (dactylic) on the third syllable from the end зо-ло-то гипердактилическая (hyperdactylic) earlier вы-ско-чи-вший Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word stress_dict StressDict None Stress dictionary; StressDict() by default

Returns None if the word is not found or has no vowels.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a word that is not a string, a stress dictionary of another type;
  • DatasetNotFoundError - the stress dictionary is not downloaded.
CodeResult 
from ruts.syllables import stress_type

tuple(stress_type(word) for word in ("земля", "корова", "золото", "выскочивший"))

('мужская', 'женская', 'дактилическая', 'гипердактилическая')

docs.title: Collocations
docs.text:
collocations(words, window=5, measure='logdice', min_freq=2, node=None, top_n=None, side=None)

Collocation extraction - pairs of words that occur together more often than independence would give: fixed expressions, terminology, the combinatorics of a word. The measures of association are those of Sketch Engine and of nltk.metrics.association.

Pairs are ordered, as in NLTK: the right word occurs at most window words after the left one, each pair of positions counted once; window=1 gives bigrams. The measures take the pair frequency divided by the window (Church and Hanks 1990, as in NLTK), which keeps the expected frequency independent of the window and Dice and the minimum sensitivity at most one; freq_pair stays undivided. So with window > 1 an always adjacent pair gets a logDice of \(14 - \log_2 window\) (13 at a window of 2), not 14 as in Sketch Engine with its raw co-occurrence; 14 needs a pair at every distance within the window. node keeps the pairs with the given word on either side, and side on one of them: "left" the collocates before the node, "right" those after it.

Words are compared as they are: case, lemmatization and stop words belong to the word extractor; lemmas suit fixed expressions, word forms suit grammatical constructions.

The function wraps collocations of the anyTS core and strips stress marks from the words and from node. Words are extracted with WordsExtractor; for Russian fixed expressions such as «точка зрения» or «рабочий класс» take its lemmas (use_lexemes=True).

CodeResult 
from ruts import WordsExtractor
from ruts.corpus import collocations

words = WordsExtractor(use_lexemes=True, lowercase=True).extract(
    "Кот сидел на окне и смотрел на птиц. Птицы улетели, и кот уснул на окне. "
    "Завтра кот снова будет сидеть на окне и смотреть на птиц."
)

collocations(words, window=2, top_n=1)
[
    (c.left, c.right, round(c.score, 2))
    for c in collocations(words, window=1, node="кот", min_freq=1, measure="mi")[:2]
]

[Collocation(left='птица', right='улететь', freq_left=3, freq_right=1, freq_pair=2, score=13.0)]
[('завтра', 'кот', 3.12), ('кот', 'снова', 3.12)]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order window int 5 Greatest distance between the words of a pair measure str 'logdice' Measure of anyts.constants.COLLOCATION_MEASURES min_freq int 2 Minimum frequency of a pair node str None Word whose combinatorics is needed; None - every pair top_n int None Number of collocations; None - all of them side str None With a node, the side of its collocates: "left" or "right"; None - both

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, and no words SourceError. An unknown measure, a window or a top_n that is not an integer of at least one, a min_freq that is not an integer, a node that is not a string, and a side other than "left" and "right" or without a node raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Collocation(left, right, freq_left, freq_right, freq_pair, score)

A list of Collocation named tuples by descending measure and frequency of the pair (ties broken alphabetically); pd.DataFrame(found) gives a table.

Field Type Description left str Left word right str Right word, occurring within the window after the left one freq_left int Frequency of the left word freq_right int Frequency of the right word freq_pair int Frequency of the co-occurrence score float Value of the chosen measure

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
The measures of measure by key, with their names and descriptions in anyts.constants.COLLOCATION_MEASURES:

Key Measures Range Higher means mi Frequency of the pair against the expected one, in bits Any number A stronger association mi3 MI with the frequency of the pair cubed Any number A stronger association t_score Difference of the observed and the expected frequency of the pair Any number A surer association dice Share of the pair in the occurrences of the two words 0-1 A stronger association logdice Dice coefficient on a logarithmic scale 14 and below A stronger association log_likelihood Significance of the association 0 and above, nan when a word fills the text or a cell is negative A more significant departure from independence, for attracted and avoided pairs alike npmi MI normalized by the information of the pair −1 to 1 A stronger association min_sensitivity Smaller share of the pair in the occurrences of either word 0-1 A stronger association

Every measure is a function of the module anyts.corpus.collocations of the frequencies of the words and of the pair and the number of words:

Parameter Type Default Description freq_a int - Frequency \(f_a\) of the first word freq_b int - Frequency \(f_b\) of the second word freq_ab float - Frequency \(f_{ab}\) of the pair n int - Number of words \(N\) of the text

A pair of zero frequency gives nan for MI, MI³, the t-score, logDice and NPMI.

The module ruts.corpus.collocations re-exports the functions of the measures (from ruts.corpus.collocations import calc_logdice).

docs.title: Mutual information
docs.text:
mi · Church and Hanks (1990)

calc_mi(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The pointwise mutual information of the two words; it overrates rare pairs.

\[ \log_2 \frac{f_{ab} N}{f_a f_b} \]

docs.title: MI³
docs.text:
mi3 · Oakes (1998)

calc_mi3(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The mutual information with the frequency of the pair cubed, which favours frequent pairs.

\[ \log_2 \frac{f_{ab}^3 N}{f_a f_b} \]

docs.title: t-score
docs.text:
t_score · Church et al. (1991)

calc_t_score(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The difference of the observed and the expected frequency of the pair over the root of the observed one; it favours frequent pairs.

\[ \frac{f_{ab} - f_a f_b / N}{\sqrt{f_{ab}}} \]

docs.title: Dice coefficient
docs.text:
dice

calc_dice(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The share of the pair in the occurrences of the two words; it does not depend on the size of the text.

\[ \frac{2 f_{ab}}{f_a + f_b} \]

docs.title: logDice
docs.text:
logdice · Rychlý (2008)

calc_logdice(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The Dice coefficient on a binary logarithmic scale, the default measure, as in Sketch Engine. It does not depend on the size of the text; below zero the link is weak.

\[ 14 + \log_2 \frac{2 f_{ab}}{f_a + f_b} \]

docs.title: Log-likelihood
docs.text:
log_likelihood · Dunning (1993)

calc_log_likelihood(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

\(G^2\) over the 2×2 contingency table of the two words: the observed frequencies \(O\) - \(f_{ab}\), \(f_a - f_{ab}\), \(f_b - f_{ab}\) and \(N - f_a - f_b + f_{ab}\) - against the expected ones \(E\) under independence. A word that fills the whole text, or a negative cell, as of a word paired with itself in a window above one, gives nan.

\[ G^2 = 2 \sum O \ln \frac{O}{E} \]

docs.title: NPMI
docs.text:
npmi · Bouma (2009)

calc_npmi(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The mutual information normalized by the information of the pair: one means the words occur only together. A pair as frequent as the text is long gives nan.

\[ \frac{MI}{-\log_2 (f_{ab} / N)} \]

docs.title: Minimum sensitivity
docs.text:
min_sensitivity · Pedersen (1998)

calc_min_sensitivity(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The smaller of the shares of the pair in the occurrences of each word.

\[ \min\left(\frac{f_{ab}}{f_a}, \frac{f_{ab}}{f_b}\right) \]

docs.title: Corpus comparison
docs.text:
compare_corpora(a, b, window=1000, features=None, labels=('A', 'B'), n_bootstrap=1000, seed=0, min_words=None)

Compares two corpora of Russian texts by every feature of a text at once: which statistics tell authors, genres, translations, human and generated texts apart - and by how much. For single words keyness does the same, for the distances between texts - delta.

The texts are cut in a row into windows of exactly window words by split_windows, so the windows of all texts have one length; an incomplete remainder at the end of a text and a text shorter than a window are dropped unless min_words allows shorter windows. The features of every window are computed by text_features or a function of one's own, and the tables of the two corpora are compared by compare_features of the anyTS core.

Chekhov versus Tolstoy over the prose of the RussianLiterature dataset: 77 and 42 works, 249 and 1423 windows of 1000 words, about a minute.

CodeResult 
from ruts.corpus import compare_corpora
from ruts.datasets import RussianLiterature

rl = RussianLiterature()
chekhov = list(rl.get_texts(genre="prose", author="Чехов"))
tolstoy = list(rl.get_texts(genre="prose", author="Толстой"))

result = compare_corpora(chekhov, tolstoy, window=1000, labels=("Чехов", "Толстой"))
columns = [
    "median_Чехов",
    "median_Толстой",
    "ci_low",
    "ci_high",
    "cohen_d",
    "cliff_delta",
    "auc",
    "p_holm",
]
result[columns].head(10).round(3)
result.loc["sents_mean", ["n_Чехов", "n_Толстой", "n_texts_Чехов", "n_texts_Толстой"]].to_dict()

                                        median_Чехов  median_Толстой  ci_low  ci_high  cohen_d  cliff_delta    auc  p_holm

cohesion_noun_overlap_2_sent                   0.080           0.141  -0.068   -0.049   -1.044       -0.750  0.125     0.0
cohesion_content_overlap_prop_all              0.015           0.027  -0.014   -0.009   -0.522       -0.742  0.129     0.0
punct_ellipsis                                14.000           2.000   5.975   23.025    1.869        0.707  0.853     0.0
cohesion_content_overlap_adjacent              0.198           0.352  -0.196   -0.127   -1.228       -0.697  0.151     0.0
cohesion_content_overlap_all                   0.094           0.188  -0.127   -0.071   -1.051       -0.678  0.161     0.0
punct_exclamation                             14.000           4.000   7.000   14.000    1.670        0.658  0.829     0.0
cohesion_noun_overlap_adjacent                 0.110           0.220  -0.142   -0.084   -1.025       -0.651  0.174     0.0
cohesion_noun_overlap_all                      0.045           0.097  -0.072   -0.035   -0.820       -0.642  0.179     0.0
cohesion_content_overlap_prop_adjacent         0.038           0.060  -0.026   -0.018   -0.820       -0.642  0.179     0.0
{'n_Чехов': 249, 'n_Толстой': 1423, 'n_texts_Чехов': 57, 'n_texts_Толстой': 41}

Cohesion sets the corpora apart most: Tolstoy repeats nouns and content words in adjacent and following sentences more often, and Chekhov has several times more ellipses and exclamations per 1000 words. The overlaps in adjacent and in all pairs of sentences partly repeat the sentence length: a long sentence has more words that may recur (the Spearman ρ of cohesion_content_overlap_all with sents_mean over the windows of Chekhov is 0.91, of Tolstoy 0.76), while the share of the lemmas repeated in the next two sentences (cohesion_content_overlap_2_sent) is hardly related to it (0.30 and 0.33). Further down the list Chekhov has shorter sentences, a higher share of finite verb forms and a lower one of participles and converbs, and Tolstoy is harder by every readability formula. Twenty works of Chekhov and one of Tolstoy are shorter than 1000 words and give no window, so the windows come from 57 and 41 works; with a smaller window they would be compared too.

The p-values take the 1672 windows for independent (see the warning below): 111 of the 146 features have a corrected p-value below 0.01, but only 21 show a large effect by Cliff's delta. The interval of the difference of the medians resamples whole works and is the safer guide: it excludes zero for 82 of those 111 features, and for the length of a sentence it spans −5.4 to −1.2 words, where the windows alone would give −4.0 to −2.7. For the ellipses it spans 6 to 23 per 1000 words: the works of Chekhov differ in them a lot, on average from a fraction of one to 84 per 1000 words.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description a list[str] - Texts of the first corpus b list[str] - Texts of the second corpus window int 1000 Window size in words; None - whole texts features Callable None Text feature function; None - text_features min_words int None Smallest number of words in a window, at most window; None - a whole window, one word with window=None

labels, n_bootstrap and seed go on to compare_features. compare_corpora checks them with check_comparison_params first, so a wrong name of a corpus or seed fails before any text is processed.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - texts that are not a list of strings, features that cannot be called;
  • SourceError - a corpus without a window of min_words words or more;
  • ParameterError - a window or min_words that is not an integer of at least one, min_words above window, labels, a number of samples or a seed that check_comparison_params rejects.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
text_features(text, nlp=None)

Returns 146 features of a text prefixed by source, 189 with the pipeline nlp; an undefined feature is nan.

Prefix Features Source basic_ shares of long, complex, simple, mono- and polysyllabic words, letters, spaces and punctuation marks; letters and syllables per word BasicStats readability_ all readability formulas and the consensus grade ReadabilityStats diversity_ lexical diversity measures DiversityStats morph_ shares of parts of speech and of single-valued features among the words (morph_pos_NOUN, morph_polarity_Neg, morph_style_variant_Short) and shares of values within the other features (morph_case_Gen, morph_tense_Past, morph_degree_Cmp; one share for a two-valued feature, morph_number_Plur) MorphStats by pymorphy3 sents_ mean sentence length in words, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, autocorrelation of adjacent lengths (sentence_rhythm) - the rhythm of the text sentence_lengths punct_ frequencies of punctuation marks by type per 1000 words and the share of the letter ё punctuation_profile cohesion_ the overlap of the sentences, pronouns, givenness, temporal cohesion and connectors; without the overlaps between paragraphs (*_para): a window cuts the paragraphs of a text CohesionStats by pymorphy3 syntax_ all syntactic statistics of the parse, only with the pipeline nlp; the parse takes the sentences of the other groups SyntaxStats

A 1000-word window takes about 0.04 s. Syntactic features need a parse, so they are not in the default set: a spaCy pipeline with a parser and parts of speech in nlp adds them, and compare_corpora and corpus_features take it through functools.partial, see the example below.

The shares of spaces, letters and punctuation marks (basic_p_spaces, basic_p_letters, basic_p_punctuations) count characters as they are: line indents, double and non-breaking spaces in the files reflect the typesetting of the edition, not the text. In a corpus from different sources collapse them beforehand, for example re.sub(r"[^\S\n]+", " ", text).

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string nlp Language None spaCy pipeline with a parser and parts of speech for the syntax_ features; None - without them

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a text that is not a string, an nlp that is not a spaCy Language object;
  • SourceError - a text without words, a text longer than the max_length of the pipeline, a pipeline without a parser or parts of speech.
corpus_features(texts, window=1000, features=text_features, min_words=None)

Returns the feature matrix of the windows indexed by (text number, window number), for your own classifiers as well; the level text of the index is what the bootstrap of compare_features resamples. Texts without words and windows shorter than min_words are skipped. compare_corpora is corpus_features for each corpus followed by compare_features; the split is needed when the features are computed once for several corpora and pairs have to be compared, for example all authors pairwise.

Parameter Type Default Description texts list[str] - Texts of the corpus window int 1000 Window size in words; None - whole texts features Callable text_features Text feature function min_words int None Smallest number of words in a window, at most window; None - a whole window, one word with window=None

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - texts that are not a list of strings, features that cannot be called;
  • SourceError - a corpus without a window of min_words words or more;
  • ParameterError - a window or min_words that is not an integer of at least one, min_words above window.

Features of your own go to features as a function of a text, text_features with a pipeline among them; with the parse the same comparison takes about five minutes:

CodeResult 
from functools import partial

import spacy
from ruts.corpus import compare_corpora, text_features

nlp = spacy.load("ru_core_news_sm")
result = compare_corpora(
    chekhov,
    tolstoy,
    window=1000,
    features=partial(text_features, nlp=nlp),
    labels=("Чехов", "Толстой"),
)
result.filter(like="syntax_", axis=0)[columns].head(5).round(3)
