docs.title: Comparison of feature tables
docs.text:
compare_features(table_a, table_b, labels=('A', 'B'), n_bootstrap=1000, seed=0)

Compares two corpora feature by feature. Each corpus is a table of the features of its windows, parts of the texts of about equal size, so the features do not depend on text length. The result has one row per column, by descending absolute Cliff's delta, the features without statistics last. The bootstrap resamples whole texts by the index level text; without it every row is a text of its own. Every feature has a generator of its own, from the seed and the name of the feature, so its interval does not change with the other columns. A column missing from one table gives nan.

Parameter Type Default Description table_a DataFrame - Features of the windows of the first corpus, one row per window table_b DataFrame - Features of the windows of the second corpus labels tuple[str, str] ('A', 'B') Names of the corpora for the columns, two strings that give distinct columns n_bootstrap int 1000 Number of bootstrap samples seed int / Generator 0 Seed of the random number generator, a non-negative integer, or a numpy Generator; None - a random one

A table that is not a DataFrame, repeats the name of a column or has a column that is not numeric raises SourceTypeError; the other parameters are checked by check_comparison_params.

check_comparison_params(labels=('A', 'B'), n_bootstrap=1000, seed=0)

Checks the parameters of compare_features before the texts are processed: it raises ParameterError unless the labels are two strings that give distinct columns (("diff", "B") would repeat median_diff), the number of bootstrap samples is an integer of at least one and the seed is None, a non-negative integer or a numpy Generator.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
For a feature with the values \(x_1 \dots x_{n_A}\) in corpus A and \(y_1 \dots y_{n_B}\) in corpus B (undefined and infinite values dropped; with fewer than two values on a side - nan):

Column Description mean_A, mean_B, median_A, median_B means and medians median_diff, ci_low, ci_high the difference of the medians and its 95% percentile bootstrap interval: both sets are resampled n_bootstrap times (bootstrap_median_diff) cohen_d \(d = (\bar{x} - \bar{y}) / s\), \(s\) - the pooled standard deviation; 0.2 - a small effect, 0.5 - medium, 0.8 - large (calc_cohen_d) cliff_delta \(\delta = P(x > y) - P(x < y)\) from −1 to 1; \(\lvert\delta\rvert\) < 0.147 - a negligible effect, < 0.33 - small, < 0.474 - medium, large otherwise (Romano et al. 2006; calc_cliff_delta) auc the feature as a classifier: the share of the pairs of windows with the value in A greater than in B, ties counted as half; \(\delta = 2 \cdot AUC - 1\), 0.5 - the feature does not tell the corpora apart u, p_value the Mann-Whitney U statistic and the two-sided p-value (scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu) p_holm the p-value with Holm's correction for the number of features (holm_correction) n_A, n_B number of windows with a defined value n_texts_A, n_texts_B number of texts behind those windows

The columns are anyts.corpus.COMPARISON_COLUMNS with the suffixes a and b replaced by the labels of the corpora. Cliff's delta and the AUC come from the same U statistic and agree; Cohen's d is sensitive to outliers and non-normality, so it is best read next to the delta.

Windows of one text are not independent

The test and the effect sizes take the windows for independent observations, which the windows of one text are not: with few texts the p-values are too small and reflect the chosen texts as much as the corpora. The bootstrap resamples whole texts (a cluster bootstrap), so its interval covers the spread between texts; it needs at least two texts on each side and is rough with few.

docs.title: Functions of the statistics
docs.text:
The statistics of a row are available one by one from ruts.corpus:

calc_cohen_d(values_a, values_b)

Cohen's d with the pooled sample variances (ddof=1); nan with fewer than two values on a side or without spread.

Parameter Type Default Description values_a list[float] - Values in the first corpus values_b list[float] - Values in the second corpus

A value that is neither a number nor a missing one (None, NA) and values that are not a flat list raise SourceTypeError.

calc_cliff_delta(values_a, values_b)

Cliff's delta, the share of the pairs where the first value is greater minus the share where it is smaller; nan for an empty set or an undefined value. Computed by sorting, in \(O((n_A + n_B) \log n_B)\) time and linear memory.

Parameter Type Default Description values_a list[float] - Values in the first corpus values_b list[float] - Values in the second corpus

A value that is neither a number nor a missing one (None, NA) and values that are not a flat list raise SourceTypeError.

bootstrap_median_diff(values_a, values_b, n_bootstrap=1000, rng=None, confidence=0.95, texts_a=None, texts_b=None)

The percentile bootstrap interval of the difference of the medians. With texts_a and texts_b whole texts are resampled, the median of a draw taken over the values of its texts; with fewer than two texts on a side the interval is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description values_a list[float] - Values in the first corpus values_b list[float] - Values in the second corpus n_bootstrap int 1000 Number of bootstrap samples rng Generator None Random number generator of numpy; None - a new one without a seed confidence float 0.95 Confidence level texts_a list None Texts of the values in the first corpus; None - every value is resampled on its own texts_b list None Texts of the values in the second corpus

A value that is neither a number nor a missing one, values that are not a flat list and texts that are not labels of one type raise SourceTypeError; an n_bootstrap that is not an integer of at least one, a confidence that is not a number in (0, 1), texts not as many as the values and an rng that is not a numpy Generator raise ParameterError.

holm_correction(p_values)

Holm's correction for multiple comparisons: the p-values are sorted in ascending order, the i-th is multiplied by (m − i + 1), where m is the number of defined values, then the running maximum is taken and capped at one; nan stays nan.

Parameter Type Default Description p_values list[float] - p-values

A p-value that is neither a number nor a missing one and p-values that are not a flat list raise SourceTypeError, and a p-value outside [0, 1] ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from ruts.corpus import calc_cliff_delta, calc_cohen_d, holm_correction

round(calc_cohen_d([2, 4, 6, 8], [1, 3, 5, 7]), 3)
calc_cliff_delta([2, 4, 6, 8], [1, 3, 5, 7])
holm_correction([0.01, 0.04, 0.03]).round(3).tolist()

0.387
0.25
[0.03, 0.06, 0.06]

docs.title: Windows of a text
docs.text:
split_windows(text, window=1000, min_words=None)

Cuts a text into consecutive windows of exactly window words, so the features that depend on length are comparable between texts. The rest is a window only with at least min_words words (by default a whole window, so it is dropped). A boundary goes before the first word of a window and its opening marks; a symmetric mark, such as a straight quote or the dash of an aside, closes the previous window when glued to its last word or after a closing mark. Windows are stripped of whitespace; window=None gives the whole text. The words are those of WordsExtractor, and the marks those of ruts.constants: quotes, brackets and dashes open a phrase (OPENING_MARKS), the straight and the English quotes and the dashes are symmetric (SYMMETRIC_MARKS), and the final marks, the comma, the semicolon, the closing brackets and guillemet close one (CLOSING_MARKS).

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string window int 1000 Size of a window in words; None - the whole text min_words int None Smallest number of words in a window; None - a whole window, or one word without a window

A text without words or shorter than min_words gives an empty list.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a text that is not a string;
  • ParameterError - a window or min_words that is not an integer of at least one, min_words above the window.
CodeResult 
from ruts.corpus import split_windows

split_windows("Раз два три четыре пять", 2, min_words=1)
split_windows("Он сказал: «Иди домой». Потом он вышел из комнаты", 4)

['Раз два', 'три четыре', 'пять']
['Он сказал: «Иди домой».', 'Потом он вышел из']

docs.title: Rhythm of the sentences
docs.text:
sentence_rhythm(lengths)

Gives the rhythm of the sentences from their lengths in words: the mean sents_mean, the standard deviation sents_std, the coefficient of variation sents_cv and the lag-1 autocorrelation of neighbouring lengths sents_autocorr (Yule, 1939). The deviation needs two sentences, the autocorrelation three of unequal lengths, the coefficient of variation a mean above zero; otherwise, and without sentences, a feature is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description lengths list[int] - Lengths of the sentences in words

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - lengths that are not a list of integers;
  • ParameterError - a negative length.
CodeResult 
from ruts.corpus import sentence_rhythm

{key: round(value, 3) for key, value in sentence_rhythm([4, 8, 2, 7]).items()}

{'sents_mean': 5.25, 'sents_std': 2.754, 'sents_cv': 0.525, 'sents_autocorr': -0.794}

docs.title: Word dispersion
docs.text:
dispersion(words, parts=10, word=None, min_freq=1)

The dispersion of a word is how evenly it is spread over the parts of a text or of a corpus. Frequency does not tell a word occurring once in every chapter from one gathered in a single chapter; the measures of dispersion (Gries 2008, 2020) complement it.

parts is the number of parts of about equal size or the sizes of the parts in order (sentences, paragraphs, chapters, documents of a corpus), adding up to the number of words; split_paragraphs of anyts.extractors gives the paragraphs of a text, whose words make the sizes; the paragraphs without words, such as a scene break of asterisks, are dropped first, since a part needs a word. Six measures are computed from the frequencies of every word by part; Gries recommends DP as the main one.

Words are compared as they are: case and lemmatization belong to the word extractor.

The function wraps dispersion of the anyTS core and strips stress marks from the words and from word. Words are extracted with WordsExtractor.

CodeResult 
from ruts import SentsExtractor, WordsExtractor
from ruts.corpus import dispersion

text = (
    "Кот сидел на окне и смотрел на птиц. Птицы улетели, и кот уснул на окне. "
    "Завтра кот снова будет сидеть на окне и смотреть на птиц."
)
we = WordsExtractor(use_lexemes=True, lowercase=True)
words = we.extract(text)
sizes = [len(we.extract(sent)) for sent in SentsExtractor().extract(text)]
sizes
dispersion(words, parts=sizes, word="кот")

# Three equal parts: «птица» only in the first and the last
[(d.word, round(d.dp, 2)) for d in dispersion(words, parts=3, min_freq=3)]

[8, 7, 11]
[Dispersion(word='кот', freq=3, dp=0.08974358974358976, dp_norm=0.12280701754385966, juilland_d=0.8725780285943101, carroll_d2=0.984770130157433, rosengren_s=0.9907464277073554, kl_divergence=0.0265483705216355)]
[('на', 0.15), ('кот', 0.32), ('окно', 0.03), ('и', 0.03), ('птица', 0.35)]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order parts int / list[int] 10 Number of parts (from 2 to the number of words) or sizes of the parts word str None Word whose dispersion is needed; None - every word min_freq int 1 Minimum frequency of a word

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, and no words SourceError. A parts that is neither an integer from 2 to the number of words nor two or more positive integers adding up to it, a word that is not a string and a min_freq that is not an integer raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Dispersion(word, freq, dp, dp_norm, juilland_d, carroll_d2, rosengren_s, kl_divergence)

A list of Dispersion named tuples by descending frequency: the word, its frequency and the measures; pd.DataFrame(result) gives a table.

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
The measures, the fields of Dispersion, with their names in anyts.constants.DISPERSION_STATS_DESC:

Field Measures Range Higher means dp Deviation of the shares of the occurrences from the shares of the parts 0 to \(1 - \min s_i\) More uneven dp_norm DP over its greatest possible value 0-1 More uneven juilland_d Variation of the relative frequencies by part 0-1 More even carroll_d2 Entropy of the relative frequencies by part 0-1 More even rosengren_s Spread of the occurrences against the sizes of the parts \(\min s_i\) to 1 More even kl_divergence Divergence of the shares of the occurrences from the shares of the parts, in bits 0 to \(-\log_2 \min s_i\) More uneven

Every measure is a function of the module anyts.corpus.dispersion of the frequencies of the word by part and the sizes of the parts. For \(n\) parts of sizes \(n_i\) and shares \(s_i\) of the text, frequencies of the word by part \(v_i\) and a total frequency \(f = \sum v_i\), \(p_i = v_i / n_i\) is the relative frequency in a part:

Parameter Type Default Description frequencies list[int] - Frequencies of the word by part sizes list[int] - Sizes of the parts

For a word of zero frequency every measure is nan.

The module ruts.corpus.dispersion re-exports the functions of the measures (from ruts.corpus.dispersion import calc_dp).

docs.title: Deviation of proportions DP
docs.text:
dp · Gries (2008)

calc_dp(frequencies, sizes)

How far the shares of the occurrences of the word by part are from the shares of the parts: 0 means the word is spread in proportion to the sizes of the parts, \(1 - s_i\) that it is all in part \(i\).

\[ DP = \frac{1}{2} \sum \left\lvert \frac{v_i}{f} - s_i \right\rvert \]

docs.title: Normalized DP
docs.text:
dp_norm · Lijffijt and Gries (2012)

calc_dp_norm(frequencies, sizes)

DP divided by its greatest possible value, so the maximum is one whatever the split.

\[ \frac{DP}{1 - \min s_i} \]

docs.title: Juilland's D
docs.text:
juilland_d · Juilland and Chang-Rodríguez (1964)

calc_juilland_d(frequencies, sizes)

One less the coefficient of variation \(V\) of the relative frequencies \(p_i\) over its greatest value \(\sqrt{n - 1}\): 1 means even, 0 all in one part. The standard deviation \(\sigma\) is that of the population, as in Gries (2020); Gries (2008) takes the sample one.

\[ 1 - \frac{V}{\sqrt{n - 1}}, \quad V = \frac{\sigma(p)}{\mu(p)} \]

docs.title: Carroll's D2
docs.text:
carroll_d2 · Carroll (1970)

calc_carroll_d2(frequencies, sizes)

The entropy of the distribution of the relative frequencies \(p_i\) over the parts, divided by its greatest value: 1 means even, 0 all in one part.

\[ \frac{H(p)}{\log_2 n} \]

docs.title: Rosengren's S
docs.text:
rosengren_s · Rosengren (1971)

calc_rosengren_s(frequencies, sizes)

1 means the word is spread in proportion to the sizes of the parts; all in part \(i\), it gives \(s_i\), so \(1/n\) in one of \(n\) equal parts.

\[ \frac{(\sum \sqrt{s_i v_i})^2}{f} \]

docs.title: Kullback-Leibler divergence
docs.text:
kl_divergence · Gries (2020)

calc_kl_divergence(frequencies, sizes)

The divergence of the shares of the occurrences of the word by part from the shares of the parts: 0 means in proportion; it grows when the word is gathered in small parts.

\[ \sum \frac{v_i}{f} \log_2 \frac{v_i / f}{s_i} \]

docs.title: Keywords
docs.text:
keyness(target, reference, measure='log_likelihood', min_freq=1, positive=True, top_n=None, n=1, lemmatize=True)

Keyword extraction (keyness) for a target corpus against a reference one: the words that occur significantly more often in the target corpus than in the reference.

Every word gets two values that Gabrielatos and Marchi and Hardie recommend reading together: the log-likelihood \(G^2\) with its p-value (whether there is a difference) and Log Ratio (how large it is), plus the chosen measure score, which sorts the list. The measures of significance (\(G^2\), chi-square, BIC) and ELL, the effect size of \(G^2\), are negative when the word is more frequent in the reference; %DIFF, Log Ratio and the odds ratio are directional by construction.

The reference may be a list of words, a mapping of frequencies (its size is the sum of the counts) or a FrequencyReference. Words are compared as they are: case, lemmatization and stop words belong to the word extractor, and both corpora have to be extracted the same way. A corpus of several texts is given as a list of their lists of words. With n above 1 the keywords are the n-grams of the words of every text, joined by underscores as the n-grams of WordsExtractor (black_cat), so an n-gram never runs across two texts; the counts and the sizes are those of the n-grams, and the frequencies per million are per million n-grams. Frequencies of n-grams - a sum of the Counter of the n-grams of every text, or a frequency dictionary of n-grams - go with n=1: a mapping and a FrequencyReference are refused with n above 1.

The function wraps keyness of the anyTS core and also takes the Lyashevskaya and Sharoff frequency dictionary FreqDict as the reference; FrequencyReference is in ruts.corpus next to it. Words are extracted with WordsExtractor.

CodeResult 
from ruts import WordsExtractor
from ruts.corpus import keyness

we = WordsExtractor(use_lexemes=True, lowercase=True)
target = we.extract(
    "Кот сидел на окне и смотрел на птиц. Птицы улетели, и кот уснул на окне. "
    "Завтра кот снова будет сидеть на окне и смотреть на птиц."
)
reference = we.extract(
    "Собака лежала на полу и дремала. Потом собака ела и снова дремала. Завтра собака будет гулять."
)

keyness(target, reference, top_n=1)
[(k.word, round(k.g2, 2)) for k in keyness(target, reference, positive=False, top_n=2)]

[Keyword(word='кот', freq_target=3, freq_reference=0.0, ipm_target=115384.61538461539, ipm_reference=0.0, g2=2.8774384815713177, p_value=0.08982881315854577, log_ratio=1.8845227825800641, score=2.8774384815713177)]
[('собака', -5.79), ('дремать', -3.86)]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description target list[str] / list[list[str]] / dict[str, int] - Words of the target corpus - one text or a list of texts - or their frequencies reference list[str] / list[list[str]] / dict[str, float] / FrequencyReference - Words of the reference corpus - one text or a list of texts - their frequencies or a reference by frequencies measure str 'log_likelihood' Measure of anyts.constants.KEYNESS_MEASURES for score and the sorting min_freq int 1 Minimum frequency of a keyword in its own corpus positive bool True Positive keywords (more frequent in the target corpus) or negative ones (more frequent in the reference) top_n int None Number of keywords; None - all of them n int 1 Length of the n-grams of the words of every text; 1 - the words

The parameters and the target corpus are checked by check_keyness_params; an n above 1 with frequencies or a FrequencyReference raises ParameterError. A reference that is not a list of strings, a list of such lists, a counter or a FrequencyReference raises SourceTypeError, and a negative, nan or infinite frequency of a counter and a corpus without words, or shorter than n words, raise SourceError.

reference may also be FreqDict, and one more parameter tells what the target corpus is against it:

Parameter Type Default Description lemmatize bool True The target corpus is word forms, False - lemmas (FreqDict only)

A frequency dictionary that is not downloaded raises DatasetNotFoundError, and an n above 1 with it ParameterError: the dictionary holds words.

check_keyness_params(measure='log_likelihood', min_freq=1, top_n=None, target=None, n=1, positive=True)

Checks the parameters of keyness before a frequency dictionary is read: it raises ParameterError unless the measure is one of KEYNESS_MEASURES, the minimum frequency is an integer, the number of keywords is None or an integer of at least one, the length of the n-grams n is an integer of at least one and positive is a bool. With target it also raises SourceTypeError unless the target corpus is a list of strings, a list of such lists or a mapping of strings to whole frequencies, and SourceError for a negative, nan or infinite frequency.

docs.title: Reference by frequencies
docs.text:
FrequencyReference(counts, size, missing=0.0, key=None, keep=None)

A reference corpus described by its frequencies alone, such as a frequency dictionary built from a corpus too large to pass as words:

Field Type Default Description counts dict[str, float] - Frequencies of the keys in the reference corpus size float - Size of the reference corpus in words missing float 0.0 Frequency of a key missing from counts key Callable None Key of a word of the target corpus in counts, such as its lemma; None - the word itself keep Callable None Whether a word of the target corpus is counted; None - every word

Only the words of the target that keep passes are counted, under their key, in the frequencies and in the size alike. A key missing from counts has the frequency missing, such as the least frequency of a dictionary: an upper bound, so its word may be a positive keyword but never a negative one. Negative keywords come only from the keys of counts that keep passes. A frequency is checked as it is read, so a large dictionary is not gone through for positive keywords: one that is not a number raises SourceTypeError, and a negative, nan or infinite one SourceError. A size or a missing that is not a finite number or is negative raises ParameterError, and a key or a keep that cannot be called SourceTypeError.

The frequency dictionary FreqDict passed as reference is turned into such a reference:

Field FreqDict counts the frequencies of FreqDict.word_ipm converted to occurrences in the corpus of the dictionary size CORPUS_SIZE of ruts.datasets.freq2011, 92 million tokens of the modern subcorpus of the Russian National Corpus missing the least frequency of the dictionary FreqDict.min_ipm, 0.4 ipm (about 37 occurrences) key the lemma of the dictionary: a word form is lemmatized by pymorphy3 (with lemmatize=False it is taken as a lemma) and brought to the conventions of the dictionary by ruts.lexical_stats.dictionary_lemma, as in LexicalStats keep the words of the Cyrillic letters of ruts.lexical_stats.DICTIONARY_WORD; numbers and words with Latin letters are left out

A dictionary entry absent from the text can be a negative keyword only if some word form is reduced to it: the dictionary keeps separate entries «его», «ее», «их» (possessive pronouns) and «во», «со», while pymorphy3 reduces these word forms to «он», «она», «они», «в», «с», and without this rule they would be negative keywords of any text. Such entries - about 1,100 for word forms and 1,500 for lemmas - are listed in the resources of the package; words that pymorphy3 only predicts («Михайлыч», «дитё») are not seen by the rule.

With lemmatize=False the conventions of the dictionary cannot be recovered from a lemma: the short form, the plural and the spelling variant are lost («должный» instead of «должен», «деньга» instead of «деньги», «счастие» instead of «счастье»), and such entries come out as false keywords. Compare word forms with the dictionary.

CodeResult 
from ruts import WordsExtractor
from ruts.corpus import keyness
from ruts.datasets import FreqDict

# The dictionary is downloaded once with FreqDict().download()
words = WordsExtractor().extract(
    "Кот сидел на окне и смотрел на птиц. Птицы улетели, и кот уснул на окне. "
    "Завтра кот снова будет сидеть на окне и смотреть на птиц."
)
[(k.word, round(k.log_ratio, 1)) for k in keyness(words, FreqDict(), min_freq=3, top_n=2)]

[('кот', 11.5), ('птица', 10.3)]

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Keyword(word, freq_target, freq_reference, ipm_target, ipm_reference, g2, p_value, log_ratio, score)

A list of Keyword named tuples by descending keyness (ties broken by descending frequency and alphabetically, words of an undefined measure last); pd.DataFrame(keywords) gives a table.

Field Type Description word str Word freq_target int Frequency in the target corpus freq_reference float Frequency in the reference corpus ipm_target float Frequency in the target corpus per million words, or n-grams ipm_reference float Frequency in the reference corpus per million words, or n-grams g2 float Signed \(G^2\) p_value float p-value of \(G^2\) log_ratio float Log Ratio score float Value of the chosen measure

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
The measures of measure by key, with their names and descriptions in anyts.constants.KEYNESS_MEASURES:

Key Measures Range Higher means log_likelihood Significance of the difference of the frequencies Any number A more significant excess in the target corpus chi2 Significance of the difference, with Yates's correction Any number A more significant excess in the target corpus diff Difference of the frequencies per million, in percent of the reference Above −100 A larger excess in the target corpus log_ratio Binary logarithm of the ratio of the frequencies per million Any number A larger excess in the target corpus bic Evidence of the difference: \(G^2\) penalized by the size of the corpora Any number Stronger evidence of an excess in the target corpus, for a word more frequent there ell Effect size of \(G^2\) −1 to 1 as a rule, nan for small expected frequencies A larger excess in the target corpus odds_ratio Ratio of the odds of the word in the corpora 0 to inf, nan if the word fills both corpora Higher odds in the target corpus

Every measure is a function of the module anyts.corpus.keyness of the frequencies of a word and the sizes of the corpora, \(N = c + d\):

Parameter Type Default Description a float - Frequency of the word in the target corpus b float - Frequency of the word in the reference corpus c float - Size of the target corpus d float - Size of the reference corpus

A zero frequency in one of the corpora is replaced with 0.5 for %DIFF, Log Ratio and the odds ratio (Hardie 2014).

The module ruts.corpus.keyness re-exports the functions of the measures (from ruts.corpus.keyness import calc_log_likelihood).

docs.title: Log-likelihood
docs.text:
log_likelihood · g2 · p_value · Rayson and Garside (2000)

calc_log_likelihood(a, b, c, d)

The log-likelihood of the frequencies of the word against the expected ones \(E_1\) and \(E_2\); a term of zero frequency is zero. The critical values are anyts.constants.G2_CRITICAL_VALUES: 3.84 for p < 0.05, 6.63 for p < 0.01, 10.83 for p < 0.001, 15.13 for p < 0.0001. The sign is negative when the word is more frequent in the reference.

\[ G^2 = 2 \left(a \ln \frac{a}{E_1} + b \ln \frac{b}{E_2}\right), \quad E_1 = \frac{c\,(a+b)}{N}, \quad E_2 = \frac{d\,(a+b)}{N} \] 
calc_p_value(g2)

The p-value of a \(G^2\) or a chi-square, whatever its sign, by the chi-square distribution with one degree of freedom; an array of values gives an array.

docs.title: Chi-square
docs.text:
chi2

calc_chi2(a, b, c, d)

The chi-square with Yates's correction over the 2×2 contingency table of the word and the other words of each corpus. When the correction exceeds the difference, the statistic is zero. The sign is negative when the word is more frequent in the reference.

\[ \chi^2 = \frac{N\,\max(\lvert a(d-b) - b(c-a) \rvert - N/2,\ 0)^2}{(a+b)(N-a-b)\,c\,d} \]

docs.title: %DIFF
docs.text:
diff · Gabrielatos and Marchi (2011)

calc_diff(a, b, c, d)

The difference of the frequencies \(NF\) per million words, in percent of the frequency in the reference.

\[ \frac{NF_a - NF_b}{NF_b} \cdot 100 \]

docs.title: Log Ratio
docs.text:
log_ratio · Hardie (2014)

calc_log_ratio(a, b, c, d)

The binary logarithm of the ratio of the frequencies \(NF\) per million words: one means the word is twice as frequent in the target corpus.

\[ \log_2 \frac{NF_a}{NF_b} \]

docs.title: BIC
docs.text:
bic · Wilson (2013)

calc_bic(a, b, c, d)

The Bayesian information criterion of \(G^2\). In absolute value above 2 it is positive evidence of a difference, above 6 strong, above 10 very strong; a value of the sign opposite to \(G^2\), when \(\lvert G^2 \rvert < \ln N\), means no evidence, not the opposite direction.

\[ \operatorname{sign}(G^2) \cdot (\lvert G^2 \rvert - \ln N) \]

docs.title: ELL
docs.text:
ell · Johnston, Berry and Mielke (2006)

calc_ell(a, b, c, d)

The effect size of \(G^2\): the share of the greatest possible departure from the expected frequencies \(E_1\) and \(E_2\). It grows without bound as the least expected frequency nears one and is nan when that frequency is at most one (a logarithm of zero or below). The sign is negative when the word is more frequent in the reference.

\[ \frac{G^2}{N \ln \min(E_1, E_2)} \]

docs.title: Odds ratio
docs.text:
odds_ratio

calc_odds_ratio(a, b, c, d)

The ratio of the odds of the word in the two corpora: one means equal odds. A word that fills the whole target corpus gives inf, the whole reference 0, both nan.

\[ \frac{a / (c - a)}{b / (d - b)} \]

docs.title: KWIC concordance
docs.text:
kwic(source, keyword, window=5, by_lemma=False, ignore_case=True)

A KWIC concordance (keyword in context) - every occurrence of a word or a phrase with its context on both sides. Occurrences are found among the words of the text by the word form, ignoring case or respecting it (ignore_case=False), or by the lemma (by_lemma=True); the keyword is lemmatized as a string, so with a lemmatizer a phrase may be written in any form and without one it is given by lemmas. The words of a string and of the keyword come from the tokenizer, those of a Doc from its tokens: a tokenizer that splits a string as the pipeline does finds the same in both. Punctuation and symbols are not words; forms are compared in the composed form of Unicode (NFC), without soft hyphens.

A phrase does not cross the end of a paragraph or a sentence unless the keyword has a final mark or a sentence start in the same place (U.S. Army). A sentence ends at a boundary of a Doc anywhere between the words, an opening mark included, or, without boundaries or with partial ones (has_sents), at a sentence start of the sentence splitter, by default a final mark before whitespace. The context is window words on each side as written, punctuation included; whitespace collapses into one space, and occurrences do not overlap.

The function calls the kwic of the anyTS core with the hooks of Russian: the words and the sentences of a string and of the keyword are those of razdel, the lemma of a word is the pymorphy3 one, in a Doc with part-of-speech annotation taken with the part of speech of the token (ruts.utils.lemmatize), so «стали» is found by «сталь» or by «стать» depending on the annotation. Stress marks are stripped for the comparison, and the word forms (with ignore_case) and the lemmas are compared in lower case with ё as е. The parts of a hyphenated word that spaCy splits are joined (кто-то is one word).

CodeResult 
from ruts.corpus import kwic, print_kwic

text = (
    "Кот сидел на окне и смотрел на птиц. Птицы улетели, и кот уснул на окне. "
    "Завтра кот снова будет сидеть на окне и смотреть на птиц."
)
lines = kwic(text, "окно", by_lemma=True, window=3)
lines[0]
print_kwic(lines, width=20)

[line.keyword for line in kwic(text, "смотреть на птица", by_lemma=True)]

Concordance(start=13, end=17, left='Кот сидел на', keyword='окне', right='и смотрел на')
        Кот сидел на  окне  и смотрел на
        кот уснул на  окне  . Завтра кот снова
     будет сидеть на  окне  и смотреть на
['смотрел на птиц', 'смотреть на птиц']

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc - Text or Doc object keyword str - Word or phrase window int 5 Number of words of context on each side by_lemma bool False Compare lemmas instead of word forms ignore_case bool True Ignore case when comparing word forms

A keyword without words, a window that is not an integer or is negative and a by_lemma or ignore_case that is not a bool raise ParameterError; a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, a keyword that is not a string and a hook that is not callable raise SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Concordance(start, end, left, keyword, right)

A list of Concordance named tuples in the order of the text.

Field Type Description start int Position of the first character of the occurrence in the text end int Position after the last character of the occurrence left str Context on the left keyword str Occurrence as written in the text right str Context on the right

docs.title: Aligned lines
docs.text:
format_kwic(concordances, width=40)

Aligns the lines on the keyword in a text, one line per occurrence: the left context is cut on the left and aligned to the right, the right one cut on the right. The lines may come from any iterable and are taken in the composed form of Unicode (NFC), so the widths count characters as shown.

Parameter Type Default Description concordances list[Concordance] - Lines of a concordance width int 40 Width of a context in characters

Lines that are a string or cannot be iterated raise SourceTypeError, and a width that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

print_kwic(concordances, width=40)

Prints the result of format_kwic.

docs.title: Stylometry
docs.text:
Measures of stylometry and authorship attribution: distances between texts by the frequencies of the most frequent words (Burrows's Delta and its variants, as in stylo) and along a text by its windows (rolling Delta), markers of preferred and avoided words (Zeta) and their shares in the segments of corpora, Kilgarriff's chi-square distance between corpora and the Mendenhall curve. The functions work on lists of units of a text: lower-case word forms (the usual choice for Delta), lemmas or character N-grams - case and lemmatization belong to the extractors.

The functions are those of the anyTS core, with the profile of the function words of Russian added as a feature of an author. The units of a text come from WordsExtractor - word forms and lemmas - and CharNgramsExtractor.

docs.title: Burrows's Delta
docs.text:
frequency_table(corpus, n_mfw=100, culling=0.0)

Builds the table of relative frequencies of a corpus, a dictionary "name of a text → units": rows are the texts, columns the n_mfw most frequent units by descending mean relative frequency (alphabetically when equal); culling keeps the units that occur in at least the given share of the texts, as in stylo.

Parameter Type Default Description corpus dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the texts by the names of the texts n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the texts a unit occurs in

A corpus that is not a mapping of lists of strings raises SourceTypeError; an empty corpus, a text without units and no unit left after culling raise SourceError, and an n_mfw that is not an integer of at least one and a culling that is not a number within [0, 1] ParameterError.

z_scores(table)

Standardizes the columns of a table of frequencies with the sample standard deviation, like scale() of R; a column with the same frequency in every text gives zeros.

Parameter Type Default Description table DataFrame - Table of relative frequencies 
delta(corpus, n_mfw=100, variant='burrows', culling=0.0)

Computes a symmetric matrix of distances from the z-scores (a DataFrame with the names of the texts); at least three texts are needed - with two, the z-scores degenerate to ±1/√2 and the distances do not depend on the frequencies.

The variants (anyts.constants.DELTA_VARIANTS), with the formulas of the sources of stylo; \(n\) is the number of units, \(z_A\) and \(z_B\) the vectors of z-scores of the texts:

Variant Key Formula Source Burrows's Delta burrows \(\frac{1}{n} \sum_i \lvert z_{A,i} - z_{B,i} \rvert\) Burrows (2002), dist.delta Quadratic Delta quadratic \(\frac{1}{n} \sqrt{\sum_i (z_{A,i} - z_{B,i})^2}\) Argamon (2008), dist.argamon Eder's Delta eder \(\sum_i \frac{n - i + 2}{n} \lvert z_{A,i} - z_{B,i} \rvert\), \(i\) - rank of the unit by frequency Eder, dist.eder Cosine Delta cosine \(1 - \frac{z_A \cdot z_B}{\lVert z_A \rVert \lVert z_B \rVert}\) Smith and Aldridge (2011), Evert et al. (2015), dist.wurzburg

Cosine Delta clusters the texts by author best in the experiments of Evert et al. The usual number of units is 100 to 500 most frequent words, 100-200 for character N-grams.

Parameter Type Default Description corpus dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the texts by the names of the texts n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them variant str 'burrows' Variant of Delta of anyts.constants.DELTA_VARIANTS culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the texts a unit occurs in

The corpus, n_mfw and culling raise the errors of frequency_table; fewer than three texts raise SourceError, and an unknown variant ParameterError.

delta_profiles(reference, samples, n_mfw=100, variant='burrows', culling=0.0, statistics=None)

Distances by Delta for authorship attribution. The most frequent units, the culling and the statistics of the z-scores come from the reference texts (the profiles of the authors) or from a separate set statistics, such as training windows when the profiles are too few to estimate the spread of the frequencies; the texts under test samples get the same units and scaling. The result is the distances from the samples (rows) to the references (columns); the nearest reference is the presumed author. Unlike in delta, a sample affects neither the units nor the scaling, so its result does not depend on the other samples.

Parameter Type Default Description reference dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the reference texts by the names of the texts samples dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the texts under test by the names of the texts n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them variant str 'burrows' Variant of Delta of anyts.constants.DELTA_VARIANTS culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the texts a unit occurs in statistics dict[str, list[str]] None Texts of the units and of the statistics of the scaling; None - the reference texts

The corpora, n_mfw and culling raise the errors of frequency_table; fewer than three texts for the statistics raise SourceError, and an unknown variant ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from ruts import WordsExtractor
from ruts.corpus import delta, delta_profiles, frequency_table

texts = {
    "А": "Кот сидел на окне и смотрел на птиц. Птицы улетели, и кот уснул на окне.",
    "Б": "Собака лежала на полу и дремала. Потом собака ела и снова дремала на полу.",
    "В": "Завтра кот снова будет сидеть на окне и смотреть на птиц, а собака будет дремать.",
}
we = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True)
corpus = {name: we.extract(text) for name, text in texts.items()}

frequency_table(corpus, n_mfw=5).round(3)
delta(corpus, n_mfw=5).round(3)
delta(corpus, n_mfw=5, variant="cosine").round(3)

sample = {"?": we.extract("Кот проснулся на окне и снова смотрел на птиц.")}
delta_profiles(corpus, sample, n_mfw=5).round(3)

Б  0.143  0.143   0.143  0.000  0.000

docs.title: Rolling Delta
docs.text:
rolling_delta(reference, text, window=5000, step=1000, n_mfw=100, variant='burrows', culling=0.0, statistics=None)

Delta along a text, after rolling.delta of stylo: the reference texts and the text under test are cut into windows of window units every step units, the rest shorter than a window dropped. The most frequent units, the culling and the statistics of the z-scores come from the windows of the reference texts, or of a separate set statistics, and every window of the text is compared by the variant of Delta with the centroid of the windows of every reference text. The result is the distances from the windows (rows, by the position of their middle in units) to the references (columns); where the nearest reference changes along the text, so does the style - another author of a part of a text written together, a borrowed passage. Unlike stylo, which sums the differences of the raw frequencies, the distances are those of delta_profiles over z-scores.

Scaled by their own windows, the centroids of the references balance each other, and Cosine Delta loses its sense: the cosine distances of a window to the references average 1 (weighted by their windows and the lengths of their centroids), with two references they add up to 2 and the lines are mirrored, so a passage of a third author looks halfway between them. With few references, Cosine Delta needs statistics of more texts - other authors, other works; Burrows's and Eder's Delta are not bound so. With statistics a single reference is enough.

Parameter Type Default Description reference dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the reference texts by the names of the texts text list[str] - Units of the text under test window int 5000 Size of a window in units step int 1000 Distance between the starts of the windows in units n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them variant str 'burrows' Variant of Delta of anyts.constants.DELTA_VARIANTS culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the windows a unit occurs in statistics dict[str, list[str]] None Texts whose windows give the units and the statistics of the scaling; None - the reference texts

A corpus that is not a mapping of lists of strings and units of the text that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError. No reference texts, fewer than two without statistics, a text without units or shorter than a window, fewer than three windows of the statistics and no unit left after culling raise SourceError. An unknown variant, a window, a step or an n_mfw that is not an integer of at least one, a step greater than the window and a culling that is not a number within [0, 1] raise ParameterError.

rolling_delta(corpus, corpus["А"] + corpus["Б"], window=6, step=3, n_mfw=10).round(3)

docs.title: Zeta
docs.text:
zeta(target, comparison, segment_size=2000, top_n=None)

Markers of preferred and avoided words after Burrows (2007) and Craig and Kinney (2009). Every text of both corpora is split into segments of about segment_size words (the length over the size rounded half up, at least one segment); \(DP\) is the share of the segments of a corpus with the word. Zeta is \(DP_{target} - DP_{comparison}\), from −1 to 1 (zeta.craig in stylo; the classic Zeta of Craig, \(DP_{target} + (1 - DP_{comparison})\), is greater by one); the logarithmic Zeta is \(\log_2 \frac{DP_{target}}{DP_{comparison}}\) (Schöch et al. 2018), a zero share replaced by half a segment. The list goes from the words the target corpus prefers to those it avoids.

Parameter Type Default Description target list[str] / list[list[str]] - Words of the target corpus - one text or a list of texts comparison list[str] / list[list[str]] - Words of the comparison corpus segment_size int 2000 Size of a segment in words top_n int None Number of words from the start of the list; None - all of them

The result is a list of ZetaScore(word, dp_target, dp_comparison, zeta, log_zeta) named tuples by descending Zeta, by descending logarithmic Zeta and alphabetically when equal. A corpus that is neither a list of strings nor a list of such lists raises SourceTypeError, and a corpus without words SourceError; a segment_size or a top_n that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from ruts.corpus import zeta

zeta(corpus["А"], corpus["Б"], segment_size=5, top_n=2)
zeta(corpus["А"], corpus["Б"], segment_size=5)[-1]

[ZetaScore(word='кот', dp_target=0.6666666666666666, dp_comparison=0.0, zeta=0.6666666666666666, log_zeta=2.0), ZetaScore(word='окне', dp_target=0.6666666666666666, dp_comparison=0.0, zeta=0.6666666666666666, log_zeta=2.0)]
ZetaScore(word='собака', dp_target=0.0, dp_comparison=0.6666666666666666, zeta=-0.6666666666666666, log_zeta=-2.0)

zeta_segments(corpora, preferred, avoided, segment_size=2000)

The shares of the markers of Zeta in the segments of corpora, as oppose of stylo places the segments: every text is split into segments as in zeta, and a segment gets the shares of the words of the lists preferred and avoided found in it. With the markers of a target corpus against a comparison corpus, the segments of the target lie high on the left of the plane of the two shares and those of the comparison low on the right; the segments of a disputed text show which group it is near (zeta_scatter_plot).

Parameter Type Default Description corpora dict[str, list[str] / list[list[str]]] - Words of the corpora by name - one text or a list of texts each preferred Collection[str] - Words the target corpus prefers - the start of the list of zeta avoided Collection[str] - Words the target corpus avoids - the end of the list segment_size int 2000 Size of a segment in words

The result is a DataFrame of the segments in the order of the corpora and of their texts, with the columns corpus (the name of the corpus), preferred and avoided (the shares of the lists). Corpora that are not a mapping and a corpus or a list of markers that is not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError; no corpora, an empty list of markers and a corpus without words SourceError, and a segment_size that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

from ruts.corpus import zeta_segments

scores = zeta(corpus["А"], corpus["Б"], segment_size=5)
preferred = [score.word for score in scores if score.zeta > 0]
avoided = [score.word for score in scores if score.zeta < 0]
zeta_segments(corpus, preferred, avoided, segment_size=5).round(3)

docs.title: Kilgarriff's chi-square
docs.text:
kilgarriff_chi2(words_a, words_b, n_mfw=500)

The distance between two corpora after Kilgarriff (2001): for the n_mfw most frequent words of the joint corpus the expected frequencies in the corpora are proportional to their sizes, \(\chi^2 = \sum (O - E)^2 / E\) over the words and both corpora. The greater the value, the more the corpora differ; it grows with the size of the corpora, so only pairs of equal sizes are comparable.

Parameter Type Default Description words_a list[str] - Words of the first corpus words_b list[str] - Words of the second corpus n_mfw int 500 Number of the most frequent words of the joint corpus

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, a corpus without words SourceError, and an n_mfw that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from ruts.corpus import kilgarriff_chi2

round(kilgarriff_chi2(corpus["А"], corpus["Б"], n_mfw=5), 3)

6.018

docs.title: Function word profile
docs.text:
function_words_profile(source)

The shares of adpositions, coordinating and subordinating conjunctions, particles, pronouns, determiners and interjections (ruts.constants.FUNCTION_UD_POS: ADP, CCONJ, SCONJ, PART, PRON, DET, INTJ) among the words of the text - by the first pymorphy3 analysis for a list of words and by the annotation for a Doc with parts of speech; punctuation is not counted. Function words do not depend on the topic, so their profile is a classic authorship feature (the Marusenko school).

Parameter Type Default Description source list[str] / Doc - Words of the text or Doc object

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a list of strings nor a Doc;
  • SourceError - a source without words.

docs.title: Lyashevskaya and Sharoff frequency dictionary
docs.text:
FreqDict(data_dir=DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR)

The frequency dictionary of modern Russian by O. N. Lyashevskaya and S. A. Sharoff (Freq2011): 52,138 lemmas of the modern subcorpus of the Russian National Corpus (1950-2007, 92 million tokens) with the ipm frequency, the range R (the number of corpus segments out of 100 in which the lemma occurs), Juilland's D, the number of documents and the part of speech in MyStem tags (s, v, a, adv, s.PROP for proper names).

The dictionary is downloaded from dict.ruslang.ru (HTTP only, 493 KB). No license is stated; the authors ask to cite the original source:

Citation

Ляшевская О. Н., Шаров С. А. Частотный словарь современного русского языка (на материалах Национального корпуса русского языка). М.: Азбуковник, 2009.

For lookup, a lemma with several parts of speech (а - conjunction, particle, interjection) is merged: ipm is summed, R, D and the number of documents are taken as maxima; the lemma is lowercased and ё is replaced with е, as in the dictionary. The parsed dictionary is cached by file path and read once per process, so creating FreqDict() for every text is cheap. The dictionary is used by LexicalStats and as a reference corpus in keyness (the dictionary corpus size is CORPUS_SIZE, 92 million tokens).

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a data_dir that is neither a string nor a Path.

from ruts.datasets import FreqDict

fd = FreqDict()
fd.download()
fd.info["citation"]

'Ляшевская О. Н., Шаров С. А. Частотный словарь современного русского языка (на материалах Национального корпуса русского языка). М.: Азбуковник, 2009.'

docs.text:

The downloaded archive is verified against a SHA-256 checksum (the file on the site has not changed since 2013); a corrupted or replaced file is deleted with a DownloadError, so that a repeated download is not skipped. docs.title: Russian poetry corpus
docs.text:
PoetryCorpus(data_dir=DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR)

The Russian poetry corpus PoetryCorpus collected by Ilya Gusev for the rupo library: 16,694 poems by 195 authors of the 18th-20th centuries, 13 million characters. Every poem has an author and a title (or its first line), 12,857 have years of writing (from 1725 to 1996), 3,904 have themes, 20 themes in total:

Theme Poems Theme Poems О любви (love) 2,839 О природе (nature) 76 Военные (war) 724 Патриотические (patriotic) 72 О дружбе (friendship) 155 Посвящения (dedications) 38 Детские (children's) 106 Спортивные (sports) 36 О животных (animals) 78 the other 11 themes up to 21 each

The most poems are by Vysotsky (539), Pushkin (401), Blok (286), Akhmatova (277) and Fet (251). The corpus is distributed under the Apache-2.0 license and suits stylometry - comparing authors and periods, verse studies and model training.

The corpus file (27 MB) is downloaded from the repository at a pinned commit and verified against a SHA-256 checksum; it is read as a stream, so memory does not depend on the corpus size.

docs.title: Russian classical literature
docs.text:
RussianLiterature(data_dir=DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR)

The RusLit collection of Russian classical literature (on Kaggle - russian-literature): 373 works by 12 authors of the 19th - early 20th century, 39 million characters, three genres:

Genre Key Authors Works Prose prose Chekhov (77), Tolstoy (42), Dostoevsky (33), Gorky (33), Bryusov (30), Gogol (16), Herzen (11), Pushkin (10), Turgenev (10), Blok (4), Lermontov (3) 269 Poetry poems Pushkin (35), Lermontov (18), Nekrasov (15), Blok (10) 78 Publicism publicism Tolstoy 26

The texts are in the public domain (Kaggle states the PDDL license), collected from LitLib, Wikisource and Ilibrary. The year of writing is taken from the collection's info.csv files (1825 or 1824-1825); 27 works have none. The collection's folder names are in Latin script; records give authors by their Russian names from the AUTHORS table (Chekhov → «Антон Чехов»). The collection suits authorship attribution and genre comparison: texts of one author in different genres and of one genre by different authors.

The repository archive (20 MB) is downloaded at a pinned commit, verified against a SHA-256 checksum and extracted; texts are read one at a time, the single cp1251 file is decoded automatically.

In the source most files begin with the author's name and the title («Александр Пушкин» and «19 ОКТЯБРЯ», «Валерий Брюсов. Бемоль», «Л.Н.Толстой», «Горький Максим»), which is a feature leak for authorship attribution. О НАУКЕ» with the title «О науке (Ответ крестьянину)») and dedications («Посвящается графине М. Н. Толстой»). For strict attribution check the beginnings of the texts or drop the first lines.

docs.title: Koziev stress dictionary
docs.text:
StressDict(data_dir=DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR)

Ilya Koziev's stress dictionary (all_accents): 1,680,535 word forms with the position of the primary stress. Data from Wikipedia and Wiktionary is extended with forms generated from the inflection tables of the author's grammar dictionary under the assumption that stress does not move in declension and conjugation, so forms with mobile stress (реки́ - ре́ки, воды́ - во́ды) get one of the variants, homographs (за́мок - замо́к) share one line, and the letter ё is replaced with е throughout.

The dictionary is distributed under the CC0 license and downloaded from the author's repository at a pinned commit (10.6 MB, a 77 MB file) with a SHA-256 checksum check. The file is read once per process and indexed in memory as a whole without parsing lines: a word form is found by binary search over the sorted file, so loading takes a fraction of a second and the dictionary occupies about 100 MB of memory.

The dictionary is used by VerseStats and by the accentuation functions word_stress and accentuate: they correct known dictionary errors, restore stress from the letter ё and fit it to the meter.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a data_dir that is neither a string nor a Path.

sd.download()
sd.info["license"]

TextsByGrade(data_dir=DEFAULT_DATASET_DIR)

The dataset of grade-labeled texts from Ivan Begtin's Plain Russian Language project. The dataset contains 68 texts from the project repository distributed under the CC0 1.0 license: 55 from the TEXT_LIST list, on which the coefficients of the Russian readability formulas of the plainrussian preset of ReadabilityStats were fitted, and 13 from repository folders not included in the list. The label is the school grade or the year of study:

Label Texts Count 1 fairy tales, Bianki, Gaidar, Tolstoy 11 3-4 Troepolsky, Paustovsky, Rybakov, Korolenko, Grigorovich 10 5-9 Carroll, Shukshin, Kaverin, Tolstoy, Astafyev, Solzhenitsyn 12 10-11 Korolenko, Bunin, Kuprin, Platonov, Gorky, Rasputin, Dovlatov 18 12 Wikipedia article 1 15 newspaper article 1 17 regulatory and business documents: laws, regulations, government news 15

Labels 12-14 correspond to years 1-3 of university, 15-17 - to years 4-6, as in the grade_to_age table. Paragraphs are separated by line breaks; the hard line breaks of the original lib.ru files are removed.

docs.title: Readability formula checks
docs.text:
The dataset is used in the library tests to check the readability formulas: the Spearman correlation of formula values with the grade labels over all 68 texts must be at least 0.7, and that of the consensus grade at least 0.8. Values with the default coefficients:

Formula Spearman's ρ Mean absolute error, grades Flesch-Kincaid test 0.79 4.0 Flesch reading ease −0.79 - Coleman-Liau index 0.77 3.0 SMOG index 0.82 4.0 Automated readability index 0.80 3.9 LIX readability index 0.81 - RIX readability index 0.77 - Solovyev, Ivanov and Solnyshkina formula 0.77 4.7 Matskovsky formula 0.76 - Tuldava formula 0.78 - Dale-Chall index 0.82 3.8 Gunning fog index 0.80 3.9 Consensus grade 0.81 3.6

A breakdown over all groups of statistics - coefficient presets, lexis, syntax, morphology, cohesion and a check on the SovChLit reader - is in the notebook 02_text_complexity_by_grade.ipynb.

The mean consensus grade grows with the label: 3.0 for grade 1, 5.8 for grades 3-4, 6.5 for 5-9, 7.4 for 10-11 and 22.1 for documents labeled 12-17. The large error on documents is expected: the grade formulas are calibrated on school texts, and label 17 is nominal.

docs.title: Character N-gram extraction
docs.text:
CharNgramsExtractor(n=2, lowercase=False, within_words=False, tokenizer=None)

A class for extracting character N-grams from a text - sequences of N characters taken with a sliding window over the string. Character N-grams are a standard feature of stylometry and authorship attribution (Stamatatos 2009) and can replace words in measures such as Burrows's Delta.

Whitespace runs are collapsed into a single space, punctuation marks are kept. With within_words=True N-grams do not cross word boundaries: the text is split into words by the tokenizer, punctuation is dropped, and words shorter than N yield no N-grams.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - an n that is not an integer of at least one, a lowercase or within_words that is not a bool.

The class extends the CharNgramsExtractor of the anyTS core with the hook of Russian: its default word tokenizer for within_words, the method tokenize(text), is the default tokenizer of WordsExtractor, the tokenize function of the razdel library with the dialogue dashes glued to words split off (ruts.utils.iter_tokens). Stress marks and soft hyphens are removed from the text before extraction (ruts.utils.strip_marks). The list of N-grams is passed to delta as text units instead of words.

CodeResult 
from ruts import CharNgramsExtractor

text = "Кот сидел  на окне, а пёс - на полу."

ce = CharNgramsExtractor(n=3, lowercase=True)
ce.extract(text)[:6]
CharNgramsExtractor().extract(text)[:8]
CharNgramsExtractor(n=3, lowercase=True, within_words=True).extract(text)

('кот', 'от ', 'т с', ' си', 'сид', 'иде')
('Ко', 'от', 'т ', ' с', 'си', 'ид', 'де', 'ел')
('кот', 'сид', 'иде', 'дел', 'окн', 'кне', 'пёс', 'пол', 'олу')

A class for extracting sentences from a text.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description tokenizer Pattern / Callable None Tokenizer or regular expression; by default the sentenize method min_len int 0 Minimum length of an extracted sentence in characters, 0 for no bound max_len int 0 Maximum length of an extracted sentence in characters, 0 for no bound

Note

A regular expression as the tokenizer is a separator for re.split. A blank line - a line break, optional whitespace and another line break - ends a sentence of any tokenizer: the text is split at blank lines first and every part goes to the tokenizer, so a heading or a paragraph without a final mark is a sentence of its own, and so is a part without words, such as a line of asterisks, which the statistics leave out. The sentences are stripped of whitespace at the edges before the length bounds, and empty ones are dropped.

Note

A spaCy pipeline can be passed as the tokenizer: tokenizer=lambda text: (sent.text for sent in nlp(text).sents).

docs.title: Word extraction
docs.text:
WordsExtractor(tokenizer=None, filter_punct=True, filter_nums=False, use_lexemes=False, stopwords=None, lowercase=False, ngram_range=(1, 1), min_len=0, max_len=0)

A class for extracting words from a text.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - an ngram_range that is not a pair of integers or whose lower bound is below one or above the upper one, a length bound that is not an integer, a negative bound, a minimum above the maximum, a switch that is not a bool;
  • SourceTypeError - stop words that are not a collection of strings.

The class extends the WordsExtractor of the anyTS core with the hooks of Russian: the tokenizer tokenize(text) is the tokenize function of the razdel library with the dialogue dashes glued to words split off (ruts.utils.iter_tokens), the lemma lemmatize(word) is the first parse of the MorphAnalyzer of the pymorphy3 library (ruts.utils.parse_all: «её» is parsed as «ее», since pymorphy3 has no parse of «её» as a personal pronoun, «нем» as «нём», «есть» as «быть»), and the number pattern number_pattern also matches ranges, fractions and ordinals: 2020-2021, 5.5, 1,5, 3-й, 90-х. Before any tokenizer stress marks and soft hyphens are removed from the text, and й and ё of two characters are composed into one letter (ruts.utils.strip_marks).

CodeResult 
from ruts import WordsExtractor

text = "Не имей 100 рублей, а имей 100 друзей"

we = WordsExtractor(use_lexemes=True, stopwords=["не", "а"], filter_nums=True, ngram_range=(1, 2))
we.extract(text)

('иметь', 'рубль', 'иметь', 'друг', 'иметь_рубль', 'рубль_иметь', 'иметь_друг')

Parameter Type Default Description tokenizer Pattern / Callable None Tokenizer or regular expression; by default the tokenize method filter_punct bool True Filter punctuation marks filter_nums bool False Filter numbers matched by number_pattern use_lexemes bool False Use word lemmas of the lemmatize method stopwords Collection[str] None Stop words, compared case-insensitively lowercase bool False Convert words to lower case ngram_range tuple[int, int] (1, 1) Lower and upper bound of the N-gram size min_len int 0 Minimum length of an extracted word in characters, 0 for no bound max_len int 0 Maximum length of an extracted word in characters, 0 for no bound

Note

A regular expression as the tokenizer is a separator for re.split. The filters are applied in order: punctuation, numbers, lemmatization, lower case, stop words, word length. A punctuation mark is a token of marks and symbols only, multi-character ones included: ?!, --, …, € (anyts.utils.is_punctuation). Empty and whitespace tokens are dropped before the filters. N-grams join the words with _.

docs.title: Basic statistics
docs.text:
BasicStats(source, sents_extractor=None, words_extractor=None, normalize=False, complex_syl_factor=4, long_word_letter_factor=6)

The basic statistics of a text: the counts of its sentences, words, characters, syllables and punctuation marks and the distributions of its words. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy. Letters are counted by str.isalpha, so digits, hyphens and marks inside a word are not letters.

The words and the sentences of a string come from the extractors. A Doc gives its tokens as words, without punctuation marks and symbols such as € or %, and its boundaries as sentences, or those of the sentence extractor when it has none or only partial ones (has_sents); an extractor given is used on its text instead. A blank line ends a sentence of a string and of a Doc without boundaries; a Doc with boundaries does so when its pipeline has start_sents_after_blank_lines (registered by a language library under its own name) before the parser, senter or sentencizer. A sentence without words, such as punctuation alone, is not counted.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, an extractor of another type;
  • SourceError - a source without words;
  • ParameterError - a threshold that is not an integer of at least one, a normalize that is not a bool.

The class extends the BasicStats of the anyTS core with the hooks of Russian: the syllables of a word are counted by count_syllables, the default extractors are the Russian SentsExtractor and WordsExtractor, the punctuation marks are counted by the count_punctuations of ruTS, and the parts of a hyphenated word that spaCy splits are joined (во-первых is one word). The blank line component of ruTS is called ruts_blank_lines: nlp.add_pipe("ruts_blank_lines", before="parser"). Stress marks and soft hyphens count neither as characters nor as parts of words, and й and ё of two characters are one letter (ruts.utils.strip_marks): a text with stresses gives the same statistics as without them. The statistics are computed when the object is created; the print_stats table is in Russian.

CodeResult 
from ruts import BasicStats

text = "Существуют три вида лжи: ложь, наглая ложь и статистика"
bs = BasicStats(text, normalize=True)
bs.print_stats()

With normalize=True the object has the normalized statistics too, of the type float: the counts of the words divided by the number of words, those of the characters by the number of characters.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
count_words_by_syllables(min_syllables) and count_words_by_letters(min_letters) return the number of words with at least the given number of syllables or letters; a minimum that is not an integer raises ParameterError.

The methods recount complex and long words with a threshold other than the one set when the object was created: this is how ReadabilityStats computes the SMOG index (a complex word has 5 or more syllables) and LIX (a long word has 7 or more letters).

get_stats(flat) returns a dictionary with the distributions c_letters and c_syllables, the statistics of stats_desc, the distribution c_punctuations and, with normalize=True, the normalized counts, as a copy: editing it does not change the object. With flat=True the distributions give a key for every value the text has, such as c_letters_3 and c_punctuations_comma.

print_stats() prints a table with the statistics of stats_desc, their descriptions and the headers from stats_headers.

The normalized statistics p_* are not in the table.

to_dataframe() returns the flat statistics, get_stats(flat=True), as a one-row DataFrame of pandas with a column for every key. A dictionary statistic gives columns only for the keys the text has, so in frames of several texts joined with pandas.concat a count a text lacks is NaN. Only these columns may be filled with 0: elsewhere NaN is an undefined value.

docs.title: Punctuation marks
docs.text:
count_punctuations(text, marks=PUNCTUATION_MARKS, dash_pattern=DASH_PATTERN)

Counts punctuation marks by type, the distribution of c_punctuations: commas, periods, question and exclamation marks, ellipses, colons, semicolons, dashes, hyphens, guillemets, quotation marks, parentheses and other marks. Dashes typed with hyphens (dash_pattern) are counted first, then ellipses - …, three or more periods, or two after ? and !, one mark whose periods are not counted as periods (Who?.. is a question and an ellipsis) - then each mark by its type in marks; any other character of the Unicode categories P and S is another mark (§, €, °).

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string marks dict[str, str] PUNCTUATION_MARKS Type of every mark, among PUNCTUATION_TYPES dash_pattern Pattern DASH_PATTERN Dashes typed with hyphens

A mark of marks that is not a single character or has an unknown type raises ParameterError; a text that is not a string, marks that are not a mapping and a dash_pattern that is not a compiled regular expression raise SourceTypeError.

In ruTS the PUNCTUATION_MARKS and DASH_PATTERN of ruts.basic_stats are the marks of the core with the low quotation mark „ as a quotation mark and the pattern of dashes by which a hanging hyphen before и, или, либо or a comma stays a hyphen (двух- и трёхкомнатные, сорока-, пятидесятилетние), while a dialogue dash typed with a hyphen is a dash (- Ушли, - сказал он).

CodeResult 
from ruts.basic_stats import count_punctuations

text = "Кот — «зверь»... Пёс, конечно, - друг; а кто-то (тот, что ещё жив) — нет!"
{kind: count for kind, count in count_punctuations(text).items() if count}

docs.title: Dashes typed with hyphens
docs.text:
dash_pattern(conjunctions=(), hanging_before_comma=False)

Builds the dash_pattern of count_punctuations. A hanging hyphen glued to a letter or a digit and carried on to a later word (pre- and post-war, 5- and 10-year) stays a hyphen before spaces of a line and one of the conjunctions, case ignored, and with hanging_before_comma before a comma (two-, three- and four-year). A language whose dialogue closes a line with a hyphen before a comma (-Come -he said-, and left) leaves hanging_before_comma off. Without the parameters the pattern is DASH_PATTERN.

Parameter Type Default Description conjunctions Collection[str] () Conjunctions after a hanging hyphen hanging_before_comma bool False Take a hyphen between a letter and a comma for a hanging one

Conjunctions that are not a collection of strings raise SourceTypeError, and an empty conjunction ParameterError.

Without the parameters the pattern is the DASH_PATTERN of the core (anyts.basic_stats), while the DASH_PATTERN of ruts.basic_stats is dash_pattern(("и", "или", "либо"), hanging_before_comma=True).

CodeResult 
from ruts.basic_stats import count_punctuations, dash_pattern

text = "Двух- и трёхкомнатные, сорока-, пятидесятилетние - сказал он"
counts = count_punctuations(text)
counts["dash"], counts["hyphen"]
counts = count_punctuations(text, dash_pattern=dash_pattern())
counts["dash"], counts["hyphen"]

docs.title: Punctuation profile
docs.text:
punctuation_profile(text, n_words=None)

The frequencies of the punctuation marks by type (count_punctuations) per 1000 words and yo_share - the share of the letter ё among the letters е and ё, that is, whether the author writes ё. Without words or without the letters е and ё the values are nan. A text that is not a string raises SourceTypeError, a number of words that is not a non-negative integer ParameterError.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string n_words int None Number of words; without it the words are extracted by WordsExtractor

The profile is an editorial and stylometric feature: Chekhov has several times more ellipses and exclamations than Tolstoy (see corpus comparison). It depends on text formatting - typographic quotation marks and dashes, the letter ё - and is easy to fake, so it is best read separately from linguistic features.

CodeResult 
from ruts.basic_stats import punctuation_profile

text = "Кот — «зверь»... Пёс, конечно, - друг; а кто-то (тот, что ещё жив) — нет!"
profile = punctuation_profile(text)
round(profile["dash"], 1), round(profile["yo_share"], 2)

docs.title: Cohesion statistics
docs.text:
CohesionStats(source, sents_extractor=None, words_extractor=None, connectors=None)

The cohesion statistics of a text in the manner of Coh-Metrix and TAACO: the overlap of the sentences, the givenness, the temporal cohesion and the connectors of a dictionary. The sentences are compared by lemmas. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, an extractor of another type, connectors that are not a dictionary of phrases and pairs of strings;
  • SourceError - a source without words;
  • ParameterError - an unknown class or kind of a connector.

The class extends the CohesionStats of the anyTS core with the Russian layer and, unlike the core, reads a string too. A string and a Doc without sentence boundaries are split into sentences by the Russian SentsExtractor; the words of a string come from the Russian WordsExtractor or from the words_extractor given. For a Doc with part-of-speech annotation the part of speech, the tense and the aspect come from token.pos_ and token.morph, and the lemma from the pymorphy3 analysis with the part of speech of the token (unit_info); for a string, a Doc without annotation and a Doc with a word extractor given, from the first pymorphy3 analysis (words_info), where the answer «нет» is a particle. The parts of a hyphenated word that spaCy splits are joined (во-первых is one word). The connectors are found by RussianConnectorMatcher over the dictionary of load_connectors. The print_stats table and the error messages are in Russian (COHESION_STATS_DESC and CORE_MESSAGES of ruts.constants).

The words are classified by the pymorphy3 tags or by the Universal Dependencies annotation of a Doc:

Notion pymorphy3 Universal Dependencies (Doc) Nouns NOUN NOUN, PROPN Pronouns NPRO, Apro, lemmas of DEMONSTRATIVE_LEMMAS PRON, DET, lemmas of DEMONSTRATIVE_LEMMAS Arguments NOUN, NPRO NOUN, PROPN, PRON Content words CONTENT_POS without STOPWORD_GRAMMEMES and demonstratives CONTENT_UD_POS without demonstratives Demonstratives lemmas of DEMONSTRATIVE_LEMMAS: этот, это, тот, такой, таковой, столько, сей, оный the same lemmas Tense and aspect grammemes past, pres, futr and perf, impf of verb forms, the tense of the existential нет and нету features Tense and Aspect CodeResult 
from ruts import CohesionStats

text = "Кот сидел на окне. Он смотрел на птиц. Птицы улетели, и кот уснул. Завтра он снова будет сидеть на этом окне."
cs = CohesionStats(text)
cs.print_stats()

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Every metric is an attribute of the object, computed when it is created - the overlaps with the next sentences and paragraphs on first use; get_stats gives those of stats_desc, all but mood_repetition by default. The functions of the cards take a sentence as the collection of its elements - lemmas of nouns, arguments or content words, values of a feature of its verbs - and see no language.

Metric Measures Range Higher means noun_overlap_adjacent Share of the adjacent pairs of sentences sharing a noun 0-1, nan for one sentence Neighbouring sentences tied tighter noun_overlap_all Share of all the pairs of sentences sharing a noun 0-1, nan for one sentence The whole text tied tighter argument_overlap_adjacent Share of the adjacent pairs sharing a noun or a pronoun 0-1, nan for one sentence Neighbouring sentences tied tighter argument_overlap_all Share of all the pairs sharing a noun or a pronoun 0-1, nan for one sentence The whole text tied tighter content_overlap_adjacent Share of the adjacent pairs sharing a content word 0-1, nan for one sentence Neighbouring sentences tied tighter content_overlap_all Share of all the pairs sharing a content word 0-1, nan for one sentence The whole text tied tighter content_overlap_prop_adjacent Mean share of the shared content words (Dice) in the adjacent pairs 0-1, nan for one sentence More words shared by neighbours content_overlap_prop_all Mean share of the shared content words (Dice) in all the pairs 0-1, nan for one sentence More words shared across the text noun_overlap_2_sent Share of the nouns of a sentence repeated in one of the next two 0-1, nan for fewer than three sentences or without nouns in the compared ones More nouns carried on argument_overlap_2_sent Share of the arguments of a sentence repeated in one of the next two 0-1, nan for fewer than three sentences or without arguments in the compared ones More arguments carried on content_overlap_2_sent Share of the content words of a sentence repeated in one of the next two 0-1, nan for fewer than three sentences or without content words in the compared ones More content words carried on noun_overlap_para Share of the nouns of a paragraph repeated in the next one 0-1, nan for one paragraph or without nouns in the compared ones More nouns carried to the next paragraph argument_overlap_para Share of the arguments of a paragraph repeated in the next one 0-1, nan for one paragraph or without arguments in the compared ones More arguments carried to the next paragraph content_overlap_para Share of the content words of a paragraph repeated in the next one 0-1, nan for one paragraph or without content words in the compared ones More content words carried to the next paragraph p_pronouns Share of the pronouns among the words 0-1 More reference by pronouns pronoun_noun_ratio Ratio of the pronouns to the nouns 0 and above, nan without nouns More pronouns per noun p_demonstratives Share of the demonstratives among the words 0-1 More pointing back p_given Share of the content words whose lemma was used before in the text 0-1, nan without content words More given information tense_repetition Share of the adjacent pairs of sentences with the same dominant tense 0-1, nan without two adjacent sentences with the feature A steadier tense mood_repetition Share of the adjacent pairs with the same dominant mood 0-1, nan without two adjacent sentences with the feature A steadier mood aspect_repetition Share of the adjacent pairs with the same dominant aspect 0-1, nan without two adjacent sentences with the feature A steadier aspect temporal_cohesion Mean of the repetitions of temporal_features 0-1, nan when one of them is nan A steadier time frame connectors Connectors per 1000 words 0-1000 More explicit links connectors_inter Inter-sentential connectors per 1000 words 0-1000 More links to the sentences before connectors_intra Intra-sentential connectors per 1000 words 0-1000 More links inside the sentences connectors_<class>, connectors_<kind> Connectors of a class or a kind of the matcher per 1000 words 0-1000 More links of the class or the kind

A list of sentences that is a string, a Doc, an iterator, a set or a table raises SourceTypeError, and so does a sentence that is not a list of strings (check_words), such as a list of spaCy tokens. The overlaps (calc_overlap, calc_proportional_overlap, calc_overlaps) take a sentence as a set too; count_given and calc_repetition count the words in order and refuse a set.
