docs.title: Binary overlap
docs.text:
noun_overlap_adjacent · noun_overlap_all · argument_overlap_adjacent · argument_overlap_all · content_overlap_adjacent · content_overlap_all · Coh-Metrix

calc_overlap(sets, adjacent=True)

The binary overlap of Coh-Metrix (CRFNO1, CRFAO1, CRFSO1 over the adjacent pairs, CRFNOa, CRFAOa, CRFSOa over all of them): the share of the pairs of sentences that share at least one element; nan for a text shorter than two sentences.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of pairs sharing an element}}{\textrm{Number of pairs}} \] Parameter Type Default Description sets list[set[str]] - Elements of every sentence adjacent bool True Count the adjacent pairs only, otherwise all the pairs

docs.title: Proportional overlap
docs.text:
content_overlap_prop_adjacent · content_overlap_prop_all · Coh-Metrix

calc_proportional_overlap(sets, adjacent=True)

The proportional overlap of Coh-Metrix (CRFCWO1, CRFCWOa): the Dice coefficient of a pair of sentences (dice) averaged over the pairs; nan for a text shorter than two sentences.

\[ \frac{1}{\textrm{Number of pairs}} \sum_{(A, B)} \textrm{Dice}(A, B) \] Parameter Type Default Description sets list[set[str]] - Elements of every sentence adjacent bool True Count the adjacent pairs only, otherwise all the pairs 
dice(first, second)

The Dice coefficient of two sets, 0 for two empty sets.

\[ \frac{2 \times |A \cap B|}{|A| + |B|} \] Parameter Type Default Description first frozenset[str] - First set second frozenset[str] - Second set

docs.title: Overlap with the next sentences and paragraphs
docs.text:
noun_overlap_2_sent · argument_overlap_2_sent · content_overlap_2_sent · noun_overlap_para · argument_overlap_para · content_overlap_para · TAACO

The adjacent overlap of TAACO, by the lemmas of the nouns, of the arguments and of the content words: the share of the distinct lemmas of a sentence repeated in one of the next two sentences (adjacent_overlap_2_*_sent), and of a paragraph repeated in the next paragraph (adjacent_overlap_*_para), over all the sentences or paragraphs that have them (calc_forward_overlap). Unlike the binary overlap, a pair of segments counts by the share of the lemmas they share. A paragraph is a part of the text between blank lines that holds words; a word that carries paragraph_start opens one, inside a sentence too, as when a parser joins a heading to the next sentence. TAACO takes every line for a paragraph: a text with a paragraph on every line and no blank lines is one paragraph here, and its *_para are nan.

calc_forward_overlap(sets, span=1)

The share of the elements of a segment repeated in the next ones: the distinct elements of every segment with span segments after it that one of these segments holds, over the distinct elements of those segments; nan for no more segments than span or for segments without elements.

\[ \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n-k} |A_i \cap (A_{i+1} \cup \dots \cup A_{i+k})|}{\sum_{i=1}^{n-k} |A_i|} \] Parameter Type Default Description sets list[set[str]] - Elements of every segment span int 1 Number \(k\) of the next segments a segment is compared with

Segments that are a string, a Doc, an iterator or a segment that is not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, a span that is not an integer above 0 ParameterError.

In ruTS both a string and a Doc are split into paragraphs.

CodeResult 
from ruts.cohesion_stats import calc_forward_overlap

calc_forward_overlap([{"кот", "окно"}, {"птица"}, {"кот"}], span=2)
text = "Кот сидел на окне. Он смотрел на птиц.\n\nПтицы улетели, и кот уснул. Завтра он снова будет сидеть на этом окне."
paragraphs = CohesionStats(text)
paragraphs.n_paragraphs, paragraphs.noun_overlap_para, paragraphs.content_overlap_para

docs.title: Pronouns and demonstratives
docs.text:
p_pronouns · pronoun_noun_ratio · p_demonstratives

The pronouns, the nouns and the demonstratives are the words analyze marks so, with the features of word_info by default.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of pronouns}}{\textrm{Number of words}}, \quad \frac{\textrm{Number of pronouns}}{\textrm{Number of nouns}}, \quad \frac{\textrm{Number of demonstratives}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

In ruTS they are marked by the functions of the word features after the table of the classes of words.

docs.title: Givenness
docs.text:
p_given

count_given(sents)

The number of given elements: an element is given when the same lemma was used earlier in any sentence, the current one included; the first occurrence is new.

Parameter Type Default Description sents list[list[str]] - Lemmas of every sentence in the order of the text

docs.title: Temporal cohesion
docs.text:
tense_repetition · mood_repetition · aspect_repetition · temporal_cohesion · Coh-Metrix

calc_repetition(sents)

The repetition of the tense and of the aspect of Coh-Metrix (SMTEMP): the share of the adjacent pairs of sentences whose verbs have the same dominant value of the feature; a pair where one of the sentences has no verb with the feature is skipped, and without a single such pair the value is nan.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of pairs with the same dominant value}}{\textrm{Number of pairs with the feature}} \] Parameter Type Default Description sents list[list[str]] - Values of the feature of the verbs of every sentence 
dominant(values)

The dominant value: the most frequent one, the first of the equally frequent; None for an empty list.

Parameter Type Default Description values list[str] - Values

CohesionStats of ruTS does not compare the mood: mood_repetition is always nan, and temporal_cohesion is the mean of tense_repetition and aspect_repetition.

docs.title: Connectors
docs.text:
connectors · connectors_inter · connectors_intra · connectors_<class> · connectors_<kind>

The occurrences of the connectors found in every sentence by the matcher of connector_matcher_class, per 1000 words. An inter-sentential connector links a sentence to the ones before: it opens a sentence, unless the matcher takes it for a subordinator (is_subordinator), whose clause or phrase belongs to the same sentence; the others are intra-sentential. Every class and kind of the matcher gives a density: connectors_causal, connectors_adversative, connectors_concessive, connectors_temporal, connectors_additive, connectors_conditional, connectors_reformulative, connectors_primary and connectors_secondary by default.

\[ 1000 \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of connectors}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \] 
load_connectors()

The connector dictionary of ruTS: the file ruts/resources/connectors.tsv, 316 connectors with a class of CONNECTOR_CLASSES and a kind of CONNECTOR_TYPES of ruts.constants, compiled after the classification of Krioni, Nikin and Filippova (2008) and checked against the Ru-RSTreebank marker list, the Ruscon database and the causal marker list of Toldova et al. (2018). The one-word «и», «а», «но» are in the dictionary, as in Coh-Metrix and TAACO; «что» and «как» are no connectors.

Class Key Examples Causal (consequential and purposive included) causal потому что, поэтому, в результате, чтобы, таким образом Adversative adversative но, однако, зато, с другой стороны, в то же время Concessive concessive хотя, несмотря на, тем не менее, и всё же, в любом случае Temporal temporal когда, затем, после того как, тем временем, в дальнейшем Additive additive и, также, кроме того, более того, например, во-первых Conditional conditional если, в случае если, при условии что, в противном случае Reformulative reformulative то есть, иными словами, в общем, подводя итог

The primary connectors (primary) are conjunctions, adverbs and particles (потому что, однако, затем), the secondary ones (secondary) lexicalized phrases with nouns and verbs (в результате этого, с другой стороны, иными словами). The rules by which a word of the dictionary counts as a connector are those of the matcher.

docs.title: Connector matcher
docs.text:
RussianConnectorMatcher(connectors)

The search of the connectors (discourse markers: because, however, on the other hand) of a dictionary in the sentences of a text. The dictionary gives the class of every connector - causal, adversative, concessive, temporal, additive, conditional or reformulative (CONNECTOR_CLASSES) - and its kind, primary or secondary (CONNECTOR_KINDS). A connector is matched by the normalized forms of its words, the longest one at every position, without overlaps; a period or a hyphen inside a connector may be split off by the tokenizer (e.g. as e, g). An occurrence is a Connector: the number of the sentence sent, the positions start and end of its words, the connector text as the dictionary writes it, its class cls and kind kind.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a dictionary that is not a mapping of a phrase to a pair of strings;
  • ParameterError - an unknown class or kind.

RussianConnectorMatcher is a subclass of the core ConnectorMatcher with the rules of Russian. Words and connectors are compared in lower case without the letter ё and stress marks (normalize_yo). A one-word connector takes a part of speech of the core CONNECTOR_POS (CCONJ, SCONJ, PART, ADV, ADP, INTJ, X) or of CONNECTOR_POS_EXTRA for its form (for example: словом - NOUN, главное - ADJ, NOUN, допустим - VERB, точнее - ADJ, т.е. - PUNCT, значит - VERB, ежели and коли - NOUN, PROPN, VERB): «раз» as a noun is no connector. The context rules are lists of ruts.constants: words after a connector (CONNECTOR_BLOCKED_AFTER: пока что, хоть бы) and before it (CONNECTOR_BLOCKED_BEFORE: ещё раз, и так далее) that make it no connector; connectors that count inside a sentence only after particular words (CONNECTOR_ONLY_AFTER: и отсюда) and do not count at its start (CONNECTOR_NOT_AT_START: the interrogative отчего); parts of speech of the word after a connector that make it a preposition or a member of the clause (CONNECTOR_BLOCKED_AFTER_POS: после обеда, едва заметный). The rules read through a punctuation mark only for CONNECTOR_READ_THROUGH_MARKS (не знал, отчего), so the parenthetical значит, stays a connector, and a mark between the words of a connector of CONNECTOR_SPLIT_BY_MARKS splits it (так, как). These parts of speech and lists are attributes of the matcher: CONNECTOR_POS is pos_tags, the others are named without CONNECTOR_ in lower case (CONNECTOR_BLOCKED_AFTER is blocked_after); the attributes not_after_pos and start_only_pos are empty in ruTS, so these rules of find do not apply.

find(words, sent_index, pos, breaks, blocked) returns the occurrences of the connectors in a sentence in the order of its words. The words are those of one sentence without punctuation, the first one its start. With the parts of speech, a one-word connector counts only with one of pos_tags or of pos_extra for its form, never after one of not_after_pos, and with one of start_only_pos only at the start of the sentence; a word without a part of speech (None) passes. Without the parts of speech the rules that read them are skipped. The positions of the punctuation marks breaks cut a connector off its neighbours: a rule does not read a word across a mark, so in so, the end the word after the comma neither blocks nor lets the connector count, unless the connector is one of read_through_marks, and a mark between the words of a connector of split_by_marks makes it none; without them the words are read as adjacent. No connector starts at a word of blocked, which a language rules out by more than the words and their parts of speech, such as its parse.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the sentence sent_index int 0 Number of the sentence, written into the occurrences pos list[str] None Parts of speech of the words breaks set[int] None Positions of the words a punctuation mark stands before blocked set[int] None Positions of the words no connector starts at

Words that are not a list of strings and parts of speech that are not a list of strings and None (the tags token.pos_ of spaCy, not the numbers token.pos) and positions that are not a collection raise SourceTypeError, a number of the sentence or a position that is not an integer, a position of a mark that is not that of a word after the first, a blocked position that is not that of a word and parts of speech not as many as the words ParameterError.

is_subordinator(connector, pos=None) checks whether an occurrence of a connector ties its clause or phrase to its own sentence: a connector of subordinators, or a one-word connector whose part of speech pos is SCONJ or ADP, but none of parcellation. The clause of a subordinating conjunction and the phrase of a preposition belong to the sentence of the connector wherever it stands, so a subordinator opening a sentence (when he came, ..., despite the rain, ...) does not link it to the ones before. A connector that is not a Connector raises SourceTypeError.

The subordinators of ruTS besides the one-word ones tagged SCONJ and ADP are CONNECTOR_SUBORDINATORS: the multi-word conjunctions and prepositions (так как, после того как, несмотря на) and the one-word ones the spaCy models or pymorphy3 tag otherwise (ежели, коли, пока, раз, хоть, едва). A conjunction of CONNECTOR_PARCELLATION (ибо) opening a sentence attaches it to the one before, so it is no subordinator.

docs.text:
word_info(word)

words_info(sents, text)

token_info(token)

ud_info(word, pos, tense, aspect)

unit_info(unit)

The features of a word for the cohesion statistics, a WordInfo named tuple: lemma, noun, pronoun, demonstrative, argument, content, tense and aspect after the table of the classes of words. word_info takes them from the first pymorphy3 analysis; words_info does the same for the words of the sentences of a text, where the answer «нет» (Нет, не видел) is a particle without tense. token_info takes them from the spaCy annotation (token.pos_, Tense, Aspect), ud_info from a given part of speech, tense and aspect of UD; the lemma comes from the pymorphy3 analysis with that part of speech (ruts.utils.lemmatize), not from token.lemma_. unit_info gives the features of a word from its tokens: a single token by token_info, a hyphenated word of several tokens (жили-были, назовите-ка) by the pymorphy3 analysis of the joined text mapped to UD (word_to_ud).

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word (word_info, ud_info) sents list[list[str]] - Words of the sentences of a text (words_info) text str - Text the words are extracted from (words_info) token Token - spaCy token (token_info) pos, tense, aspect str - Part of speech, tense and aspect of UD (ud_info) unit list[Token] - Tokens of a word (unit_info) CodeResult 
from ruts.cohesion_stats import word_info

word_info("смотрел")

WordInfo(lemma='смотреть', noun=False, pronoun=False, demonstrative=False, argument=False, content=True, tense='past', aspect='impf')

docs.title: Words of a Doc
docs.text:
split_doc_units(source, sents_extractor, join_hyphens=False)

Splits the words of a Doc or a Span into the sentences of a sentence extractor, for a Doc without sentence boundaries or one to split otherwise: the sentences are found in its text in their order, and a word of iter_doc_units belongs to the sentence its first token lies in. The words outside the sentences found, those the extractor drops, are left out, so no sentence found gives no words.

Parameter Type Default Description source Doc / Span - Doc or Span object sents_extractor SentsExtractor - Sentence extraction tool join_hyphens bool False Join the parts of hyphenated words

CohesionStats always joins the parts of hyphenated words, the function only with join_hyphens=True.

unit_text(unit)

unit_pos(unit)

unit_text gives the text of a word from its tokens without a byte order mark, stress marks and soft hyphens (ruts.utils.strip_marks), unit_pos its part of speech of UD: that of the token for a single token, and that of connector_pos of the joined text for a hyphenated word of several tokens.

Parameter Type Default Description unit list[Token] - Tokens of a word CodeResult 
import spacy
from ruts import SentsExtractor
from ruts.cohesion_stats import split_doc_units, unit_text

doc = spacy.blank("ru")("Жили-были дед да баба. Во-первых, кот спит.")
units = split_doc_units(doc, SentsExtractor())
[[unit_text(unit) for unit in sent] for sent in units]
units = split_doc_units(doc, SentsExtractor(), join_hyphens=True)
[[unit_text(unit) for unit in sent] for sent in units]

[['Жили', 'были', 'дед', 'да', 'баба'], ['Во', 'первых', 'кот', 'спит']]
[['Жили-были', 'дед', 'да', 'баба'], ['Во-первых', 'кот', 'спит']]

docs.title: Lexical diversity metrics
docs.text:
DiversityStats(source, words_extractor=None, window_len=50, mtld_threshold=0.72, mtld_min_len=10, hdd_sample_size=42, log_base=10)

The main lexical diversity metrics of a text, computed from its words.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, an extractor of another type;
  • SourceError - a source without words;
  • ParameterError - a parameter that check_params rejects.

The class extends the DiversityStats of the anyTS core: instead of a list of words it takes a text or a Doc object of the spaCy library. The words of a text are extracted by the Russian WordsExtractor or by a given one, which for a Doc is applied to its text; without an extractor the words of a Doc come from its tokens without stress marks, and the parts of a hyphenated word that spaCy splits are joined (во-первых is one word). The words are always lower-cased. The print_stats table has Russian headers and the Russian descriptions of the metrics from ruts.constants.DIVERSITY_STATS_DESC, and the error messages are in Russian, from ruts.constants.CORE_MESSAGES.

Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc - Data source words_extractor WordsExtractor None Word extraction tool; for a Doc it is applied to its text window_len int 50 Window size for MATTR and segment size for MSTTR (MATTR_WINDOW_LEN) mtld_threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for MTLD, MA-MTLD and MTLD-W (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD) mtld_min_len int 10 Minimum factor length for MTLD, MA-MTLD and MTLD-W (MTLD_MIN_LEN) hdd_sample_size int 42 Sample size for HD-D (HDD_SAMPLE_SIZE) log_base float 10 Logarithm base for the Summer, Maas and Dugast metrics (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

The constants of the defaults in parentheses, here and in the cards, are those of anyts.constants.

The object keeps the words in words, a tuple, and the five parameters under their names, changeable on the object. frequency_spectrum is the frequency spectrum of the words (calc_frequency_spectrum), and honore_r an alias of hapax_index.

check_params(window_len=50, mtld_threshold=0.72, mtld_min_len=10, hdd_sample_size=42, log_base=10, *, messages=CORE_MESSAGES)

Checks the parameters of the metrics: a window_len or an hdd_sample_size that is not an integer of at least one, an mtld_min_len that is not a non-negative integer, an mtld_threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) and a log_base that is not a finite number above 1 raise ParameterError. Called before the words are extracted, it reports a wrong parameter before an empty text.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Some metrics depend on conventions that differ between libraries. All of them except the comparison with the MTLD threshold are class parameters:

Parameter Default Other libraries Logarithm base for Summer, Maas, Dugast's U and Dugast's k 10 LexicalRichness, textcomplexity and zipfR - natural MATTR window and MSTTR segment 50 quanteda and koRpus - 100 TTR threshold for MTLD 0.72 0.66-0.75 in the literature Comparison with the MTLD threshold a factor closes at TTR ≤ 0.72 (McCarthy & Jarvis, 2010) lexical-diversity and TAALED - strict <; the values differ when TTR hits the threshold exactly Minimum MTLD factor length 10 koRpus - only in MTLD-MA, dropping shorter factors instead of extending them; LexicalRichness and textcomplexity - not applied HD-D sample size 42 35-50 in the literature

According to Zenker and Kyle (2021), MATTR, MTLD and HD-D are stable on texts of 50-200 words and longer, MTLD-W, MA-MTLD and Maas are unstable on short texts, and the TTR family never stabilizes. Texts of different lengths are compared by the windowed computation with confidence intervals.

calc_dttr(text, base=10)

A logarithmic modification of TTR (Dugast, 1978), the reciprocal of the Maas metric. The value depends on the logarithm base (see the conventions). A text without repeated words has an infinite value.

\[ \frac{\log_{10} {{\textrm{(Number of words)}}}^2}{\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of words)}}-\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of lexemes)}}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words base float 10 Logarithm base (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

A base that is not a finite number above 1 raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Moving Average Type-Token Ratio (MATTR)
docs.text:
mattr

calc_mattr(text, window_len=50)

A moving-average modification of TTR (Covington & McFall, 2010), independent of text length: a window of fixed size slides over the text, and the TTR of every window is averaged. For texts shorter than the window the TTR of the whole text is returned.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words window_len int 50 Window size (MATTR_WINDOW_LEN)

A window_len that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Mean Segmental Type-Token Ratio (MSTTR)
docs.text:
msttr

calc_msttr(text, segment_len=50)

A segmentation-based modification of TTR (Johnson, 1944), independent of text length: the text is split into segments of fixed size, and the TTR of every segment is averaged; an incomplete last segment is dropped. For texts shorter than the segment the TTR of the whole text is returned.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words segment_len int 50 Segment size (MATTR_WINDOW_LEN)

A segment_len that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MTLD)
docs.text:
mtld

calc_mtld(text, min_len=10, threshold=0.72)

A modification of MSTTR (McCarthy, 2005), independent of text length: the number of words divided by the number of factors, the stretches on which TTR drops to the threshold (TTR <= threshold, see the conventions). An incomplete last factor counts in proportion to how close its TTR came to the threshold. The value is the mean of a forward and a backward pass (McCarthy & Jarvis, 2010). The minimum factor length is non-standard (Kyle's lexical-diversity), and a min_len of 0 disables it. If no factor completes and TTR never drops below 1, the value is infinity.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_len int 10 Minimum factor length (MTLD_MIN_LEN) threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for completing a factor (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD)

A min_len that is not a non-negative integer and a threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Moving Average Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MA-MTLD)
docs.text:
mamtld

calc_mamtld(text, min_len=10, threshold=0.72, step=1)

A moving-window modification of MTLD after MTLD-MA of koRpus: a factor starts at every position of the text, and the value is the mean length of the completed factors over a forward and a backward pass. koRpus makes the forward pass only, closes a factor at TTR strictly below the threshold and drops factors shorter than the minimum length instead of extending them. With a step of k a factor starts at every k-th position from either end, as MTLDMA.steps of koRpus, and only these factors are computed: a step of 10 is several times faster. If no factor completes, the value is nan. The metric is unstable on short texts.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_len int 10 Minimum factor length (MTLD_MIN_LEN) threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for completing a factor (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD) step int 1 Distance between the starts of the factors

A min_len that is not a non-negative integer, a threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) and a step that is not an integer above 0 raise ParameterError.

docs.title: MTLD with a moving window and text wrap (MTLD-W)
docs.text:
mtldw

calc_mtldw(text, min_len=10, threshold=0.72)

A modification of MA-MTLD after mtld_ma_wrap of lexical-diversity and TAALED: factors not completed by the end of the text continue from its beginning, so all positions get equal weight. A factor cannot be longer than the text. If no factor completes, because the text is shorter than min_len or TTR drops to the threshold from no start, the value is nan. The metric is unstable on texts shorter than 100 words.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_len int 10 Minimum factor length (MTLD_MIN_LEN) threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for completing a factor (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD)

A min_len that is not a non-negative integer and a threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Hypergeometric Distribution D (HD-D)
docs.text:
hdd

calc_hdd(text, sample_size=42)

An alternative to vocd-D (McCarthy & Jarvis, 2010): the exact expected TTR of a random sample of sample_size words, without drawing samples. The hypergeometric distribution gives the probability that the sample holds each lexeme at least once; HD-D is the sum of these probabilities divided by the sample size. For texts shorter than 50 words or than the sample size the metric is undefined, and the value is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words sample_size int 42 Sample size in words (HDD_SAMPLE_SIZE)

A sample_size that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Simpson's index (D)
docs.text:
simpson_index · Wikipedia

calc_simpson_index(text)

The probability that two words drawn from the text at random without replacement are the same lexeme; \(n\) is the number of occurrences of a lexeme in the text. For texts shorter than two words the index is undefined, and the value is nan; the same holds for the inverse Simpson's index and the Gini-Simpson index.

\[ \frac{\sum n\times(n-1)}{\textrm{(Number of words)}\times(\textrm{Number of words}-1)} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Inverse Simpson's index (1/D)
docs.text:
inverse_simpson_index · Wikipedia

calc_inverse_simpson_index(text)

An estimate of the Hill number of order two (\(1/\sum_k p_k^2\)) from pairs drawn without replacement. If all words of the text are unique, Simpson's index is 0 and the inverse index is infinity.

\[ \frac{1}{D} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Gini-Simpson index (1-D)
docs.text:
gini_simpson_index · Wikipedia

calc_gini_simpson_index(text)

The probability that two randomly chosen words of the text are different.

\[ 1-D \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Hapax index (Honoré's R)
docs.text:
hapax_index · honore_r · Wikipedia

calc_hapax_index(text)

A hapax (Greek ἅπαξ λεγόμενον - "said only once") is a word that occurs only once in a corpus: baciyelmo, Sancho Panza's word for the barber's basin that Don Quixote takes for a helmet, is a hapax of Cervantes (chapter 44 of the first part of Don Quixote). The index coincides with Honoré's measure (1979), with the natural logarithm. If all words of the text are hapaxes, the index is infinity; for texts shorter than two words it is undefined, and the value is nan. calc_honore_r is the same function.

\[ 100\times\frac{\ln {\textrm{(Number of words)}}}{1-\frac{\textrm{Number of hapaxes}}{\textrm{Number of lexemes}}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

A Russian example: боливар ("a hat of a certain style") is a hapax of Pushkin's language: the word occurs only in the famous passage of "Eugene Onegin".

docs.title: Frequency spectrum
docs.text:
frequency_spectrum

calc_frequency_spectrum(text)

The number of lexemes \(V_i\) occurring exactly \(i\) times in the text, as a dictionary by the frequency \(i\) in ascending order. The hapax index, Yule's K and I, Herdan's Vm, Sichel's S, Michéa's M, Baayen's P, the hapax ratio and the α₂ exponent are computed from it, with the formulas of Tweedie and Baayen (1998).

Notation: \(N\) - number of words, \(V\) - number of lexemes, \(V_i\) - number of lexemes with frequency \(i\), \(V_1\) - hapaxes, \(V_2\) - dis legomena, \(p_k\) - relative frequency of a lexeme.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Yule's characteristic (Yule's K)
docs.text:
yule_k

calc_yule_k(text)

Yule's characteristic (Yule, 1944), one of the few measures theoretically independent of text length (Tweedie & Baayen, 1998); in practice it converges as the text grows. It is proportional to Simpson's index: \(K \approx 10^4 \cdot D\). For texts shorter than two words the value is nan.

\[ K = 10^4\times\frac{\sum_i i^2 V_i - N}{N^2} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Inverse Yule's characteristic (Yule's I)
docs.text:
yule_i

calc_yule_i(text)

The inverse Yule's characteristic. If all words of the text are unique, the value is infinity; for texts shorter than two words it is nan.

\[ I = \frac{V^2}{\sum_i i^2 V_i - V} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Herdan's Vm
docs.text:
herdan_vm

calc_herdan_vm(text)

Herdan's measure (Herdan, 1955), theoretically independent of text length. For texts shorter than two words the value is nan.

\[ V_m = \sqrt{\sum_i V_i \left(\frac{i}{N}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{V}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Sichel's S
docs.text:
sichel_s

calc_sichel_s(text)

Sichel's measure (Sichel, 1975) - the share of dis legomena, lexemes with frequency 2, among all lexemes. Stable across texts of different lengths.

\[ S = \frac{V_2}{V} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Michéa's M
docs.text:
michea_m

calc_michea_m(text)

Michéa's measure (Michéa, 1969) - the reciprocal of Sichel's measure. If the text has no dis legomena, the value is infinity.

\[ M = \frac{V}{V_2} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Brunet's W
docs.text:
brunet_w

calc_brunet_w(text, a=0.172)

Brunet's measure (Brunet, 1978). Values for texts usually lie within 10-20.

\[ W = N^{V^{-a}}, \quad a = 0.172 \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words a float 0.172 Exponent (BRUNET_W_EXPONENT)

An a that is not a finite number raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Dugast's k
docs.text:
dugast_k

calc_dugast_k(text, base=10)

Dugast's measure (Dugast, 1979), not to be confused with Dugast's U - the DTTR metric. The value depends on the logarithm base. For texts no longer than the base (\(\log N \le 1\)) the measure is undefined, and the value is nan.

\[ k = \frac{\log V}{\log \log N} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words base float 10 Logarithm base (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

A base that is not a finite number above 1 raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Baayen's P
docs.text:
baayen_p

calc_baayen_p(text)

Baayen's measure (Baayen, 1991) - the share of hapaxes among all words of the text. It equals the slope of the vocabulary growth curve at the end of the text: the probability that the next word is new (Evert, 2004).

\[ P = \frac{V_1}{N} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Orlov's Z
docs.text:
orlov_z · Tweedie and Baayen 1998

calc_orlov_z(text)

The text length at which the law of Zipf fits the vocabulary best (Orlov 1983): the solution \(Z\) for \(N\) words, \(V\) lexemes and the share \(p\) of the most frequent lexeme. The right side has a minimum over \(Z\), and \(Z\) is the solution above it; it is nan when \(V\) lies at or below that minimum or when every word is a lexeme of its own, and inf when \(V\) comes so close to \(N\) that \(Z\) overflows a float. With Yule's K, Z separated the authors best among the measures Tweedie and Baayen compared.

\[ V = \frac{Z}{\ln(pZ)} \cdot \frac{N}{N - Z} \cdot \ln \frac{N}{Z} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words CodeResult 
from ruts.diversity_stats import calc_orlov_z

words = "снесла курочка яичко не простое а золотое дед бил бил не разбил баба била била не разбила".split()
round(calc_orlov_z(words), 2)

279.56

docs.title: Hapax ratio
docs.text:
hapax_ratio

calc_hapax_ratio(text)

The share of hapaxes among all lexemes of the text.

\[ \frac{V_1}{V} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: The α₂ exponent
docs.text:
alpha2

calc_alpha2(text)

An estimate of the Zipf-Mandelbrot parameter from the lower part of the frequency spectrum (Evert, 2004). If the text has no hapaxes, the value is nan.

\[ \alpha_2 = 1 - \frac{2 V_2}{V_1} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Shannon entropy
docs.text:
entropy · Wikipedia

calc_entropy(text)

The entropy of the lexeme distribution in bits. The Hill number of order one is \(2^H\) (perplexity), of order zero - \(V\); the inverse Simpson's index estimates the one of order two.

\[ H = -\sum_k p_k \log_2 p_k \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Evenness
docs.text:
evenness

calc_evenness(text)

Pielou's evenness - the ratio of the Shannon entropy to its maximum for the given number of lexemes. For texts of a single lexeme it is undefined, and the value is nan.

\[ \frac{H}{\log_2 V} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Perplexity
docs.text:
perplexity

calc_perplexity(text)

The Hill number of order one, the effective number of lexemes of the text.

\[ 2^H \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Zipf's law slope
docs.text:
zipf_alpha · Wikipedia

calc_zipf_alpha(text)

The exponent \(\alpha\) of Zipf's law \(f(r) \propto r^{-\alpha}\), where \(r\) is the frequency rank of a lexeme, estimated by linear regression of log frequency on log rank. For natural texts \(\alpha\) is close to 1. The rank-based least squares estimate is biased; maximum likelihood is more accurate. For texts of a single lexeme the value is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Zipf-Mandelbrot fit
docs.text:
Wikipedia

fit_zipf_mandelbrot(text)

Fits the Zipf-Mandelbrot law \(f(r) = C / (r + q)^s\) to the rank-frequency distribution. With \(q = 0\) it is Zipf's law with exponent \(s\); the shift \(q\) captures the flattening of the curve on the most frequent words. The fit is by least squares in logarithmic coordinates with \(q \ge 0\), \(s \ge 0\); the lexemes of zero frequency in a counter are left out. The result is a ZipfMandelbrot named tuple with the fields c, q, s and r2 - the coefficient of determination of the fit in logarithmic coordinates. All fields are nan for texts of fewer than three lexemes, with identical frequencies of all lexemes or when the fit diverges. The parameters are unstable on short texts: the law describes large corpora.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] / Counter - List of words or a counter of their frequencies

A counter whose words are not strings or whose frequencies are not numbers raises SourceTypeError, and a negative, nan or infinite frequency SourceError (check_counts).

The Zipf's law visualizer draws this fit with show_fit=True.

CodeResult 
from ruts.diversity_stats import fit_zipf_mandelbrot

# the frequencies 12, 6, 4, 3 follow the law f = 12 / r exactly
words = ["а"] * 12 + ["б"] * 6 + ["в"] * 4 + ["г"] * 3
fit = fit_zipf_mandelbrot(words)
round(fit.c, 3), round(fit.q, 3), round(fit.s, 3), round(fit.r2, 3)

(12.001, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0)

docs.title: Heaps' law exponent
docs.text:
heaps_beta · Wikipedia

calc_heaps_beta(text)

The exponent \(\beta\) of Heaps' law \(V(N) = K \cdot N^{\beta}\) of vocabulary growth with text length, estimated by linear regression of log vocabulary size on log text length along the growth curve. On corpora of millions of words \(\beta\) lies within 0.4-0.6, on a single text within 0.6-0.9, so the values are comparable only between texts of similar length. The value depends on word order and needs several hundred words or more. For texts shorter than two words the value is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words 
vocabulary_growth(text)

The vocabulary growth curve of a list of words: the vocabulary size after every word of the text.

fit_heaps(text)

Fits Heaps' law over the vocabulary growth curve of a list of words, as calc_heaps_beta does, and returns a HeapsFit named tuple with the parameters k, beta and the coefficient of determination r2, all nan for texts shorter than two words; r2 is nan for a text of one lexeme too.

The Heaps' law plot is built from fit_heaps.

docs.title: Burstiness
docs.text:
burstiness · Kim and Jo 2016

calc_burstiness(text, min_freq=5)

How a lexeme comes in bursts rather than spread over the text, by the burstiness of Kim and Jo, which corrects that of Goh and Barabási for a finite number \(n\) of events, averaged over the lexemes of min_freq occurrences or more (BURSTINESS_MIN_FREQ). For the \(n\) occurrences of a lexeme, \(r\) is the coefficient of variation of their \(n\) intervals, the one from the last to the first around the end of the text included. The value is −1 for occurrences at equal intervals, the one around the end included (a x a x a x a x a x is −1, a x a x a x a x a about −0.69), near 0 for a rare lexeme at random places and up to 1 for occurrences in bursts; nan without such lexemes.

\[ A_n = \frac{\sqrt{n + 1} \cdot r - \sqrt{n - 1}}{(\sqrt{n + 1} - 2) \cdot r + \sqrt{n - 1}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_freq int 5 Smallest number of occurrences of a lexeme measured

A min_freq that is not an integer of at least 2 raises ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from ruts.diversity_stats import calc_burstiness

(
    calc_burstiness("да нет да нет да нет да нет да нет".split()),
    calc_burstiness("да да да да да нет нет нет нет нет".split()),
)

(-1.0, 0.18350341907227388)

docs.title: Windowed computation
docs.text:
windowed(stat)

calc_windowed(text, func, window_len=100, step=None, confidence=0.95, *, messages=CORE_MESSAGES)

The values of a metric over consecutive windows of equal length give their mean, their sample standard deviation and the confidence interval of the mean by Student's distribution. The standard way to compare texts of different lengths; Kubát and Milička's standardized TTR (not Summer's STTR) is a windowed TTR with a 1000-word window and a 95% interval. A text shorter than the window is a single window; nan windows are ignored. With fewer than two windows of a defined value the deviation and the interval are nan, and without any the mean too. A metric infinite in any window (e.g. the inverse Simpson's index on a window of unique words) makes the mean infinite and the deviation and the interval nan. The result is a WindowStats named tuple with the fields mean, std, lower, upper and n_windows, the number of the windows of a defined value.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words func Callable - Function computing the metric from a list of words window_len int 100 Window size step int None Window step; the window size by default, so the windows do not overlap confidence float 0.95 Confidence level messages dict[str, str] MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key

A func that cannot be called raises SourceTypeError; a window_len or a step that is not an integer of at least one and a confidence that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

In ruTS messages defaults to CORE_MESSAGES.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
windowed(stat, window_len=100, step=None, confidence=0.95) computes a metric of get_stats by its name over windows: calc_windowed with the function of the metric and the parameters of the object. The other arguments, the result and the errors are those of calc_windowed; an unknown name raises UnknownStatError.

CodeResult 
ds.windowed("ttr", window_len=5)
ds.windowed("ttr", window_len=5, step=2).n_windows

WindowStats(mean=0.9333333333333332, std=0.11547005383792512, lower=0.6464898180167025, upper=1.220176848649964, n_windows=3)
6

docs.title: Lexical sophistication statistics
docs.text:
LexicalStats(source, words_extractor=None, freq_dict=None)

Lexical sophistication in the manner of TAALES (Kyle, Crossley and Berger, 2018) - how rare the words of a text are: statistics by a frequency dictionary and its unigram model, the shares of the frequency bands of a list of the most frequent lemmas and the lexical density. The statistics by the dictionary are computed when first read, so the bands and the lexical density need no dictionary data.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a dictionary of another class than that of the library or, without freq_dict_class, one without lookup and ipm or none at all; an analyze that does not give LexicalWord objects;
  • SourceError - a source without words.

In ruTS a source that is neither a string nor a Doc and an extractor of another type raise SourceTypeError too, and the metrics by the dictionary without the dictionary downloaded DatasetNotFoundError.

Unlike the lexical diversity metrics, which compare the words of a text with each other, here the words are compared with the frequencies of the language (TAALES). The data source is a text or a Doc object of the spaCy library.

The class extends the LexicalStats of the anyTS core with the Russian layer: the dictionary is the Lyashevskaya and Sharoff FreqDict (freq_dict_class), and the ranks of the lemmas and the size of the list (rank, top_size) come from the embedded list of the Sharoff lemmas (get_rank). The words of a string are extracted by the Russian WordsExtractor or by a given extractor, which for a Doc is applied to its text; without an extractor the words of a Doc come from its tokens, and the parts of a hyphenated word that spaCy splits are joined. Numbers (2020, 5.5, 3-й) are not words. The lemmas come from pymorphy3: for a Doc with part-of-speech annotation by the part of speech of the token (ruts.utils.lemmatize), otherwise by the first analysis. The keys of the words in the dictionary (keys, dictionary_keys) are the lemmas brought to its conventions by dictionary_lemma: должна - должен, денег - деньги, ночью - ночь. The print_stats table and the error messages are in Russian (LEXICAL_STATS_DESC and CORE_MESSAGES of ruts.constants).

CodeResult 
from ruts import LexicalStats
from ruts.datasets import FreqDict

FreqDict().download()
ls = LexicalStats("Кот сидел на окне и смотрел на птиц")
ls.print_stats()

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc - Data source words_extractor WordsExtractor None Word extraction tool; used for a Doc too, on its text freq_dict FreqDict None Frequency dictionary; FreqDict() from the default directory by default

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description freq_dict FrequencyDictionary Frequency dictionary words, lemmas tuple[str] Words and their lemmas; the bands are counted by the lemmas keys tuple[str] Keys of the words in the dictionary entries tuple[FrequencyEntry / None] Entries of the dictionary, None for a word out of it ranks tuple[int / None] Ranks of the lemmas, None out of the list n_words, n_content_words, n_found int Number of words, of content words and of words found in the dictionary

In ruTS the dictionary is a FreqDict, and its entries are the named tuples Entry.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Every metric is an attribute or a property of the object, and get_stats gives them all. A mean is over the words found in the dictionary, and without them it is nan.

Metric Measures Range Higher means coverage Share of the words found in the dictionary 0-1 More words known to the dictionary mean_ipm, mean_ipm_content Mean frequency per million words of the words found, of the content words found Above 0 More frequent words mean_log_ipm, mean_log_ipm_content Mean decimal logarithm of the frequency of the words found, of the content words found Up to 6 More frequent words mean_range Mean range of the words found 0 and above Words used in more parts of the corpus mean_dispersion Mean dispersion of the words found That of the dictionary By the measure of the dictionary surprisal Mean surprisal of the words by the unigram model of the dictionary, in bits 0 and above Rarer words perplexity 2 to the power of the surprisal 1 and above Rarer words p_top1000, p_top2000, p_top5000, p_top10000 Share of the words with a lemma in the top 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000 of the list 0-1, nan for a band beyond top_size More frequent words p_beyond_top10000 Share of the words with a lemma beyond the top 10000 0-1, nan for a list shorter than 10000 Rarer words lexical_density Share of the content words 0-1 More content words

The metrics rely on two resources; always read the means by the dictionary next to coverage.

Resource Metrics Availability FreqDict - the Lyashevskaya and Sharoff dictionary, 52,138 lemmas with ipm, R, D coverage, mean_ipm*, mean_log_ipm*, mean_range, mean_dispersion, surprisal, perplexity downloaded once with FreqDict().download() The embedded list of the 10,000 most frequent lemmas of the Leeds internet corpus (S. A. Sharoff, mirror hingston/russian, CC BY 2.5) p_top1000, p_top2000, p_top5000, p_top10000, p_beyond_top10000, band_coverage always

docs.title: Dictionary frequency
docs.text:
coverage · mean_ipm · mean_ipm_content · mean_log_ipm · mean_log_ipm_content · mean_range · mean_dispersion · Lyashevskaya, Sharoff

The metrics are computed from the FreqDict entries for the keys of the words (keys, entries): the means are taken over the words found in the dictionary, over all of them or only over the content words. The mean frequency in ipm is sensitive to function words (и - 35,000 ipm, в - 31,000), so for comparing texts the log frequency or the mean over the content words is more convenient. The mean frequency of the content words mean_ipm_content is the FREQ2 feature of the 2023 Solovyev, Ivanov and Solnyshkina formula, whose values in the paper lie within 200-1000 (sis_grade_by_freq).

Rare words lower the coverage and the log frequency and raise the surprisal and the share beyond the top 10000:

CodeResult 
from ruts import LexicalStats

ls = LexicalStats("Фелинолог пребывал на подоконнике")
ls.coverage, ls.mean_log_ipm, ls.surprisal, ls.p_beyond_top10000

(0.75, 2.3063585317426494, 14.515882690436708, 0.25)

docs.title: Surprisal and perplexity
docs.text:
surprisal · perplexity

calc_surprisal(lemmas, freq_dict)

The mean surprisal of the words by the unigram model of a frequency dictionary, in bits; a word out of the dictionary gets its lowest frequency min_ipm. The perplexity is 2 to its power.

\[ \frac{1}{N} \sum_{w} -\log_2 \frac{\max(\textrm{ipm}_w, \textrm{min\_ipm})}{10^6} \] Parameter Type Default Description lemmas list[str] - Keys of the words in the dictionary freq_dict FrequencyDictionary - Frequency dictionary

No words give nan; keys that are not a list of strings and a dictionary without ipm and min_ipm raise SourceTypeError, a lowest frequency that is not above zero ParameterError.

In ruTS the dictionary is a FreqDict with the lowest frequency of 0.4 ipm: a dictionary of another class raises SourceTypeError.

CodeResult 
from ruts.datasets import FreqDict
from ruts.lexical_stats import calc_surprisal

calc_surprisal(["кот", "сидеть", "фелинолог"], FreqDict())

15.570731790883956

docs.title: Frequency bands
docs.text:
p_top1000 · p_top2000 · p_top5000 · p_top10000 · p_beyond_top10000 · band_coverage(bands, unique)

The share of the words whose lemma has a rank (rank) within the top \(N\) of the list, for the bounds 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000 of FREQUENCY_BANDS; the share beyond the top 10000 is the rest, the words out of the list included. A band beyond the size of the list (top_size) is nan, and so is the share beyond the top 10000 for a list shorter than 10000.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of words with a rank up to } N}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

This builds a frequency band profile in the manner of the Lexical Frequency Profile.

get_rank(lemma)

The rank of a lemma by the embedded Sharoff list, None for a lemma outside the list; the lemma may be in any case, with ё or without.

Parameter Type Default Description lemma str - Lemma 
load_top_lemmas()

The whole list from the file ruts/resources/sharoff_top10000.txt: the rank of every lemma, lowercased and with ё replaced by е, starting from 1; duplicates keep the smaller rank.

CodeResult 
from ruts.lexical_stats import get_rank, load_top_lemmas

get_rank("и"), get_rank("кот"), get_rank("фелинолог")
len(load_top_lemmas())

(1, 2009, None)
9989

docs.title: Lexical density
docs.text:
lexical_density

The share of the content words (nouns, adjectives, verbs, adverbs without pronominal and parenthetical words) among all the words; a content word is defined by is_content_word for a string and by CONTENT_UD_POS for an annotated Doc.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of content words}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
band_coverage(bands, unique) gives the share of the words with a lemma in the top N of the list for every bound N of bands (FREQUENCY_BANDS by default), or with unique=True the share of the distinct lemmas. Bounds that are not a list of integers or a bound out of 1 and top_size() raise ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from ruts import LexicalStats

ls = LexicalStats("Кот сидел на окне и смотрел на птиц")
ls.band_coverage(unique=True)
ls.band_coverage(bands=(100, 500))

docs.title: Morphological statistics
docs.text:
MorphStats(source, words_extractor=None)

The morphological statistics of a text: the part of speech and the features of Universal Dependencies of every word, counted by value or given word by word. By default the data source is a Doc object of spaCy with the parts of speech, read by token.pos_ and token.morph; a language library reads a string or a Doc without them in its own way.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is not a Doc, an analyze that does not give MorphWord objects;
  • SourceError - a source without parts of speech or without words.

In ruTS the data source is a text or a Doc with or without part-of-speech annotation, and the statistics are computed when the object is created. A source that is neither a string nor a Doc and an extractor of another type raise SourceTypeError, and only a source without words raises SourceError.

The class extends the MorphStats of the anyTS core with the Russian analysis of the words and the markers of the verb forms. The words of a string are extracted by the Russian WordsExtractor or by a given extractor, which for a Doc is applied to its text; without an extractor the words of a Doc come from its tokens, and the parts of a hyphenated word that spaCy splits are joined. The print_stats and print_markers tables and the error messages are in Russian (MORPHOLOGY_STATS_DESC, MORPHOLOGY_MARKERS_DESC and CORE_MESSAGES of ruts.constants).

CodeResult 
from ruts import MorphStats

text = "Постарайтесь получить то, что любите, иначе придется полюбить то, что получили"
ms = MorphStats(text)
ms.print_stats("pos", "tense", "number", "person", filter_none=True)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc - Data source words_extractor WordsExtractor None Word extraction tool; used for a Doc too, on its text

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description words tuple[str] Words of the text tags tuple[str] Features of every word in the CoNLL-U format (Case=Nom|Number=Plur), _ for a word without them pos tuple[str / None] Part of speech of every word animacy, aspect, ..., voice tuple[str / None] Value of a statistic for every word, None for a word without the feature

ruTS also has the attribute lemmas (tuple[str]) - the lemmas of the words that pymorphy3 gives by the part of speech of the word.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
The statistics are the part of speech pos and the features of the table below (MORPHOLOGY_FEATURES of ruts.constants). For a Doc object with part-of-speech annotation the values are taken from token.pos_ and token.morph, that is, by context (стали is a verb or a noun). For a string, a Doc without annotation and a Doc with a words extractor given the first pymorphy3 analysis is used: the OpenCorpora grammemes are mapped to UD by the OPENCORPORA_TO_UD_POS and OPENCORPORA_TO_UD_GRAMMEMES tables of ruts.constants, and a feature that pymorphy3 gives two values at once (the animacy of words in -кки) is undefined.

Statistic Feature Values pos Part of speech NOUN, PROPN, VERB, AUX, ADJ, DET, PRON, NUM, ADV, ADP, CCONJ, SCONJ, PART, INTJ, X animacy Animacy Anim, Inan aspect Aspect Perf, Imp case Case Nom, Gen, Dat, Acc, Ins, Loc, Par, Voc degree Degree of comparison Pos, Cmp, Sup gender Gender Masc, Fem, Neut, Com involvement Clusivity In, Ex mood Mood Ind, Imp, Cnd number Number Sing, Plur person Person 1, 2, 3 polarity Negation Neg style_variant Short form Short tense Tense Past, Pres, Fut transitivity Transitivity Tran, Intr verb_form Verb form Fin, Inf, Part, Conv voice Voice Act, Pass, Mid

The values for a string and for an annotated Doc may differ: spaCy assigns Voice=Act to finite forms and Voice=Mid to reflexive verbs, distinguishes AUX and resolves homonymy by context; pymorphy3 determines voice only for participles and takes the first analysis.

docs.title: Part of speech
docs.text:
pos · UD

For a string the OpenCorpora parts of speech are mapped to UD as follows:

OpenCorpora UD Note NOUN NOUN, PROPN first names, surnames, patronymics, toponyms and organizations by pymorphy3 tags - PROPN, but only for capitalized word forms: pymorphy3 ignores case and tags ordinary words as names (лев, роза, мороз) ADJF, ADJS, COMP ADJ, DET, PRON, NUM pronominal adjectives (этот, мой, весь) - DET, «который» - PRON, «один» - NUM; a comparative without context counts as an adjective VERB, INFN, PRTF, PRTS, GRND VERB the form goes into verb_form: Fin, Inf, Part, Conv; the auxiliary AUX is distinguished only by spaCy NUMR, NUMB, ROMN NUM ADVB, PRED ADV predicatives (надо, нельзя) - adverbs without tense, as in the Russian UD corpora; the existential нет and нету, which UD treats as verbs, have the present tense NPRO PRON PREP ADP CONJ CCONJ, SCONJ subordinating conjunctions by the SUBORDINATING_CONJUNCTIONS list (что, чтобы, если, когда, хотя, потому) PRCL PART INTJ INTJ LATN, UNKN X

есть is taken for a form of быть, not of есть meaning to eat.

docs.title: Degree, negation and short form
docs.text:
degree · polarity · style_variant

For a string these features are derived by the rules of Russian UD. Adjectives (except pronominal ones) and adverbs have a degree: Cmp for the comparative and for более, менее, выше, ниже, Sup for the superlative (красивейший), Pos for the others. The particles не, ни and the answer нет (Нет, не пойду, but not Денег нет) carry the negation. Short adjectives and participles (рад, прочитана) carry the short form, but not the forms in -о like неверно, нужно, so a string has fewer short forms than a Doc of a model.

CodeResult 
from ruts import MorphStats

ms = MorphStats("Нет, я не рад: книга прочитана быстрее красивейшей сказки")
ms.explain_text("degree", "polarity", "style_variant", filter_none=True)

docs.title: Transitivity and clusivity
docs.text:
transitivity · involvement · OpenCorpora

OpenCorpora features absent from Russian UD: transitivity (Tran, Intr) and clusivity (In - the speaker is included in the action, Ex - not included). They are computed via pymorphy3 for verbs (for a Doc - from the analysis with the spaCy lemma) and appear in the tags feature string as Subcat and Clusivity.

CodeResult 
from ruts import MorphStats

ms = MorphStats("Постарайтесь получить то, что любите")
ms.tags[0]
ms.transitivity, ms.involvement

'Aspect=Perf|Clusivity=Ex|Mood=Imp|Number=Plur|Subcat=Intr|VerbForm=Fin'
(('Intr', 'Tran', None, None, 'Tran'), ('Ex', None, None, None, None))

docs.title: Verb forms
docs.text:
get_markers() · print_markers()

The shares of the grammatical forms of the verb (the words with the part of speech VERB and AUX), each of its own base; a share with an empty base is nan.

Marker Share Base p_indicative, p_imperative, p_conditional of the indicative, imperative and conditional mood finite forms p_infinitive, p_participle, p_converb of infinitives, participles and converbs all verb forms p_perfective of the perfective aspect verb forms with aspect p_passive of passive participles all verb forms p_reflexive of reflexive forms in -ся, -сь all verb forms

The conditional mood is detected by the particle бы (б), so the words extractor must not drop particles.

ms = MorphStats("Если бы я знал, я бы пришел за книгами, прочитанными вчера")
ms.get_markers()

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
get_stats(*stats, filter_none=False, flat=False) gives the number of the words by value of every statistic selected, all of them by default, in the order of the first occurrences; None counts the words without the feature, and filter_none leaves them out. With flat the keys are statistic_value, such as pos_NOUN, without the words that lack the feature, as in to_dataframe. An unknown statistic raises UnknownStatError.

explain_text(*stats, filter_none=False) gives every word with the values of the statistics selected; filter_none leaves out those a word lacks. An unknown statistic raises UnknownStatError.

print_stats(*stats, filter_none=False) prints a table for every statistic selected: the descriptions of its values from the most frequent, with the number of the words. A value of several joins the descriptions of its parts with a slash. An unknown statistic raises UnknownStatError.

CodeResult 
from ruts import MorphStats

text = "Постарайтесь получить то, что любите, иначе придется полюбить то, что получили"
ms = MorphStats(text)
ms.get_stats("pos", "tense", "number", "person", filter_none=True)
ms.get_stats("pos", "tense", flat=True)
ms.explain_text("pos", "tense", "number", "person", filter_none=True)

to_dataframe() returns the flat statistics, get_stats(flat=True), as a one-row DataFrame of pandas with a column for every key. A dictionary statistic gives columns only for the keys the text has, so in frames of several texts joined with pandas.concat a count a text lacks is NaN. Only these columns may be filled with 0: elsewhere NaN is an undefined value.

In ruTS the markers are the shares of the verb forms.

The describe method is that of the statistics interface of the anyTS core; the morphological statistics have no scales, so it gives None for the statistics of get_stats.

MorphWord is a word of analyze: its text word, its part of speech pos (None when unknown) and its features features - the values of the features of Universal Dependencies by their names ({"Case": "Nom"}), a value of several joined by commas.

In ruTS MorphWord is imported from ruts.morph_stats too.

docs.title: Phonostatistics
docs.text:
PhonStats(source, words_extractor=None, window_len=3)

The phonetic statistics of a text: its sounds by class, their clusters, sequences and repetitions, and its syllables. A sound is a letter of a word by default, or a sound of its transcription when a library gives one. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy; the words are taken in lower case, and an extractor passed explicitly is used on the text of a Doc.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, an extractor of another type;
  • SourceError - a source without words;
  • ParameterError - a window that is not an integer of at least 2.

The class extends the PhonStats of the anyTS core with the hooks of Russian: the sounds are the letters of a word in the classes of the table below, without devoicing, reduction and stress; the iotated е, ё, ю, я after a vowel make no hiatus, and a word is divided into syllables by the rising sonority rule (Avanesov) of the syllabify function. Stress marks are dropped from the words of a text and of a Doc, and the parts of a hyphenated word that spaCy splits are joined (во-первых is one word). The print_stats table and the error messages are in Russian (PHON_STATS_DESC and CORE_MESSAGES of ruts.constants). The computation time grows linearly with the length of the text.

Class Letters Constant Vowels а, е, и, о, у, ы, э, ю, я, ё RU_VOWELS Sonorant consonants л, м, н, р, й RU_CONSONANTS_SONOR, RU_CONSONANTS_YET Voiced obstruents б, в, г, д, ж, з RU_CONSONANTS_HIGH Voiceless obstruents к, п, с, т, ф, х, ц, ч, ш, щ RU_CONSONANTS_LOW Signs ь, ъ - no sounds: not counted in the shares and do not break a consonant cluster RU_MARKS CodeResult 
from ruts import PhonStats

text = "Ног нет, а хожу, рта нет, а скажу: когда спать, когда вставать, когда работу начинать"
ps = PhonStats(text)
ps.print_stats()

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Every metric is an attribute of the object, computed when it is created, and get_stats gives them all.

Metric Measures Range Higher means p_vowels Share of the vowels among the sounds of the classes 0-1, nan without sounds A more vocalic text p_sonorants Share of the sonorants among the sounds of the classes 0-1, nan without sounds A more sonorous text p_voiced Share of the voiced obstruents among the sounds of the classes 0-1, nan without sounds More voiced obstruents p_voiceless Share of the voiceless obstruents among the sounds of the classes 0-1, nan without sounds More voiceless obstruents consonant_vowel_ratio Ratio of the consonants to the vowels 0 and above, nan without vowels Denser consonants p_heavy_clusters Share of the clusters of three consonants or more 0-1, nan without clusters Heavier clusters p_hiatus Hiatuses of word_hiatus per word 0 and above, nan without sounds More vowels in a row cv_entropy Shannon entropy of the CV patterns of the words, in bits 0 and above, nan without sounds More varied shapes of the words hardness Voiceless obstruents to the vowels and the sonorants 0 and above, nan without vowels and sonorants A harder sound alliteration Repetition index of the consonants in windows of window_len words 0 and above, nan for a text shorter than the window or with no consonant shared by two words Consonants repeated closer together assonance Repetition index of the vowels in windows of window_len words 0 and above, nan for a text shorter than the window or with no vowel shared by two words Vowels repeated closer together p_open_syllables Share of the syllables that end in a vowel 0-1, nan without syllables More open syllables mean_syllable_len Mean length of a syllable in sounds 1 and above, nan without syllables Longer syllables

The functions of ruTS take words as strings and count by the Russian classes of letters of the table above. The calc_* functions check their arguments: words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, and a window that is not an integer of at least 2 ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from ruts.phon_stats import (
    calc_alliteration,
    calc_consonant_clusters,
    calc_cv_entropy,
    calc_hiatus,
    cv_pattern,
    is_open_syllable,
)

words = ["слышно", "бесшумно", "шуршат", "камыши", "у", "поэта"]
cv_pattern("всплеск"), is_open_syllable("съе")
calc_consonant_clusters(words)
calc_hiatus(words), calc_cv_entropy(words)
calc_alliteration(words, window_len=2)

docs.title: Shares of the classes of the sounds
docs.text:
p_vowels · p_sonorants · p_voiced · p_voiceless

The share of the sounds of every class - the vowels, the sonorants and the voiced and voiceless obstruents - among the sounds of all of them; a sound of skipped or of no class (a digit, a letter of another script) counts in none.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of sounds of the class}}{\textrm{Number of vowels and consonants}} \]

docs.title: Ratio of the consonants to the vowels
docs.text:
consonant_vowel_ratio

The number of the consonants n_consonants to the number of the vowels n_vowels.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of consonants}}{\textrm{Number of vowels}} \]

docs.title: Consonant clusters
docs.text:
p_heavy_clusters · c_clusters

calc_consonant_clusters(text)

The distribution of the consonant clusters of the words by length. A cluster is a run of consonants inside a word, a single consonant between vowels or at the edge of a word included; ь and ъ do not break a cluster.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Hiatuses
docs.text:
p_hiatus

calc_hiatus(text)

The number of the vowel hiatuses, two or more vowels in a row inside a word: аэропорт, аист, поэзия (о-э). The iotated е, ё, ю, я after a vowel denote [j] and a vowel and make no hiatus: заяц, моя, красивая, читает.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Entropy of the CV patterns
docs.text:
cv_entropy

The Shannon entropy of the CV patterns of the words (cv_pattern), in bits, where \(P(p)\) is the share of the words with the pattern \(p\) among the words that have one.

\[ -\sum_{p} P(p) \log_2 P(p) \] 
calc_cv_entropy(text)

The entropy of the CV patterns of a list of words: the higher the value, the more varied the phonetic shape of the words. Words without vowels and consonants (numbers, Latin script) are left out, and without other words the value is nan.

cv_pattern(word)

The CV pattern of a word or a syllable: vowels are marked V, consonants C, and ь, ъ and the other characters are left out.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words (calc_cv_entropy) word str - Word or syllable (cv_pattern)

docs.title: Hardness
docs.text:
hardness

The number of the voiceless obstruents to the number of the vowels and the sonorants.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of voiceless obstruents}}{\textrm{Number of vowels} + \textrm{Number of sonorants}} \]

docs.title: Alliteration and assonance
docs.text:
alliteration · assonance

calc_alliteration(text, window_len=3)

calc_assonance(text, window_len=3)

The alliteration and assonance indices of a list of words: the repetition index calc_repetition_index over the consonant and over the vowel letters of the words. Letters are compared, not sounds: devoicing, stress and reduction are not taken into account.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words window_len int 3 Window in words (PHON_WINDOW_LEN) 
calc_repetition_index(words, window_len, features=None)

The repetition index: the number of windows of window_len neighbouring words where a feature (a letter or a sound) occurs in two words or more, summed over the features, divided by the number expected if the words stood in random order. A window of shuffled words is a sample without replacement, so for a feature found in \(K\) of the \(N\) words, a window of \(w\) words holds it in two words or more with the hypergeometric probability

\[ P = 1 - \frac{\binom{N-K}{w} + K \binom{N-K}{w-1}}{\binom{N}{w}} \]

and the expected number is the sum of these probabilities over the features times the \(N - w + 1\) windows. Since the expectation comes from the text itself, the index shows whether the repetitions gather in neighbouring words, not how frequent a feature is: it averages to 1 over the orders of the words and is well above 1 when the repetitions come closer than chance. A word counts a feature once; the index is nan for a text shorter than the window or with no feature shared by two words.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] / list[list[str]] - Features of every word: a string of its letters or a collection of its sounds window_len int - Window in words, at least 2 features Collection[str] None Features to count, all of them by default

Words that are not a list of strings or of collections of strings and features that are not a collection of strings raise SourceTypeError, and a window_len that is not an integer of at least 2 ParameterError.

docs.title: Syllables
docs.text:
p_open_syllables · mean_syllable_len

The syllables are the sounds of every syllable of a word by syllable_sounds; a syllable without a sound of the classes (a number) is no syllable, in c_syllable_patterns too. An open syllable ends in a vowel by its CV pattern (cv_pattern), and the length of a syllable is the length of that pattern: the sounds of the classes, without skipped and the signs out of them.

In ruTS the length of a syllable is the number of its letters without ь and ъ.

is_open_syllable(syllable)

Checks whether a syllable is open, that is ends in a vowel; ь and ъ after a vowel do not close it.

Parameter Type Default Description syllable str - Syllable

docs.title: Readability metrics
docs.text:
ReadabilityStats(source, sents_extractor=None, words_extractor=None, preset='plainrussian')

The readability metrics of a text from its basic statistics: the mean sentence length in words, the mean word length in syllables or letters, the share of polysyllabic and of long words and the variability of word length. The data source is a text, a Doc object of spaCy or ready basic statistics, which are reused as they are; the extractors are passed on to the basic statistics of a text or a Doc. The formulas count only the letters of the counted words, so a word extractor that drops words does not lengthen the mean word.

The metrics are properties computed on each access, so a change of the coefficients of an object applies at once.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string, a Doc nor basic statistics, basic statistics of a class other than those of the library, an extractor of another type, a string or a Doc to a class without basic_stats_class;
  • SourceError - a source without words or sentences;
  • ParameterError - an unknown preset or one that is not a string.

The metrics assess readability on the side of the language - the complexity of words and syntactic constructions, not the typographic design of the text. They presume that short sentences are easier to read than long ones, long words make reading harder, and low-frequency and unfamiliar words slow a reader down.

The class extends the ReadabilityStats of the anyTS core with the hooks of Russian, given in the cards of the metrics: the basic statistics of ruTS, which take the Russian SentsExtractor and WordsExtractor by default, the coefficient presets, the Russian formulas, the consensus grade over the formulas of ruTS, the stages of the Russian school, the scales with Russian labels and the reading speeds of Russian readers. The print_stats table and the error messages are in Russian (READABILITY_STATS_DESC and CORE_MESSAGES of ruts.constants).

CodeResult 
from ruts import ReadabilityStats

text = "Ног нет, а хожу, рта нет, а скажу: когда спать, когда вставать, когда работу начинать"
rs = ReadabilityStats(text)
rs.print_stats()
