docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc / BasicStats - Data source (a string, a Doc object or ready basic statistics) sents_extractor SentsExtractor None Sentence extraction tool words_extractor WordsExtractor None Word extraction tool preset str 'plainrussian' Coefficient preset: plainrussian, fiction or academic

The object keeps the basic statistics of the text in bs, the name of the preset in preset, read-only, and the coefficients of the preset by formula in coefficients, a copy that can be changed for one object. An object of another preset can reuse the basic statistics: ReadabilityStats(rs.bs, preset="fiction").

docs.title: Coefficient presets
docs.text:
The coefficients of the formulas are parameters of their functions, and a preset gives them by formula. The presets differ in the coefficients of the Flesch-Kincaid test and the Flesch index; the coefficients of the Coleman-Liau, SMOG and ARI indices in all presets come from the plainrussian project, since no other adaptations for Russian have been published, and the other formulas do not depend on the preset.

Preset Source Corpus Flesch-Kincaid test Flesch index plainrussian Plain Russian Language (Begtin) 68 grade-labeled texts 0.318·ASL + 14.2·ASW − 30.5 206.835 − 1.3·ASL − 60.1·ASW (Oborneva, variant A, since plainrussian does not derive the Flesch index) fiction Oborneva (2005/2006) about 6 million words of fiction 0.5·ASL + 8.4·ASW − 15.59 206.835 − 1.3·ASL − 60.1·ASW (variant A) academic Solovyev, Ivanov, Solnyshkina (2018); Solnyshkina and Kiselnikov (2015) 14 social studies textbooks for grades 5-11 0.36·ASL + 5.76·ASW − 11.97 (FKG_SIS) 206.836 − 1.52·ASL − 65.14·ASW (Oborneva, variant B)

Here ASL is the mean number of words per sentence, ASW the mean number of syllables per word. The table of all coefficients is ruts.constants.READABILITY_PRESETS.

CodeResult 
ReadabilityStats(text).flesch_kincaid_grade
ReadabilityStats(text, preset="fiction").flesch_kincaid_grade
ReadabilityStats(text, preset="academic").flesch_kincaid_grade

-2.0633333333333326
5.91
3.0299999999999994

The presets agree with the grade label alike but give different scales, and they do not order texts quite alike. On the TextsByGrade dataset the Spearman correlation of the Flesch-Kincaid test with the grade label for all three presets is 0.79, while the medians of the test by label group differ:

Label Texts plainrussian fiction academic 1 11 2.9 7.5 4.0 3-4 10 4.2 8.7 4.9 5-9 12 4.4 8.7 4.9 10-11 18 6.7 11.7 7.0 12-17 17 23.7 24.4 15.9 1 (SovChLit) 179 1.5 6.1 3.1

On school texts (labels 1-11) the test with the fiction preset is about four grades above the label (median deviation +3.9 against −0.9 for plainrussian and −0.2 for academic), and about five on the first-grade reader SovChLit. Its value should therefore not be read as a grade of the Russian school: for the grade of the reader use plainrussian (the default; its coefficients were fitted on TextsByGrade) or academic, and fiction to compare with works that use Oborneva's coefficients. The consensus grade depends on the preset less, since the Flesch-Kincaid test is only one of its formulas (the median on TextsByGrade is 7.75 for fiction against 6.75 for plainrussian).

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
A formula is computed by the function of its card on the counts of bs; the default coefficients of the functions are adapted for Russian. The core formulas take their coefficients from coefficients, where the preset sets those of the Flesch-Kincaid test, the Flesch index and the Coleman-Liau, SMOG and ARI indices, while the formulas of Solovyev, Ivanov and Solnyshkina, of Matskovsky and of Dale-Chall are computed with the coefficients of their functions, and coefficients does not affect them. A formula of counts gives nan when the number of words or of sentences it divides by is zero. The formulas of other languages, with their original coefficients and without a calibration for Russian, are computed by the UnadaptedReadabilityStats class.

Metric Measures Range Higher means flesch_kincaid_grade Grade by the sentence length and the syllables per word Years of schooling, below 0 for the simplest texts A harder text flesch_reading_easy Ease of reading by the sentence length and the syllables per word Nominally 0-100, above 100 for the simplest texts and below 0 for the hardest An easier text coleman_liau_index Grade by the letters and the sentences per 100 words Years of schooling, below 0 for the simplest texts A harder text smog_index Grade by the complex words per sentence Years of schooling A harder text automated_readability_index Grade by the letters per word and the sentence length Years of schooling, below 0 for the simplest texts A harder text lix Sentence length and the share of long words 0 and above A harder text rix Long words per sentence 0 and above A harder text sis_grade Grade by the sentence length and the letters per word School grade, below 0 for the simplest texts A harder text matskovsky_index Sentence length and the share of complex words 0 and above A harder text tuldava Syllables per word and the logarithm of the sentence length 0 and above A harder text dale_chall_index Grade by the share of complex words and the sentence length Years of schooling A harder text gunning_fog_index Grade by the sentence length and the share of complex words Years of schooling A harder text consensus_grade Median of the grade formulas and the reading ease as a grade Years of schooling, below 0 for the simplest texts A harder text reading_time Reading time at the reading speed (reading_speed) Minutes, above 0 A longer text mu_index Mean word length in letters against its variance; outside get_stats Above 0, nan with fewer than two words or without variability An easier text

docs.title: Flesch-Kincaid grade
docs.text:
flesch_kincaid_grade · Kincaid et al., 1975

calc_flesch_kincaid_grade(n_syllables, n_words, n_sents, a=0.318, b=14.2, c=30.5)

The years of schooling needed to read the text, by the mean sentence length in words and the mean word length in syllables.

\[ a \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} + b \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of syllables}}{\textrm{Number of words}} - c \]

The default coefficients come from the current version of the Plain Russian Language project. Other coefficients for Russian are given by the presets: Oborneva's (0.5, 8.4, 15.59) and FKG_SIS of Solovyev, Ivanov and Solnyshkina (0.36, 5.76, 11.97).

Parameter Type Default Description n_syllables int - Number of syllables n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 0.318 Coefficient a, at the mean sentence length b float 14.2 Coefficient b, at the mean word length c float 30.5 Coefficient c, the constant

docs.title: Flesch reading ease
docs.text:
flesch_reading_easy · Flesch, 1948

calc_flesch_reading_easy(n_syllables, n_words, n_sents, a=1.3, b=60.1, c=206.835)

The ease of reading a text by the mean sentence length in words and the mean word length in syllables.

\[ c - a \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} - b \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of syllables}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

The default coefficients are Oborneva's (2005/2006, variant A). Variant B of the same works (1.52, 65.14, 206.836), used by the Kazan group, is given by the academic preset.

Parameter Type Default Description n_syllables int - Number of syllables n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 1.3 Coefficient a, at the mean sentence length b float 60.1 Coefficient b, at the mean word length c float 206.835 Coefficient c, the constant

The bands of describe are the scale ruts.constants.READING_EASE_LEVELS:

Value Reading [90, ∞) 5th grade [80, 90) 6th grade [70, 80) 7th grade [60, 70) 8th and 9th grade [50, 60) 10th and 11th grade [30, 50) university (−∞, 30) university graduate

docs.title: Coleman-Liau index
docs.text:
coleman_liau_index · Coleman and Liau, 1975

calc_coleman_liau_index(n_letters, n_words, n_sents, a=0.055, b=0.35, c=20.33)

The years of schooling needed to read the text, by the letters and the sentences per 100 words.

\[ a \cdot \frac{100 \cdot \textrm{Number of letters}}{\textrm{Number of words}} - b \cdot \frac{100 \cdot \textrm{Number of sentences}}{\textrm{Number of words}} - c \]

The default coefficients come from the Plain Russian Language project.

Parameter Type Default Description n_letters int - Number of letters of the words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 0.055 Coefficient a, at the letters per 100 words b float 0.35 Coefficient b, at the sentences per 100 words c float 20.33 Coefficient c, the constant

docs.title: SMOG index
docs.text:
smog_index · McLaughlin, 1969

calc_smog_index(n_complex, n_sents, a=1.1, b=64.6, c=0.05)

The years of schooling needed to read the text, by the polysyllabic words per sentence. In the original formula the polysyllabic words have three or more syllables and b brings their number to a sample of 30 sentences.

\[ a \cdot \sqrt{b \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of polysyllabic words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}}} + c \]

A number of words or sentences that is not a non-negative integer raises ParameterError.

The default coefficients of the Plain Russian Language project were fitted for complex words of five or more syllables, so ReadabilityStats passes the number of words of at least 5 syllables to the function (ruts.constants.SMOG_COMPLEX_SYL_FACTOR) rather than the n_complex_words attribute of the basic statistics.

Parameter Type Default Description n_complex int - Number of complex words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 1.1 Coefficient a, at the square root b float 64.6 Coefficient b, under the square root c float 0.05 Coefficient c, the constant

docs.title: Automated readability index (ARI)
docs.text:
automated_readability_index · Smith and Senter, 1967

calc_automated_readability_index(n_letters, n_words, n_sents, a=6.26, b=0.2805, c=31.04)

The years of schooling needed to read the text, by the letters per word and the words per sentence.

\[ a \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of letters}}{\textrm{Number of words}} + b \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} - c \]

The default coefficients come from the Plain Russian Language project.

Parameter Type Default Description n_letters int - Number of letters of the words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 6.26 Coefficient a, at the letters per word b float 0.2805 Coefficient b, at the mean sentence length c float 31.04 Coefficient c, the constant

The grade can be read as reader age:

Value Age 1 6-7 years 2 7-8 years 3 8-9 years 4 9-10 years 5 10-11 years 6 11-12 years 7 12-13 years 8 13-14 years 9 14-15 years 10 15-16 years 11 16-17 years 12 17-18 years 13 18-24 years 14 24+ years

docs.title: LIX readability index
docs.text:
lix · Björnsson, 1968

calc_lix(n_long_words, n_words, n_sents)

The mean sentence length plus the percentage of long words, the words of more than six letters; there are no coefficients to fit. The values read as text types:

Value Text 0-30 very easy texts, children's books 30-40 easy texts, fiction, newspaper articles 40-50 texts of medium difficulty, magazine articles 50-60 hard texts, popular science, official texts 60-100 very hard texts, laws and bureaucratic language \[ \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} + \frac{100 \cdot \textrm{Number of long words}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_long_words int - Number of long words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences

These bands are the scale of describe, ruts.constants.LIX_LEVELS; its last band is open above. The n_long_words attribute of the basic statistics of ruTS counts words of six or more letters, so ReadabilityStats passes the number of words of at least 7 letters to the function.

rix · Anderson, 1983

calc_rix(n_long_words, n_sents)

docs.title: Solovyev, Ivanov and Solnyshkina formula
docs.text:
sis_grade · sis_grade_by_stage(stage) · Solovyev, Ivanov, Solnyshkina, 2023

calc_sis_grade(n_letters, n_words, n_sents, a=-17.5, b=0.56, c=2.45)

The school grade needed to read a Russian academic text, by the mean sentence length in words and the mean word length in letters, not in syllables as in the Flesch-Kincaid test. The formula was derived on the Russian Academic Corpus of 154 textbooks for grades 2-11 (5.7 million tokens); the mean error is about one grade. The authors computed the mean sentence length over spaCy tokens, which include punctuation, so the ruTS computation over words gives a slightly lower grade.

\[ a + b \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} + c \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of letters}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_letters int - Number of letters of the words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float -17.5 Coefficient a, the constant b float 0.56 Coefficient b, at the mean sentence length c float 2.45 Coefficient c, at the mean word length

The default coefficients are those of the general formula. The coefficients the authors give for the education stages are in the ruts.constants.SIS_GRADE_STAGES table, taken by the sis_grade_by_stage method:

Stage a b c grades 2-4 -2.59 0.17 0.61 grades 5-7 -5.29 0.20 1.34 grades 8-11 -3.26 0.21 1.35

docs.title: Solovyev, Ivanov and Solnyshkina formula with frequency
docs.text:
sis_grade_by_freq(mean_ipm, stage) · Solovyev, Ivanov, Solnyshkina, 2023

calc_sis_grade_freq(n_letters, n_words, n_sents, mean_ipm, a=-14.46, b=0.58, c=2.15, d=-0.0026)

The variant of the general formula with a fourth feature FREQ2 - the mean frequency of the words of the text by the Lyashevskaya and Sharoff dictionary (table 7 of the paper): the more frequent the words, the lower the grade. In the paper FREQ2 values lie within 200-1000, which corresponds to the mean frequency of content words (LexicalStats.mean_ipm_content); the mean over all words including conjunctions and prepositions is several times larger. On the TextsByGrade dataset the formula with frequency gives the same correlation with the grade as the formula without it (Spearman's ρ 0.76 against 0.77), as in the paper.

\[ a + b \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} + c \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of letters}}{\textrm{Number of words}} + d \cdot \textrm{FREQ2} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_letters int - Number of letters of the words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences mean_ipm float - Mean frequency of content words (ipm) a float -14.46 Coefficient a, the constant b float 0.58 Coefficient b, at the mean sentence length c float 2.15 Coefficient c, at the mean word length d float -0.0026 Coefficient d, at the mean frequency

The default coefficients are those of the general formula. The coefficients of the education stages from the same table are in the ruts.constants.SIS_GRADE_FREQ_STAGES table, taken by the stage parameter of the sis_grade_by_freq method:

Stage a b c d grades 2-4 -1.21 0.2 0.56 -0.0025 grades 5-7 -5.18 0.17 1.35 -0.00043 grades 8-11 1.3 0.23 0.88 -0.0035 CodeResult

rs.sis_grade, rs.sis_grade_by_stage("2-4")
rs.sis_grade_by_freq(LexicalStats(text).mean_ipm_content)

docs.title: Matskovsky formula
docs.text:
matskovsky_index · Matskovsky, 1976

calc_matskovsky_index(n_complex, n_words, n_sents, a=0.62, b=0.123, c=0.051)

The first readability formula for Russian, derived by the method of successive intervals - by the mean sentence length and the percentage of complex words. A complex word here has more than three syllables, so ReadabilityStats passes the number of words of at least 4 syllables to the function.

\[ a \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} + b \cdot \frac{100 \cdot \textrm{Number of complex words}}{\textrm{Number of words}} + c \] Parameter Type Default Description n_complex int - Number of complex words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 0.62 Coefficient a, at the mean sentence length b float 0.123 Coefficient b, at the share of complex words c float 0.051 Coefficient c, the constant

docs.title: Tuldava formula
docs.text:
tuldava · Tuldava, 1975

calc_tuldava(n_syllables, n_words, n_sents)

The text difficulty formula of Tuldava ("Ob izmerenii trudnosti tekstov" - "On measuring the difficulty of texts", Uchenye zapiski Tartuskogo universiteta, issue 345, 1975, pp. 102-120) as given by Ivanov, Solnyshkina and Solovyev (2018): the mean number of syllables per word times the decimal logarithm of the mean sentence length in words; there are no coefficients to fit. The formula has no scale and no conversion to a grade: it does not enter the consensus grade, and describe gives None. koRpus computes it with the natural logarithm.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of syllables}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \cdot \lg \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_syllables int - Number of syllables n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences CodeResult 
from ruts import ReadabilityStats
from ruts.readability_stats import calc_tuldava

docs.title: Dale-Chall index
docs.text:
dale_chall_index · Dale and Chall, 1948

calc_dale_chall_index(n_complex, n_words, n_sents, a=0.552, b=0.273)

The years of schooling in the US system needed to understand the text, by the percentage of complex words and the mean sentence length. The original formula takes the share of unfamiliar words by a list of 3000 familiar ones; no such free list exists for Russian, so the adaptation of the Plain Russian Language project with the share of complex words is applied. A complex word has five or more syllables, so ReadabilityStats passes the number of words of at least 5 syllables to the function (ruts.constants.SMOG_COMPLEX_SYL_FACTOR). The original coefficients of the formula are 0.1579 and 0.0496.

\[ a \cdot \frac{100 \cdot \textrm{Number of complex words}}{\textrm{Number of words}} + b \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_complex int - Number of complex words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 0.552 Coefficient a, at the share of complex words b float 0.273 Coefficient b, at the mean sentence length

docs.title: Gunning fog index
docs.text:
gunning_fog_index · Gunning, 1952

calc_gunning_fog_index(n_complex, n_words, n_sents, a=0.4)

The years of schooling needed to read the text, by the mean sentence length and the percentage of complex words, in the original formula the words of three or more syllables.

\[ a \cdot \left(\frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{Number of sentences}} + \frac{100 \cdot \textrm{Number of complex words}}{\textrm{Number of words}}\right) \]

The index is used in the adaptation of the Plain Russian Language project: a complex word has five or more syllables, so ReadabilityStats passes the number of words of at least 5 syllables to the function (ruts.constants.SMOG_COMPLEX_SYL_FACTOR). SEO services additionally multiply the result by 0.78; no justification for this multiplier has been published.

Parameter Type Default Description n_complex int - Number of complex words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences a float 0.4 Coefficient a

docs.title: Consensus grade
docs.text:
consensus_grade

The consensus_grade attribute is the median of the values of the grade formulas (grade_stats) rounded half up, together with the reading ease in years of schooling (reading_ease_to_grade), not rounded. A library aligns the bounds of reading_ease_grades, and of each scale of preset_reading_ease_grades, with its scale of the reading ease, so that the consensus grade and describe read the value alike.

The grade formulas of ruTS (ruts.constants.READABILITY_GRADE_STATS) are the Flesch-Kincaid test, the Coleman-Liau, SMOG, ARI, Dale-Chall and Gunning indices and the Solovyev, Ivanov and Solnyshkina formula, and the Flesch index is converted to a grade by the bands of its reading scale, so an index of 45 reads as university both in describe and in the consensus grade. The consensus grade is an analog of text_standard of textstat, which takes the mode instead of the median; the median is more robust to the outliers of individual formulas.

calc_consensus_grade(grades, flesch_reading_easy=None, to_grade=flesch_reading_easy_to_grade)

The median of the values of the grade formulas rounded half up, together with the reading ease in years of schooling by to_grade, not rounded - so a band of 8.5 votes for 8.5.

\[ \textrm{median}\left(\lfloor g_1 + 0.5 \rfloor, \ldots, \lfloor g_k + 0.5 \rfloor, \textrm{to\_grade}(\textrm{reading ease})\right) \] Parameter Type Default Description grades list[float] - Values of the grade formulas flesch_reading_easy float None Value of the reading ease to_grade Callable flesch_reading_easy_to_grade Conversion of the reading ease into years of schooling

No values at all, a grade or a reading ease that is not a finite number raise ParameterError; grades that are not a list and a to_grade that is not callable raise SourceTypeError.

flesch_reading_easy_to_grade(flesch_reading_easy, grades=((90, 5), (80, 6), (70, 7), (60, 8.5), (50, 10.5), (30, 14), (0, 17)), below=17)

Conversion of the Flesch reading ease into years of schooling for the consensus grade: the grade of the first band whose lower bound the value reaches, or below under the last bound; values above 100 belong to the first band. A reading ease or a below that is not a finite number raises ParameterError, and so do grades that are empty or not pairs of finite numbers with descending bounds.

The default bands of ruTS are the bands of the reading scale of the index (READING_EASE_LEVELS), so that the consensus grade and describe read a value alike: 8.5 and 10.5 are the middles of the bands "8th and 9th grade" and "10th and 11th grade", 14 is "university" and 17 is "university graduate", that is university years 1-3 and 4-6 by the table of stages. These bands are ruts.constants.READING_EASE_GRADES, the reading_ease_grades attribute of ReadabilityStats:

Flesch index Grade [90, ∞) 5 [80, 90) 6 [70, 80) 7 [60, 70) 8.5 [50, 60) 10.5 [30, 50) 14 (−∞, 30) 17 Parameter Type Default Description flesch_reading_easy float - Value of the reading ease grades list[tuple[float, float]] READING_EASE_GRADES Lower bounds and their grades in descending order of the bounds below float 17 Grade below the last bound

docs.title: Reading time
docs.text:
reading_time · reading_time_by_speed(wpm) · reading_time_by_norm(norm) · Kuznetsov and Khromov, 1991

calc_reading_time(n_words, wpm=180, *, messages=CORE_MESSAGES)

The reading time of a text in minutes: the number of words divided by the reading speed.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of words}}{\textrm{wpm}} \]

A number of words that is not a non-negative integer and a speed that is not a positive number raise ParameterError.

The silent reading norm of an adult is 120-180 words per minute (Kuznetsov and Khromov, 1991); the upper bound is the default. The norms are in the ruts.constants.READING_SPEED_NORMS table, the reading-aloud norms of primary school by the Russian federal standard among them:

Norm Words per minute adult_silent 120-180 grade_1 25-40 grade_2 60-80 grade_3 80-100 grade_4 90-110 Parameter Type Default Description n_words int - Number of words wpm float 180 Reading speed, words per minute (READING_SPEED_WPM) messages dict[str, str] CORE_MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key, a keyword

docs.title: Legibilidad µ
docs.text:
mu_index · Muñoz Baquedano and Muñoz Urra, 2006

The mean number of letters per word divided by its sample variance, times 100; there are no coefficients to fit. Words without letters (numbers) are left out; with fewer than two words or without variability the index is undefined (nan).

\[ 100 \cdot \frac{\bar{x}}{s^2}, \quad s^2 = \frac{\sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2}{n - 1} \]

where \(x_i\) is the number of letters of a word and \(n\) the number of words.

The index was fitted on Spanish texts, so it stays outside the get_stats of ruTS, though the object has the mu_index property. Its function is calc_mu_index of the anyTS core.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
describe_grade(stat) returns the school stage and reader age for the consensus grade or the grade formula stat, consensus_grade by default; another metric raises ParameterError.

describe_level(stat) returns the band of the interpretation scale (level_scale) of the metric stat, flesch_reading_easy by default; a metric without a scale of bands and an undefined value (nan) raise ParameterError.

describe(stat) returns the reading of any metric by its scale: for the consensus grade and a grade formula the school stage and reader age (describe_grade), for a metric with a scale of bands (level_scale) its band, for another metric of grade_scales the stage and age of the years of schooling its scale gives, and None for a metric without a scale or with an undefined value (nan). A name that is neither in stats_desc nor a public property of the class raises UnknownStatError.

reading_time_by_speed(wpm) returns the reading time of the text in minutes at the speed wpm, words per minute; a speed that is not a positive number raises ParameterError.

reading_time_by_norm(norm) returns the reading times of the text in minutes at the speeds of the norm norm of reading_speed_norms, in their order; an unknown norm raises ParameterError.

In ruTS the norms come from the ruts.constants.READING_SPEED_NORMS table, and the method returns the reading times at the upper and at the lower bound of the norm.

sis_grade_by_stage(stage) returns the value of the Solovyev, Ivanov and Solnyshkina formula with the coefficients of the education stage stage: 2-4, 5-7 or 8-11; an unknown stage raises ParameterError.

sis_grade_by_freq(mean_ipm, stage=None) returns the value of the formula with frequency at the mean frequency of content words mean_ipm - the mean_ipm_content attribute of LexicalStats - with the coefficients of the stage stage or, without it, of the general formula. A negative or infinite frequency, a frequency that is not a number and an unknown stage raise ParameterError, and nan gives nan.

get_stats() returns a dictionary of the readability metrics of stats_desc.

print_stats() prints a table of the readability metrics with their descriptions from stats_desc under the headers of stats_headers.

CodeResult 
from ruts import ReadabilityStats

text = "Ног нет, а хожу, рта нет, а скажу: когда спать, когда вставать, когда работу начинать"
rs = ReadabilityStats(text)
rs.describe_grade(), rs.describe_grade("gunning_fog_index")
rs.describe("flesch_reading_easy"), rs.describe_level("lix")
rs.describe("rix"), rs.describe("matskovsky_index")
rs.reading_time_by_speed(120), rs.reading_time_by_norm("grade_1")
rs.get_stats()

docs.title: Scales
docs.text: The describe_level method reads the Flesch index, LIX and RIX by the scales of bands of their cards (ruts.constants.READABILITY_LEVEL_SCALES), and describe reads any metric: these three by the same scales, the grade formulas and the consensus grade by the education stages of grade_to_age; for a metric without a scale it gives None.

docs.title: School stage and age
docs.text:
grade_to_age(grade, levels=((1, 3, '1-3-й класс', '6-8 лет'), (4, 6, '4-6-й класс', '9-11 лет'), (7, 9, '7-9-й класс', '12-14 лет'), (10, 11, '10-11-й класс', '15-16 лет'), (12, 14, '1-3-й курс вуза', '17-19 лет'), (15, 17, '4-6-й курс вуза', '20-22 года')), above=('аспирантура', 'старше 22 лет'))

The school stage and reader age by the value of a grade formula: the value is rounded half up and falls into the first stage whose last year it does not exceed, values below 1 into the first stage; above the last stage lies above. A grade that is not a finite number, stages that are not quadruples of two whole years and two strings in ascending order of the years and an above that is not a pair of strings raise ParameterError.

The default stages of ruTS are taken from the GRADE_TEXT table of the Plain Russian Language project (ruts.constants.GRADE_AGE_LEVELS and POSTGRADUATE_LEVEL):

Grade Stage Age 1-3 grades 1-3 6-8 years 4-6 grades 4-6 9-11 years 7-9 grades 7-9 12-14 years 10-11 grades 10-11 15-16 years 12-14 university years 1-3 17-19 years 15-17 university years 4-6 20-22 years above 17 postgraduate over 22 years Parameter Type Default Description grade float - Value of a grade formula levels list[tuple[int, int, str, str]] GRADE_AGE_LEVELS Stages as the first and the last year, the stage and the age, in ascending order above tuple[str, str] POSTGRADUATE_LEVEL Stage and age above the last stage

docs.title: Band of a scale
docs.text:
scale_level(value, scale)

The band of a scale for a value: the scale is given as the lower bounds of its bands in descending order, the value falls into the first band whose bound it reaches, and the lowest band is open below.

Parameter Type Default Description value float - Value of a metric scale list[tuple[float, Any]] - Lower bounds and their bands in descending order

A value that is not a finite number and a scale that is empty, not a list of pairs of a finite lower bound and a band or with bounds that do not descend raise ParameterError.

The scales of ruTS are ruts.constants.READING_EASE_LEVELS, LIX_LEVELS and RIX_LEVELS.

CodeResult 
from ruts.constants import READING_EASE_LEVELS
from ruts.readability_stats import calc_flesch_reading_easy, scale_level

flesch = calc_flesch_reading_easy(n_syllables=60, n_words=30, n_sents=2)
flesch, scale_level(flesch, READING_EASE_LEVELS)

docs.title: Stage norms
docs.text:
The consensus grade tells which stage a text is for, but not what a text of that stage is like. For this the ruts.constants.LEVEL_NORMS table holds the norms of the features of the stages: the usual ranges (quartiles) of the sentence length in words, the word length in letters, the share of words of five or more syllables and the lexical diversity MTLD of texts of at least 100 words labeled with the stage in the SovChLit and TextsByGrade datasets. School stages with at least 10 such texts have norms:

Stage Texts Words per sentence Letters per word Share of words of 5+ syllables MTLD grades 1-3 73 8.1-10.7 4.56-5.03 0.0-0.022 104-178 grades 4-6 12 10.2-14.6 5.16-5.33 0.039-0.052 220-373 grades 10-11 18 15.6-17.9 5.11-5.57 0.035-0.065 277-513

The norms of grades 1-3 come almost entirely from texts of grade 1 (70 of 73), so a text for grades 2-3 can come out above the norm, the sentence length above all. Grades 7-9 have seven texts in the datasets, and the university labels of TextsByGrade mark a Wikipedia article, a newspaper article and regulatory documents, not texts written for students of a given year, so these stages have no norms. The features of a text shorter than 100 words, MTLD above all, should not be compared with the norms.

docs.title: Features of a text
docs.text:
level_features(source)

The features of a text that the stage norms cover: words per sentence, letters per word (of the words the grade formulas count), the share of words of five or more syllables (the complex words of SMOG, Gunning fog and Dale-Chall) and the lexical diversity MTLD. They are computed the same way as for the norms, so they can be compared with them; the features of a Doc are computed from its text, not from the sentence boundaries of spaCy. A source that is neither a string nor a Doc raises SourceTypeError, a source without words or sentences SourceError.

Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc - Data source (a string or a Doc object)

docs.title: Norms and the reading of a feature
docs.text:
level_norms(grade)

The norms of the features of the stage a grade belongs to - the usual range (quartiles) of each feature of level_features - or None for a stage without norms. A grade belongs to a stage as in grade_to_age: it is rounded half up, and a grade below 1 belongs to the first stage. A grade that is not a finite number raises ParameterError.

Parameter Type Default Description grade float - Grade of the reader or consensus grade of a text 
describe_level_norm(stat, value, grade)

The reading of a feature of a text by the norms of the stage a grade belongs to: «ниже нормы ступени» (below), «в норме ступени» (between the quartiles, inclusive) or «выше нормы ступени» (above), the bands of ruts.constants.LEVEL_NORM_BANDS. A stage without norms and an undefined value (nan) give None, an unknown feature raises UnknownStatError, and a value that is not a number and a grade that is not a finite number raise ParameterError.

Parameter Type Default Description stat str - Name of a feature of ruts.constants.LEVEL_NORMS_DESC value float - Value of the feature grade float - Grade of the reader or consensus grade of a text CodeResult 
from ruts.datasets import SovChLit
from ruts.readability_stats import describe_level_norm, level_features, level_norms

level_norms(2)["words_per_sent"], level_norms(8)
text = next(SovChLit().get_texts())
features = level_features(text)
{stat: describe_level_norm(stat, value, 1) for stat, value in features.items()}

docs.title: SEO style metrics
docs.text:
StyleStats(source, words_extractor=None, stopwords=None, top_n=10, cliches=None, nausea_stopwords=None)

The style metrics of a text: the SEO metrics of Advego and Text.ru and the markers of the officialese style. The services publish no formulas, so the common definitions are taken. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy.

The SEO metrics are counted on the words of the word extractor, in lower case by default, or on the tokens of a Doc; an extractor passed explicitly is used on the text of a Doc. The markers are counted on the word forms in lower case (forms), whatever the extractor.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, an extractor of another type, a list that is not a list of strings;
  • SourceError - a source without words;
  • ParameterError - a top_n that is not an integer of at least one.

The class extends the StyleStats of the anyTS core with the hooks of Russian, given in the cards of the metrics. The words of a string are extracted by the Russian WordsExtractor and are not lemmatized, so the forms of one word count as different words, as in Advego; to compute by lemmas, pass a WordsExtractor with use_lexemes=True and lowercase=True. The given word lists and the phrases are compared without the letter ё (normalize_yo). The words of a Doc lose their stress marks, and the parts of a hyphenated word that spaCy splits are joined (во-первых is one word). The print_stats table and the error messages are in Russian (STYLE_STATS_DESC and CORE_MESSAGES of ruts.constants).

CodeResult 
from ruts import StyleStats

text = "Ног нет, а хожу, рта нет, а скажу: когда спать, когда вставать, когда работу начинать"
StyleStats(text).print_stats()

docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc - Data source words_extractor WordsExtractor None Word extraction tool; used for a Doc too, on its text stopwords list[str] None Words of water; without them is_water_word decides top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words of the academic nausea and the naturalness by Zipf's law (NAUSEA_TOP_N) cliches list[str] None Cliches; cliches_list of the class by default nausea_stopwords list[str] None Stopwords of the academic nausea; without them is_stopword decides

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description words tuple[str] Words of the SEO metrics forms tuple[str] Word forms in lower case, of the markers

The metrics are properties computed on each access.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
get_stats gives all the metrics. A metric is computed by the function of its card on words or forms with the hooks of the class.

Metric Measures Range Higher means classic_nausea Repetition of the most frequent word 0 and above, grows with the text One word pressed harder academic_nausea Share of the most frequent significant words 0-100 % A narrower vocabulary water Share of the words without content 0-100 % Less content per word spam Share of the repeated words 0-100 % More repetition zipf_naturalness Agreement of the top frequencies with Zipf's law 0-100 %, nan without ranks to compare Closer to a natural text verbal_nouns Share of the verbal nouns among the nouns 0-100 %, nan without nouns A more nominal style compound_prepositions Compound prepositions per 100 words 0-100 More officialese parentheticals Parenthetical expressions per 100 words 0-100 More insertions cliches Cliches per 100 words 0-100 More cliches

The cards give the bands that describe reads, after the norms of Advego, Text.ru, pr-cy and megaindex, in Russian (STYLE_NORMS). The norms are guidelines of the services for website texts of several hundred words: on short texts nausea and spam values are uninformative, and the norms do not apply to fiction. The markers of the officialese have no norms.

The functions check their words: words, stop words, keywords and phrases that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Classic nausea
docs.text:
classic_nausea · Advego

calc_classic_nausea(text)

How much one word is pressed: the square root of the occurrences \(f_1\) of the most frequent word. The value is not corrected for the length of the text, so it grows with the text; no words give 0.

\[ \sqrt{f_1} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words Value Reading [0, 5] the Advego norm (5, 7] at the upper bound of the Advego norm (7, ∞) above the Advego norm

docs.title: Academic nausea
docs.text:
academic_nausea · nausea_words() · Advego

calc_academic_nausea(text, top_n=10, stopwords=None)

The share of the occurrences of the top_n most frequent significant words among all the words, in percent.

\[ 100 \cdot \frac{\sum_{w \in \textrm{top}_n} f_w}{\textrm{Number of words}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words stopwords list[str] None Stop words; without them is_stopword decides

A top_n that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

Value Reading [0, 5) below the Advego norm [5, 15] the Advego norm (15, 100] above the Advego norm 
find_nausea_words(text, top_n=10, stopwords=None)

The top_n most frequent words without the stop words, those the academic nausea counts, with their occurrences: the most frequent first, words of equal frequency in the order of the text. A stop word is a word of stopwords, compared ignoring case and the letter ё, or, without the list, a word of is_stopword.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words stopwords list[str] None Stop words; without them is_stopword decides

A top_n that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

is_stopword(word)

Whether a word is insignificant for the academic nausea by its part of speech in pymorphy3: conjunctions, particles, prepositions, pronominal nouns, interjections and predicatives (CONJ, PRCL, PREP, NPRO, INTJ, PRED), and the words with the grammemes Apro, Prnt, Dmns, Ques - pronominal adjectives, parenthetical words, demonstrative and interrogative adverbs. The sets are ruts.constants.STOPWORD_POS and ruts.constants.STOPWORD_GRAMMEMES.

CodeResult 
from ruts.style_stats import find_nausea_words

find_nausea_words(["кот", "и", "кот", "и", "пес"], top_n=1)

{'кот': 2}

docs.title: Water content
docs.text:
water · Text.ru

calc_water(text, stopwords=None)

The share of the words without content, in percent: the words of stopwords, compared ignoring case and the letter ё, or, without the list, the words of is_water_word. Advego's "water" is a different indicator; it is not implemented here.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words stopwords list[str] None Water words Value Reading [0, 15) natural water content by Text.ru [15, 30] excessive water content by Text.ru (30, 100] high water content by Text.ru 
is_water_word(word)

Whether a word is "water" by its part of speech in pymorphy3, for the water content and the stopwords layer of the highlighting: conjunctions, particles, pronominal nouns and interjections (CONJ, PRCL, NPRO, INTJ; the set ruts.constants.WATER_POS). pymorphy3 tags the parenthetical words конечно and например as conjunctions, so they are water too. Prepositions, pronominal adjectives and predicatives, unlike in is_stopword, are not water.

docs.title: Spam score
docs.text:
spam · Text.ru

calc_spam(text)

The share of the repeated words in percent: every occurrence of a word after the first.

\[ 100 \cdot \left(1 - \frac{\textrm{Number of lexemes}}{\textrm{Number of words}}\right) \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words Value Reading [0, 30) natural text by Text.ru [30, 60] SEO-optimized text by Text.ru (60, 100] spammed text by Text.ru

docs.title: Naturalness by Zipf's law
docs.text:
zipf_naturalness · pr-cy, megaindex

calc_zipf_naturalness(text, top_n=10)

The agreement of the frequencies of the most frequent words with the ideal distribution of Zipf's law, \(f_r = f_1 / r\), where \(f_1\) is the frequency of the most frequent word and \(r\) the rank. The ranks run from 2 to \(R = \min(\textrm{top}_n, V, f_1)\), where \(V\) is the number of lexemes. Negative values are cut to 0. Without ranks to compare - all the words hapaxes, one lexeme or top_n below 2 - the value is nan.

\[ 100 \cdot \left(1 - \frac{1}{R - 1} \sum_{r=2}^{R} \frac{|r \cdot f_r - f_1|}{f_1}\right) \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words

A top_n that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

Value Reading [0, 50) below the pr-cy and megaindex norm [50, 100] the pr-cy and megaindex norm

docs.title: Verbal nouns
docs.text:
verbal_nouns

calc_verbal_nouns(text)

The share of the verbal nouns among the nouns (by the first pymorphy3 analysis), in percent; nan for a text without nouns. A noun is verbal when its lemma ends with a suffix of VERBAL_NOUN_SUFFIXES (-ние, -нье, -тие, -тье, -ствие, -ция) or belongs to VERBAL_NOUN_LEMMAS (производство, руководство, строительство) - the function ruts.utils.is_verbal_noun. The heuristic also catches non-verbal words with the same suffixes (здание). find_verbal_nouns(text) returns the bounds of the words found as slices of the list.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Compound prepositions and cliches
docs.text:
compound_prepositions · cliches

calc_phrase_density(text, phrases)

The occurrences of the phrases of a list per 100 words. The phrases are compared ignoring case and the letter ё, and a phrase starting with an infinitive, alone or after «не», is found in any form of its verb, participles and gerunds included («имело место», «доведено до сведения»). expand_phrases(text, phrases) gives these variants from the text, each with its phrase. StyleStats counts this way, over the word forms (forms), the compound prepositions of COMPOUND_PREPOSITIONS (в целях, в связи с, в рамках, за счет) and the cliches of OFFICIALESE_CLICHES (на сегодняшний день, в настоящее время, иметь место) or of the parameter cliches.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words phrases list[str] - Phrases with words separated by spaces

docs.title: Parenthetical words
docs.text:
parentheticals

calc_parentheticals(text)

The number of parenthetical words per 100 words: the phrases of PARENTHETICALS (таким образом, как правило, в частности, кроме того) and, outside them, the single words with the pymorphy3 grammeme Prnt (конечно, например, впрочем; the function is_parenthetical(word)). find_parentheticals(text) returns the bounds of the words and phrases found as slices of the list.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Keyword density
docs.text:
keyword_density(*keywords) · Text.ru

calc_keyword_density(text, keywords)

The occurrences of every keyword per 100 words. A keyword of several words separated by spaces is a sequence of words whose occurrences may overlap. The words and the keywords are compared in lower case without the letter ё, as the stop words and the phrases, and the keywords of a set come in sorted order.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words keywords list[str] - Keywords or phrases

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
keyword_density(*keywords) gives the density of keywords and phrases in percent (calc_keyword_density with normalize of the class), nausea_words() the most frequent significant words of the academic nausea with their occurrences (find_nausea_words).

markers() returns the markers of the officialese found by metric - verbal_nouns, compound_prepositions, parentheticals, cliches - as the forms write them, in the order of the text.

from ruts import StyleStats

text = "В целях повышения качества в кратчайшие сроки, как правило, проводится проверка"
StyleStats(text).markers()
StyleStats(text, top_n=2).nausea_words()

docs.title: Syntactic statistics
docs.text:
SyntaxStats(source)

The syntactic statistics of a text by its dependency tree (Ivanov, Solnyshkina and Solovyev 2018): the measures of the tree and of the syntactic constructions. The data source is a Doc object of spaCy with a dependency parse and parts of speech. Punctuation, symbols and whitespace are no nodes of the tree, and the distances are counted in positions of words. The units of L2SCA, the prepositional chains and the similarity of sentences are computed on first use, so a subclass whose stats_desc does not name them does not pay for them.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is not a Doc;
  • SourceError - a source without a dependency parse (relations and sentence boundaries), without parts of speech, without lemmas when the class requires them, or without words.

The class extends the SyntaxStats of the anyTS core with the Russian layer. The relations and features are those of the Universal Dependencies annotation of the ru_core_news_sm, ru_core_news_md and ru_core_news_lg models; the quality of the statistics is bounded by the quality of the parse: the small ru_core_news_sm model errs in parts of speech and relations noticeably more often than ru_core_news_lg. The parts of a hyphenated word that spaCy splits are joined (во-первых is one word), and the clauses, participial clauses, negations and split predicates follow the rules of Russian given in the cards of the metrics. ruTS adds its own metrics of genitive chains and adverbial participle clauses. The syntactic markers of officialese are the passive, participial clauses, genitive chains, split predicates and the ratio of nouns to verbs. The print_stats table and the error messages are in Russian (SYNTAX_STATS_DESC and CORE_MESSAGES of ruts.constants).

Ivanov, Solnyshkina and Solovyev tested the features on a corpus of school textbooks: the numbers of coordination chains, participial clauses and noun phrase modifiers correlate with the textbook grade at 0.88-0.93. The cards of the metrics name the original features of the paper and their correlation coefficients with the textbook grade.

import spacy
from ruts import SyntaxStats

nlp = spacy.load("ru_core_news_sm")
text = "Дом, построенный рабочими в прошлом году, был продан. Он сказал, что не придёт, и ушёл, хлопнув дверью."
ss = SyntaxStats(nlp(text))
ss.print_stats()

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Every metric is an attribute of the object, computed when it is created - the units of L2SCA, the prepositional chains and the similarity of sentences on first use - and get_stats gives them all. The measures of a sentence (the longest dependency, the depth, the nodes per leaf) are averaged over the sentences; the constructions are given per sentence.

docs.title: Dependency distance
docs.text:
mean_dependency_distance · std_dependency_distance · max_dependency_distance · p_adjacent_dependencies

calc_dependency_distances(tokens, join_hyphens=False)

The dependency distances (Liu 2008): the distance between a word and its head in positions of words, punctuation left out, in the order of the words. The head of a sentence and a word whose head lies outside the sequence are skipped.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one position

The mean dependency distance grows with sentence length, and the longest one is the best of the tree features at the level of a single sentence. One-word sentences enter none of the metrics of the distances.

CodeResult 
import spacy
from ruts.syntax_stats import calc_dependency_distances

nlp = spacy.load("ru_core_news_sm")
doc = nlp("Повышение эффективности использования ресурсов предприятия обсуждалось на совещании.")
calc_dependency_distances(doc)

[5, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2]

docs.title: Tree depth
docs.text:
tree_depth

calc_tree_depth(tokens, join_hyphens=False)

The depth of the dependency tree: the longest path from the head of a sentence to a leaf, in relations between words; the maximum for several sentences, 0 for a sentence of one word. With join_hyphens a hyphenated word is one word, and the words that hang on any of its parts are one level below it.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

The depth is LONGEST_PATH of the paper of Ivanov et al. (r = 0.84).

docs.title: Leaves and subtrees
docs.text:
leaves_per_sent · subtrees_per_sent · nodes_per_leaf

A leaf is a word without dependent words (count_children), a subtree a word with them. The nodes per leaf are the words of a sentence over its leaves, averaged over the \(S\) sentences.

\[ \frac{1}{S} \sum_{s=1}^{S} \frac{\textrm{Number of words of } s}{\textrm{Number of leaves of } s} \]

The features of the paper: LEAVES_NUMBER (r = 0.84), PATH_NUMBER (r = 0.87) and AVERAGE_PATH (r = 0.84). The distribution of the words by number of dependents, the branching profile, is the attribute c_children.

docs.title: Words before the root
docs.text:
words_before_root · Coh-Metrix

The left embeddedness of Coh-Metrix (SYNLE): the number of the words of a sentence before its root, the main predicate, averaged over the sentences whose root is a word. The root of a sentence with a copula is its nominal part (she is a doctor), as Universal Dependencies has it. In a language with a free word order the measure reads the order as much as the complexity.

docs.title: Valency of the finite verbs
docs.text:
verb_valency

calc_valency(token, join_hyphens=False)

The valency of a token: the number of its dependent words, the relations cc, conj, parataxis and punct left out (anyts.constants.VALENCY_IGNORED_DEPS); with join_hyphens=True a hyphenated dependent counts once, so came in Some-one came has one dependent and not two.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

A finite verb is one of is_finite_verb; the valency is VERBS_DEP of the paper (r = 0.43).

docs.title: Coordination chains
docs.text:
coordination_chains_per_sent · mean_coordination_chain_len

calc_coordination_chains(tokens, join_hyphens=False)

The lengths of the coordination chains, in the order of their first words. A chain is a group of words linked by conj, whichever word each conjunct hangs on: Universal Dependencies attaches every conjunct to the first one (pears → apples, plums → apples), ClearNLP to the previous one (pears → apples, plums → pears); both give one chain of three for apples, pears and plums. A nested coordination (cats and dogs, or birds) and an enumeration split between several heads are one chain too. The length of a chain is the number of its words; a conjunct whose head lies outside the sequence is not linked to it. With join_hyphens a hyphenated word is one conjunct, linked by the conj of any of its parts (member and vice-governor is a chain of two).

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

The number of chains per sentence (SOCHIN_NUMBER, r = 0.93) and their mean length (AVERAGE_SOCHIN_LENGTH, r = 0.87) are the strongest syntactic predictors of textbook complexity.

docs.title: Clauses
docs.text:
clauses_per_sent · mean_clause_len

is_clause_head(token)

Checks whether a word heads a clause: the head of the sentence or a word with ccomp, advcl, acl, csubj, parataxis and their subtypes (anyts.constants.CLAUSE_DEPS), except full participles, adverbial participles and infinitives under a noun («желание уйти»): participial and adverbial participle clauses are counted apart, and a short participle («дом построен») is the predicate of its clause. Under xcomp only an infinitive of is_infinitive_clause heads a clause: a finite form under xcomp is a parse error of the Russian models. An infinitive subject (csubj) of a modal word («нужно уйти», «можно войти», «следует отметить») heads no clause of its own. A parenthetical construction (parataxis) and a coordinated predicate (a conj relation from the clause head) form their own clause only if they can be a predicate (is_predicate): «Он сказал: „Уходи“» and «думала, что он умен» are clauses, while the parentheticals «например», «конечно», «во-первых», which spaCy models also attach as parataxis, are not.

is_infinitive_clause(token)

Checks whether an infinitive under xcomp heads a clause of its own («хочет уйти», «попросил его уйти»): it does not when it makes one predicate with its head (is_infinitive_periphrasis) or stands in a participial or adverbial participle clause («решивший уйти», «желая уйти»).

is_infinitive_periphrasis(token)

Checks whether an infinitive makes one predicate with its head: a modal or phasal verb or a modal word of INFINITIVE_PERIPHRASES («может уйти», «должен прийти», «начал читать», «взялся читать», «перестал курить», «пришлось уйти», «стоит отметить», «нужно уйти», «можно войти», «пора идти»), the short form of a modal adjective of MODAL_SHORT_ADJECTIVES («готов уйти», «рад помочь») or the hortative «давай», «давайте» of HORTATIVE_WORDS without a negation («давайте играть», but not «не давайте детям играть»).

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token

docs.title: Subordinate clauses
docs.text:
subordinate_clauses_per_sent · p_complex_sents

is_subordinate_clause_head(token)

Checks whether a word heads a subordinate clause: a clause head (is_clause_head) with ccomp, advcl, acl, csubj and their subtypes, or a coordinated predicate of a subordinate clause.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token

The features of the paper: PODCHIN_RATE (r = 0.64), the subordinate clauses per sentence, and PODCHIN_NUMBER (r = 0.62), the share of the sentences with at least one subordinate clause.

docs.title: Infinitive clauses
docs.text:
infinitive_clauses_per_sent

is_infinitive_clause_head(token)

Checks whether a word heads an infinitive clause under a verb: an infinitive under xcomp that heads a clause of its own (is_infinitive_clause: «хочет уйти», «попросил его уйти»), or an infinitive coordinated with it. Such a clause is counted apart from the subordinate ones, as grammars of many languages take it for a part of a simple sentence.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token CodeResult 
import spacy
from ruts.syntax_stats import is_clause_head, is_infinitive_clause_head, is_subordinate_clause_head

nlp = spacy.load("ru_core_news_sm")
doc = nlp("Он хочет уйти, но может остаться, если его попросят.")
[token.text for token in doc if is_clause_head(token)]
[token.text for token in doc if is_subordinate_clause_head(token)]
[token.text for token in doc if is_infinitive_clause_head(token)]

['хочет', 'уйти', 'может', 'попросят']
['попросят']
['уйти']

docs.title: Production units of L2SCA
docs.text:
t_units_per_sent · mean_t_unit_len · clauses_per_t_unit · p_complex_t_units · verb_phrases_per_t_unit · coordinate_phrases_per_clause · complex_nominals_per_clause · Lu 2010

The indices of the L2 Syntactic Complexity Analyzer (L2SCA) that the other metrics do not give, on Universal Dependencies. MLC and C/S are mean_clause_len and clauses_per_sent; MLS and DC/C come from the counts, n_words / n_sents and n_subordinate_clauses / n_clauses.

  • A T-unit is a main clause with the clauses that depend on it: the head of a sentence and every clause head joined to it through conj or parataxis (anyts.constants.MAIN_CLAUSE_DEPS), so I came, and he left holds two; a conjunct of a subordinate clause is none. A conjunct without a subject of its own (I came and left) is a predicate sharing the T-unit of the clause it is coordinated to, as in L2SCA, unless its person, number or gender - those of its auxiliary or copula, its own without one - differ from those of that clause: in a language that drops its subjects the ending names another one (llegamos al puerto y nos esperabas). An existential there (expl of ClearNLP) is a subject. A T-unit is complex with a subordinate clause (is_subordinate_clause_head) whose nearest T-unit above is it.
  • A verb phrase is a predicate (is_predicate) that is no auxiliary or copula: a verb, an auxiliary used as a predicate (there is trouble), a word with a subject or a copula; an infinitive that makes one predicate with its head (is_infinitive_periphrasis), and its infinitive conjunct, is part of the verb phrase of the head.
  • A coordinate phrase is a coordination with a conjunct that is no clause head (the man and the woman, is big and nice) or a predicate without a subject of its own (came and left), counted once by its first conjunct; a coordination of clauses with their own subjects counts as clauses.
  • The clauses are those of is_clause_head, as in the other metrics: a predicate sharing a subject and an infinitive clause count as clauses, while L2SCA counts finite clauses with a subject, so C/T, C/S and CN/C run higher and MLC lower than in L2SCA.
  • A complex nominal is a noun with a modifier of anyts.constants.COMPLEX_NOMINAL_DEPS (an adjective, a complement, a relative or participial clause, an apposition, a possessive), or a nominal clause, a clause head of anyts.constants.NOMINAL_CLAUSE_DEPS or a conjunct of one.
\[ \textrm{MLT} = \frac{\textrm{Words}}{\textrm{T-units}}, \quad \textrm{C/T} = \frac{\textrm{Clauses}}{\textrm{T-units}}, \quad \textrm{CT/T} = \frac{\textrm{Complex T-units}}{\textrm{T-units}}, \quad \textrm{CN/C} = \frac{\textrm{Complex nominals}}{\textrm{Clauses}} \]

docs.title: Modifiers of a noun
docs.text:
modifiers_per_noun

count_noun_modifiers(token, join_hyphens=False)

Counts the modifiers of a noun phrase: the dependents with the relations amod, det, nmod, nummod, acl and their subtypes (anyts.constants.NOUN_MODIFIER_DEPS); conj and appos are no modifiers.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

The number of modifiers is NOUNS_DEP of the paper (r = 0.88).

docs.title: Prepositional chains
docs.text:
prep_chains_per_sent · max_prep_chain_len · Profiling-UD

A prepositional chain is two or more nested complements with a preposition, each hanging on the previous one: on the mat of the house of the mayor (length 3). The links are the words of the hook is_prep_complement, and the chains and their lengths are those of calc_modifier_chains; a chain may start at a complement of a verb (obl) or at a prepositional predicate with a copula (was in the house of the mayor), but not at a conjunct of a complement (in Madrid and in the centre of the city), and a predicate of a relative clause (the house that was by the river) is no link of the chain of its noun. The chains read Universal Dependencies alone: ClearNLP heads a phrase by its preposition (prep, pobj), so its parses give no chains.

The genitive chains of ruTS (genitive_chains_per_sent) are counted apart: their links are prepositionless genitive modifiers («повышение эффективности использования ресурсов»), and those of a prepositional chain are complements with a preposition.

docs.title: Genitive chains
docs.text:
genitive_chains_per_sent · max_genitive_chain_len

calc_genitive_chains(tokens)

The lengths of the genitive chains in the order of the words: the chains of calc_modifier_chains whose modifiers are prepositionless genitive modifiers; «повышение эффективности использования ресурсов» is a chain of length 3.

is_genitive_modifier(token)

Checks whether a word is a prepositionless genitive modifier: a word with the nmod relation in the genitive case without a dependent preposition (case), «дом отца», but not «дом у дороги».

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens (calc_genitive_chains) token Token - Token (is_genitive_modifier) CodeResult 
import spacy
from ruts.syntax_stats import calc_genitive_chains

nlp = spacy.load("ru_core_news_sm")
calc_genitive_chains(
    nlp("Повышение эффективности использования ресурсов предприятия обсуждалось на совещании.")
)

[4]

docs.title: Participial clauses
docs.text:
participle_clauses_per_sent · mean_participle_clause_len

The clauses headed by the words of the hook is_participle_clause; the length of a clause is the number of the words in the subtree of its head (subtree_len).

is_participle_clause(token)

Checks whether a word heads a participial clause: a full participle (is_participle) with at least one dependent word, the coordination and parenthetical relations left out. Short participles («дом построен») are predicates rather than modifiers and head no clauses. The features of the paper are PRICH_RATE (r = 0.91) and PRICH_V.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token

docs.title: Adverbial participle clauses
docs.text:
converb_clauses_per_sent · mean_converb_clause_len

is_converb_clause(token)

Checks whether a word heads an adverbial participle clause: an adverbial participle (is_converb) with at least one dependent word, the coordination and parenthetical relations left out. The length of a clause is the number of the words in the subtree of the adverbial participle (subtree_len). The features of the paper are DEEPRICH_RATE (r = 0.44) and DEEPRICH_V.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token

docs.title: Passive
docs.text:
p_passive · p_agentless_passive

is_passive(token, join_hyphens=False)

Checks whether a word is a passive verb form: a verb with Voice=Pass or a dependent nsubj:pass, csubj:pass, aux:pass, or nsubjpass, csubjpass, auxpass of ClearNLP (PASSIVE_DEPS).

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

A value that is not a Token raises SourceTypeError.

has_agent(token, join_hyphens=False)

Checks whether a word has an agent: a dependent obl:agent, or agent of ClearNLP (AGENT_DEPS). The arguments and the error are those of is_passive.

is_agentless(token, join_hyphens=False)

Checks whether a word is a passive form (is_passive) without an agent (has_agent), with the same arguments and error.

In Russian the passive is a passive participle or the reflexive passive («обсуждалось»), and an agentless form is «дом построен», but not «дом построен рабочими».

docs.title: Infinitives, negations and split predicates
docs.text:
infinitives_per_sent · negations_per_sent · split_predicates_per_sent

The infinitives (is_infinitive of anyts.utils), the words of negation of the hook is_negation and the split predicates of the hook find_split_predicates, per sentence.

is_negation(token)

Checks whether a word is a negative particle: a particle (PART) with the feature Polarity=Neg or the particle «не», «ни» (NEGATION_PARTICLES); the conjunction «ни» of «ни… ни» is no negation. The negations are NEG of the paper (r = 0.70).

find_split_predicates(tokens)

is_light_verb(token)

is_reflexive(token)

is_split_predicate_noun(token, verb=None)

The split predicates, a marker of officialese, are pairs of a verb and a noun in the order of the words: a light verb (is_light_verb) with a lemma of LIGHT_VERBS (for example: осуществлять, производить, проводить, вести, обеспечивать, оказывать, принимать, иметь and their reflexive passives проводиться, приниматься, вестись) with a nominal part (is_split_predicate_noun), a noun with a verbal lemma (ruts.utils.is_verbal_noun) or a lemma of SPLIT_PREDICATE_NOUNS (for example: роль, работа, помощь, мера) with a verb verb of its own phrase (оказать помощь, принять меры, but not получить работу): осуществлять проверку, оказать помощь, принято решение, проверка проводится. At most one nominal part is taken per verb in the order of preference obj, nsubj:pass, nsubj (only for a reflexive or passive verb, is_reflexive), iobj, nmod, obl; prepositional adjuncts and the passive agent (obl:agent, instrumental obl) are not counted. The verb lemma is taken from the pymorphy3 analysis twice: with the part of speech of the token (get_lemma) and as a verb (ruts.utils.lemmatize).

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens (find_split_predicates) verb Token None Light verb (is_split_predicate_noun); without it the phrase is not checked CodeResult 
import spacy
from ruts.syntax_stats import find_split_predicates, is_negation

nlp = spacy.load("ru_core_news_sm")
doc = nlp("Проверка проводится ежегодно, но решение не принято.")
find_split_predicates(doc)
[token.text for token in doc if is_negation(token)]

[(проводится, Проверка), (принято, решение)]
['не']

docs.title: Order of the subjects and the objects
docs.text:
p_preverbal_subjects · p_preverbal_objects · Profiling-UD

The order of the subjects and of the direct objects in the manner of Profiling-UD: the shares of those before their head, the predicate. Only the nominal ones (NOUN, PROPN) count: the place of a pronoun, such as a clitic object, is set by the grammar. A subject is a word of nsubj (anyts.constants.NOMINAL_SUBJECT_DEPS), an object one of obj (anyts.constants.OBJECT_DEPS), with the relations of ClearNLP and the subtypes.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Nominal subjects before their head}}{\textrm{Nominal subjects}}, \quad \frac{\textrm{Nominal objects before their head}}{\textrm{Nominal objects}} \]

docs.title: Similarity of adjacent sentences
docs.text:
pos_edit_distance · syntax_similarity · Coh-Metrix

How alike the structures of two adjacent sentences are, averaged over the \(S - 1\) pairs. pos_edit_distance is the edit distance of the parts of speech \(P_s\) of the words of the sentences (SYNMEDpos of Coh-Metrix) over the length \(n\) of the longer sentence of the pair, calc_edit_distance. syntax_similarity is the similarity of the multisets of the dependency triples \(T\) of the two sentences (dependency_triples, calc_multiset_similarity), in the manner of SYNSTRUT of Coh-Metrix, which compares the nodes of phrase-structure trees.

\[ \frac{1}{S - 1} \sum_{s=1}^{S-1} \frac{\textrm{lev}(P_s, P_{s+1})}{\max(n_s, n_{s+1})}, \quad \frac{1}{S - 1} \sum_{s=1}^{S-1} \frac{|T_s \cap T_{s+1}|}{|T_s \cup T_{s+1}|} \]

docs.title: Ratio of the nouns to the verbs
docs.text:
noun_verb_ratio

The number of the nouns n_nouns to the number of the verb forms n_verbs.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of nouns}}{\textrm{Number of verb forms}} \]

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
The methods get_stats, to_dataframe, print_stats and describe are those of the statistics interface of the anyTS core; the syntactic statistics have no scales, so describe gives None for the statistics of get_stats.

The functions work with spaCy tokens: the calc_* and find_* functions and dependency_triples take a sequence of tokens (Doc, Span or a list), the is_* and count_* functions a single token, and calc_edit_distance and calc_multiset_similarity lists of the items of sentences; the words of a sequence are the tokens of is_word. The functions of the dependency tree come from the core, those of the Russian constructions are ruTS's own. Relation subtypes (acl:relcl, nsubj:pass, nummod:gov) are counted by the base relation (base_dep) where noted.

docs.title: Words of a sequence
docs.text:
get_words(tokens, join_hyphens=False)

The words of a sequence of tokens in their order; with join_hyphens=True a word the tokenizer split at its hyphens is one word, given by its part that holds its relation, as with the dependents of get_children (governor in He is vice-governor), or by its first part when a hyphen holds it.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

docs.title: Hyphenated words
docs.text:
A tokenizer may split a word at its hyphens (well-known into well, -, known), and a parser then hangs every part on its own head. With join_hyphens=True the functions of the tree take a word whose parts anyts.utils.joins_previous joins for one word with its hyphens. A word holding the head of the sentence has no head; the head of another one is that of its part hanging outside it, the nearest to the root (a word rather than a hyphen when equal). The dependents of a word are the words whose head hangs on one of its tokens, each given by that part (or by its first part when it hangs by a hyphen); its subtree is the word and the words that hang on it, directly or through punctuation. So every word has one dependency and is the dependent of one word.

SyntaxStats and the functions of the Russian constructions always join hyphenated words. The functions of the core, is_predicate, count_noun_modifiers, is_passive, has_agent and is_agentless included, take join_hyphens=False by default: they give the values of SyntaxStats with join_hyphens=True.

docs.title: Head of a sentence
docs.text:
is_root(token)

Checks whether a token is the head of its sentence: its head is the token itself.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token

docs.title: Base relation
docs.text:
base_dep(token)

The relation of a token without its subtype, which Universal Dependencies separates by a colon: nsubj:pass gives nsubj, expl:pass gives expl.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token

docs.title: Dependent words
docs.text:
get_children(token, join_hyphens=False)

The dependent words of a token, punctuation and whitespace left out; with join_hyphens=True, the dependents of the whole hyphenated word the token belongs to.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word 
count_children(token, join_hyphens=False)

The number of the dependent words of a token; the arguments are those of get_children.

subtree_len(token, join_hyphens=False)

The number of words in the subtree of a token: the token itself and all of its direct and indirect dependents; the arguments are those of get_children.

docs.title: Verb forms
docs.text:
is_finite_verb(token)

Checks whether a token is a finite verb: the part of speech VERB with VerbForm=Fin, so a finite auxiliary (AUX) is not one.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token 
is_infinitive(token)

Checks whether a token is an infinitive, VerbForm=Inf whatever its part of speech.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token 
is_participle(token)

is_converb(token)

is_participle checks whether a token is a full participle (VerbForm=Part without Variant=Short and StyleVariant=Short), is_converb whether it is an adverbial participle (VerbForm=Conv); the argument is the same token.

docs.title: Predicate of a clause
docs.text:
is_predicate(token, join_hyphens=False)

Checks whether a word can be the predicate of its clause: a verb (VERB, AUX), a word with a subject of its own (nsubj, csubj and their subtypes, anyts.constants.SUBJECT_DEPS) or with a copula (cop), so the nominal predicate of he is tall and of a language that drops the subject passes and a parenthetical word does not.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

A value that is not a Token raises SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Chains of modifiers
docs.text:
calc_modifier_chains(tokens, is_modifier, join_hyphens=False)

The lengths of the chains of nested modifiers, in the order of the words. A chain is two or more modifiers each hanging on the previous one, such as the complements of the increase of the efficiency of the use of resources (length 3); the check is_modifier of a language says what a modifier is (a complement with a preposition, a noun in the genitive). A chain starts at a modifier whose head is none, and its length is the number of modifiers in its longest branch. The links are those of get_children: punctuation is no link, and with join_hyphens a hyphenated word is one link.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens is_modifier Callable[[Token], bool] - Whether a word is a modifier of the chain join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

A check that is not callable raises SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Complements with a preposition
docs.text:
is_prep_complement(token, join_hyphens=False)

Checks whether a word is a complement with a preposition: a word with the relation nmod or obl or a subtype of them (anyts.constants.PREP_COMPLEMENT_DEPS), or a predicate with a copula out of a relative clause (acl), that has a dependent of the relation case that is an adposition (ADP) or begins one of several words (fixed: in front of). A noun in a case without a preposition and a possessive marker are none.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

A value that is not a Token raises SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Dependency triples
docs.text:
dependency_triples(tokens, join_hyphens=False)

The dependency triples of the words of a sentence (get_words), in their order: the part of speech of the head of a word - the nearest word above it through punctuation - its relation without a subtype (base_dep) and its own part of speech, such as ("NOUN", "amod", "ADJ") for a red house. The head of the sentence, and a word with no word above it, give an empty head and the relation root, whatever its label.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

Tokens that are not a Doc, a Span or a list of Token objects raise SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Edit distance and multiset similarity
docs.text:
calc_edit_distance(sents)

The mean edit distance of the items of adjacent sentences: the Levenshtein distance of every two - the fewest insertions, deletions and substitutions that turn one into the other - over the number of the items of the longer one, 0 for the same sequences and 1 for ones with no item in common; nan for fewer than two sentences.

Parameter Type Default Description sents list[list] - Items of every sentence, such as its parts of speech

Sentences that are not a list of lists, or items that cannot be hashed, raise SourceTypeError.

calc_multiset_similarity(sents)

The mean similarity of the multisets of the items of adjacent sentences: the weighted Jaccard similarity of every two - the items they share, each as many times as the sentence with fewer of them has it, over the items of both, each as many times as the sentence with more of them has it - 1 for the same multisets and for two empty ones, 0 for disjoint ones; nan for fewer than two sentences. A mapping is read by its keys, as a set.

Parameter Type Default Description sents list[list] - Items of every sentence, such as its dependency triples

Sentences that are not a list of collections, or items that cannot be hashed, raise SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Helper functions
docs.text:
is_word(token)

Checks whether a token is a word: not whitespace and not a token of is_punctuation, so symbols like %, €, + and invisible characters are no words either. The words of iter_doc_tokens and the nodes of the dependency tree of the syntactic statistics are such tokens.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token 
has_feature(token, field, value)

Checks whether a token carries a morphological feature with a given value: has_feature(token, "VerbForm", "Fin").

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token field str - Name of the feature value str - Value of the feature 
get_lemma(token)

The lemma of a token in lower case by the pymorphy3 analysis with the part of speech of the token (ruts.utils.lemmatize), not token.lemma_.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token

docs.title: Formulas of other languages
docs.text:
UnadaptedReadabilityStats(source, sents_extractor=None, words_extractor=None)

Readability formulas made for English, German or Italian, computed from the basic statistics of a text with the coefficients they were published with (Linsear Write in the form of textstat), without a calibration for its language. Their values compare texts of one language with each other; they are no grade levels of another language. A word without syllables (a number, a preposition of one consonant) counts as monosyllabic in FORCAST and the Wiener Sachtextformeln and as easy in Linsear Write, as in textstat. The data source is a text, a Doc object of spaCy or a ready BasicStats object, as for ReadabilityStats.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string, a Doc nor a BasicStats object, basic statistics of another class, an extractor of another type, a string or a Doc for a class without basic_stats_class;
  • SourceError - a source without words or without sentences.

The class extends the UnadaptedReadabilityStats of the anyTS core with the basic statistics of ruTS, which count the syllables and the letters of Russian words and take the Russian SentsExtractor and WordsExtractor by default. The print_stats table and the error messages are in Russian (UNADAPTED_READABILITY_STATS_DESC and CORE_MESSAGES of ruts.constants).

The formulas are not calibrated for Russian. Their values serve to compare Russian texts with each other and with the results of these formulas in other tools, but they give no grade of the Russian school: on the first-grade texts of the TextsByGrade dataset the median FORCAST is 14.9, the Powers-Sumner-Kearl grade 8.2 and the Wiener Sachtextformel 1 9.4. These formulas therefore have no reading scales, describe gives None for them, and they do not enter the consensus grade. The formulas with coefficients for Russian are in ReadabilityStats.

CodeResult 
from ruts import UnadaptedReadabilityStats

text = "Ног нет, а хожу, рта нет, а скажу: когда спать, когда вставать, когда работу начинать"
urs = UnadaptedReadabilityStats(text)
urs.print_stats()
