docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc / BasicStats - Data source sents_extractor SentsExtractor None Sentence extraction tool, not used for ready basic statistics words_extractor WordsExtractor None Word extraction tool, not used for ready basic statistics

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description bs BasicStats Basic statistics of the text

Ready basic statistics can be taken from a ReadabilityStats object, so as not to compute them again:

CodeResult 
from ruts import ReadabilityStats

rs = ReadabilityStats(text)
urs = UnadaptedReadabilityStats(rs.bs)
urs.bs is rs.bs, urs.forcast

(True, 13.0)

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Every metric is a property of the object, computed on each access from bs, and get_stats gives them all. A hard word has complex_syl_factor syllables or more (3), a long word long_word_letter_factor letters or more (7).

Metric Language and readers Range Higher means forcast English technical texts, a grade 5-20 Harder linsear_write English, a grade -1 and above Harder powers_sumner_kearl English primary school texts, a grade Any Harder eflaw English for foreign learners 1 and above Harder wiener_sachtextformel_1 ... wiener_sachtextformel_4 German non-fiction, a grade from 4 to 15 Any Harder dickes_steiwer German, without syllables Any Easier gulpease Italian, by letters 0-100 for most texts Easier fucks German, syllables per sentence 0 and above Harder strain_index English 0 and above Harder elf English texts read aloud 0 and above Harder wheeler_smith English primary school texts 0 and above Harder

Here ASL is the mean number of words per sentence, ASW the mean number of syllables per word. The functions of the formulas are imported from ruts.unadapted_readability_stats and compute a value from counts:

CodeResult 
from ruts.unadapted_readability_stats import calc_forcast, calc_gulpease

calc_forcast(n_monosyllable_words=30, n_words=150)
calc_gulpease(n_letters=550, n_words=100, n_sents=8)

17.0
58.0

docs.title: FORCAST
docs.text:
forcast · Caylor et al., 1973

calc_forcast(n_monosyllable_words, n_words)

The grade of Caylor et al. (1973) for technical texts: 20 minus a tenth of the monosyllabic words per 150 words, from 5 (every word monosyllabic) to 20; nan without words.

\[ \textrm{FORCAST} = 20 - \frac{150 \times \textrm{Monosyllabic words}}{10 \times \textrm{Words}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_monosyllable_words int - Number of monosyllabic words n_words int - Number of words

A count that is not an integer or is negative, and more monosyllabic words than words, raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Linsear Write
docs.text:
linsear_write

calc_linsear_write(n_easy_words, n_hard_words, n_sents)

The grade of Linsear Write in the form of textstat; the Lensear Write Formula of O'Hayre (1966) is another one, of the monosyllabic words and the sentences of a sample of 100 words. An easy word, of at most two syllables, weighs 1 and a hard one 3; their sum per sentence \(r\) is halved above 20, and otherwise loses 2 before it is halved. It is computed over the whole text rather than a sample of 100 words; nan without sentences.

\[ r = \frac{\textrm{Easy words} + 3 \times \textrm{Hard words}}{\textrm{Sentences}}, \quad \textrm{LW} = \begin{cases} r / 2 & r > 20 \\ (r - 2) / 2 & r \le 20 \end{cases} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_easy_words int - Number of the words of one or two syllables n_hard_words int - Number of the words of three syllables or more n_sents int - Number of sentences

A count that is not an integer or is negative raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Powers-Sumner-Kearl grade
docs.text:
powers_sumner_kearl · Powers et al., 1958

calc_powers_sumner_kearl(n_syllables, n_words, n_sents)

The recalculation of the Flesch formula by Powers, Sumner and Kearl (1958) as a grade, for primary school texts; nan without words or sentences.

\[ \textrm{PSK} = 0.0778 \times \textrm{ASL} + 4.55 \times \textrm{ASW} - 2.2029 \] Parameter Type Default Description n_syllables int - Number of syllables n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences

A count that is not an integer or is negative raises ParameterError.

docs.title: McAlpine EFLAW
docs.text:
eflaw · McAlpine, 2005

calc_eflaw(n_mini_words, n_words, n_sents)

The score of McAlpine (2005) for readers of English as a foreign language: the words and the mini words, of one to three letters (mini_word_letters), per sentence; 20 and below is very easy, 30 and above confusing. nan without sentences.

\[ \textrm{EFLAW} = \frac{\textrm{Words} + \textrm{Mini words}}{\textrm{Sentences}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_mini_words int - Number of the words of one to three letters n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences

A count that is not an integer or is negative raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Wiener Sachtextformel
docs.text:
wiener_sachtextformel_1 · wiener_sachtextformel_2 · wiener_sachtextformel_3 · wiener_sachtextformel_4 · Bamberger and Vanecek, 1984

calc_wiener_sachtextformel(n_complex, n_long_words, n_monosyllable_words, n_words, n_sents, variant=1)

The four formulas of Bamberger and Vanecek (1984) for German non-fiction, a grade from 4 to 15, over the percentages of the words of three syllables or more (MS), of more than six letters (IW) and of one syllable (ES) and the mean sentence length (SL); nan without words or sentences. A variant that is not an integer from 1 to 4 raises ParameterError.

\[ \begin{aligned} \textrm{WSTF}_1 &= 0.1935 \cdot \textrm{MS} + 0.1672 \cdot \textrm{SL} + 0.1297 \cdot \textrm{IW} - 0.0327 \cdot \textrm{ES} - 0.875 \\ \textrm{WSTF}_2 &= 0.2007 \cdot \textrm{MS} + 0.1682 \cdot \textrm{SL} + 0.1373 \cdot \textrm{IW} - 2.779 \\ \textrm{WSTF}_3 &= 0.2963 \cdot \textrm{MS} + 0.1905 \cdot \textrm{SL} - 1.1144 \\ \textrm{WSTF}_4 &= 0.2744 \cdot \textrm{MS} + 0.2656 \cdot \textrm{SL} - 1.693 \end{aligned} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_complex int - Number of the words of three syllables or more n_long_words int - Number of the words of more than six letters n_monosyllable_words int - Number of monosyllabic words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences variant int 1 Variant of the formula, from 1 to 4

A count that is not an integer or is negative raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Dickes-Steiwer index
docs.text:
dickes_steiwer · Dickes and Steiwer, 1977

calc_dickes_steiwer(n_letters, n_words, n_sents, n_types)

The short formula of Dickes and Steiwer (1977) for German, as Bamberger and Vanecek (1984) give it, over the letters per word, the words per sentence and the type-token ratio, without syllables; higher is easier. nan without words or sentences.

\[ \textrm{DS} = 235.95993 - 73.021 \ln\left(\frac{\textrm{Letters}}{\textrm{Words}} + 1\right) - 12.56438 \ln\left(\frac{\textrm{Words}}{\textrm{Sentences}} + 1\right) - 50.03293 \cdot \textrm{TTR} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_letters int - Number of the letters of the words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences n_types int - Number of the distinct words

A count that is not an integer or is negative raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Gulpease index
docs.text:
gulpease · Lucisano and Piemontese, 1988

calc_gulpease(n_letters, n_words, n_sents)

The index of Lucisano and Piemontese (1988) for Italian, by letters rather than syllables: about 0 for the hardest texts and 100 for the easiest, beyond them for extreme ones; below 80 a text is hard for a reader of primary school, below 40 for a reader with a secondary education. nan without words.

\[ \textrm{Gulpease} = 89 + \frac{300 \times \textrm{Sentences} - 10 \times \textrm{Letters}}{\textrm{Words}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_letters int - Number of the letters of the words n_words int - Number of words n_sents int - Number of sentences

A count that is not an integer or is negative raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Fucks index
docs.text:
fucks · Fucks, 1955

calc_fucks(n_syllables, n_sents)

The style characteristic of Fucks (1955): the mean word length in syllables times the mean sentence length in words, the syllables per sentence; nan without sentences.

\[ \textrm{Fucks} = \textrm{ASW} \times \textrm{ASL} = \frac{\textrm{Syllables}}{\textrm{Sentences}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_syllables int - Number of syllables n_sents int - Number of sentences

A count that is not an integer or is negative raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Strain index
docs.text:
strain_index · Nathaniel, 2009

calc_strain_index(n_syllables, n_sents)

The index of Nathaniel (2009): the syllables of three sentences over 10, here those of three sentences on average over the whole text; nan without sentences.

\[ \textrm{Strain} = \frac{3 \times \textrm{Syllables}}{10 \times \textrm{Sentences}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_syllables int - Number of syllables n_sents int - Number of sentences

A count that is not an integer or is negative raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Easy listening formula
docs.text:
elf · Fang, 1966

calc_elf(n_syllables, n_syllabic_words, n_sents)

The formula of Fang (1966) for texts read aloud: the syllables above one per word, per sentence, a word without syllables (a number) adding none; 12 and below is easy to listen to. nan without sentences.

\[ \textrm{ELF} = \frac{\textrm{Syllables} - \textrm{Words of one syllable or more}}{\textrm{Sentences}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_syllables int - Number of syllables n_syllabic_words int - Number of the words of one syllable or more n_sents int - Number of sentences

A count that is not an integer or is negative raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Wheeler-Smith index
docs.text:
wheeler_smith · Wheeler and Smith, 1954

calc_wheeler_smith(n_polysyllable_words, n_sents)

The index of Wheeler and Smith (1954) for primary school texts: the mean sentence length times the share of the words of two syllables or more, times 10, which makes 10 such words per sentence; it reads sentences where the original reads units ended by any final mark. nan without sentences.

\[ \textrm{WS} = 10 \times \textrm{ASL} \times \frac{\textrm{Words of two syllables or more}}{\textrm{Words}} \] Parameter Type Default Description n_polysyllable_words int - Number of the words of two syllables or more n_sents int - Number of sentences

A count that is not an integer or is negative raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Verse statistics
docs.text:
VerseStats(source, stress_dict=None)

The verse statistics of a text: stresses, the meter and the number of feet, pyrrhics and the stress profile, rhyme schemes, line ending types and stanzas. The data source is a text with line breaks or a Doc object of the spaCy library; the statistics are computed when the object is created.

The text is split into lines and stanzas (by blank lines), the words are accented with the StressDict dictionary, then a syllabo-tonic meter is fitted with the algorithm of Barakhnin, Kozhemyakina and Kuznetsova and the remaining stress ambiguity is resolved; rhymes are found by the phonetic key of the line ending (algorithm). A stress mark in the text overrides the dictionary, while the marks and soft hyphens do not get into the lines; a proclitic stressed by a mark takes the stress of the word after it separated by a space - на́ сердце. A stress mark is taken as the author's and is not moved to an ictus, so a text after the accentuate function, where the marks are placed by the dictionary without a meter, gives other values than the same text without marks.

The class is built on the Stats statistics interface of the anyTS core. The stress dictionary is downloaded once: StressDict().download() (10 MB). A text with letters but without Russian words (Latin script) gives empty statistics - n_lines 0, meter None, shares nan.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, a stress dictionary of another type;
  • SourceError - a source without words (empty, digits and punctuation only);
  • DatasetNotFoundError - the stress dictionary is not downloaded, with a hint on how to download it.
CodeResult 
from ruts import VerseStats
from ruts.datasets import StressDict

StressDict().download()
text = """Мой дядя самых честных правил,
Когда не в шутку занемог,
Он уважать себя заставил
И лучше выдумать не мог."""
vs = VerseStats(text)
vs.print_stats()

docs.title: Meter and feet
docs.text:
meter · n_feet · c_feet · p_deviations · Barakhnin et al., 2019

detect_meter(text, stress_dict=None)

The meter of a poem by the algorithm: ямб (iamb), хорей (trochee), дактиль (dactyl), амфибрахий (amphibrach), анапест (anapest) or None if no syllabo-tonic meter fits - this filters out dolnik, accentual verse, syllabic verse, free verse and prose. The number of feet of a line is the number of its ictuses: n_feet is the prevailing number of feet, c_feet the distribution of the lines by the number of feet. p_deviations is the share of the stresses of polysyllabic words left on weak positions after the fitting (deviations from the meter).

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text of the poem stress_dict StressDict None Stress dictionary; StressDict() by default

The errors are those of VerseStats.

CodeResult 
from ruts.verse_stats import detect_meter

lermontov = """Тучки небесные, вечные странники!
Степью лазурною, цепью жемчужною
Мчитесь вы, будто как я же, изгнанники,
С милого севера в сторону южную.

Кто же вас гонит: судьбы ли решение?
Зависть ли тайная? злоба ль открытая?
Или на вас тяготит преступление?
Или друзей клевета ядовитая?"""

blok = """Девушка пела в церковном хоре
О всех усталых в чужом краю,
О всех кораблях, ушедших в море,
О всех, забывших радость свою."""

detect_meter(lermontov), detect_meter(blok)

p_masculine · p_feminine · p_dactylic · c_clausulas

The type of the ending (clausula) of a line by the number of syllables after the last stress: masculine - the stress on the last syllable, feminine - one syllable after the stress, dactylic - two, hyperdactylic - three or more (VERSE_CLAUSULAS, as stress_type of a word). c_clausulas is the distribution of the lines by type; the shares are taken over the lines whose last word has a known stress.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
accentuate() returns the text with stresses placed: an acute accent (U+0301) is put after the stressed vowel of every stressed word, while unstressed words (clitics, monosyllables off the ictus) and words without a found stress stay unmarked. Only the lines with words get into the text (as in lines), and stanzas are separated by a blank line. Unlike the accentuate function, the stresses are fitted to the meter.

docs.title: Algorithm
docs.text:
Stresses and the meter are determined with the algorithm of Barakhnin, Kozhemyakina and Kuznetsova (CEUR 2019):

  1. Dictionary stresses. The stressed syllable of every word is looked up: by the letter ё, the only syllable of a monosyllable, otherwise the StressDict dictionary with the STRESS_CORRECTIONS fixes (erroneous and mobile dictionary stresses collected from frequent PoetryCorpus forms and the RIFMA annotation: ещё, себе́, пе́ред, зо́лото, леса́х, спеши́т, земли́). Hyphenated compounds are looked up as a whole, then by parts; poetic contractions (желанье - желание) and converbs (забыв - забывший) are looked up by the full form.
  2. Meter fitting. Each of the five meters has its own strong positions - ictuses: iamb cC, trochee Cc, dactyl Ccc, amphibrach cCc, anapest ccC (VERSE_METERS). The meter with the fewest dictionary stresses of polysyllabic words on weak positions wins, ties are broken by the number of stressed ictuses. A stress in the anacrusis - on the syllables before the first ictus of the line - does not count as a violation: it is common in ternary meters (Ста́ли дни холоднее).
  3. Disambiguation. Monosyllabic prepositions, conjunctions and particles (VERSE_PROCLITICS) are unstressed, other monosyllables are stressed only on an ictus; polysyllabic function words (VERSE_WEAK_WORDS: или, чтобы, перед, через, после) are stressed if the dictionary stress falls on an ictus. A dictionary stress of a polysyllabic word on a weak position is moved to the ictus if the word contains exactly one ictus, it is the only such word in the line or all of them are disyllabic (forms with mobile stress: воды́ - во́ды, реки́ - ре́ки), and no violations remain in the line after the move - otherwise the line is considered non-metrical; a stress by the letter ё and a stress in the anacrusis are never moved. A word without a dictionary stress gets its only ictus; with several ictuses, the stress of the last word of a line is chosen by rhyme with the neighbouring lines, otherwise the last ictus.
  4. Check. The meter is not determined if after fitting more than a tenth of the polysyllabic word stresses (VERSE_MAX_DEVIATIONS) remain on weak positions, or if more than 15% of the dictionary stresses of polysyllabic words had to be moved to an ictus (VERSE_MAX_MOVED) with four or more moves (VERSE_MIN_MOVED) - the text is dolnik, accentual verse, syllabic verse, free verse or prose: there the fitting moves the stresses of arbitrary disyllabic words rather than of mobile-stress forms, and without the second threshold a dolnik or accentual verse with frequent disyllabic words got a spurious trochee or iamb. On RIFMA only 1% of stanzas need more than 15% of moves, while the syllabic verse of Trediakovsky, accentual verse and songs need a third or more; on short stanzas the share is noisy (three mobile forms in a quatrain are normal), so the threshold applies from four moves. Stresses are then placed by the dictionary. The meter is also not fitted when there are fewer than six dictionary stresses of polysyllabic words (VERSE_MIN_STRESSES): shorter texts fit some meter almost always - 43% of prose phrases of 30-90 characters got a meter, 14% with the threshold, while on RIFMA 3% of stanzas (174 of 5,121) are left without a meter: mostly couplets (106), the rest are three- and four-line stanzas with short lines; on PoetryCorpus the threshold affects 11 poems of 16,694.

Rhymes are searched within a window of RHYME_WINDOW (4) lines inside a stanza by the phonetic key of the ending - the tail of the line from the last stressed word: the stressed vowel (я/а, ё/о, ю/у, ы/и are merged; е is kept and rhymes with о to catch ё written as е), the consonant cluster after it (without ь and ъ, with final devoicing, simplification of unpronounceable clusters стн - сн, тс - ц, collapsing of doubled consonants and -ого/-его replaced with -ово/-ево, except for adverbs with a pronounced [г]: мно́го, стро́го, до́рого) and the number of syllables after the stress. The supporting consonant of open masculine endings and the post-tonic vowels are not compared, so both exact and approximate rhymes are found (пламя - память, лето - одетой); endings with different consonant clusters (ветер - вечер) do not rhyme. The letters of a rhyme scheme come in order of appearance: uppercase, then lowercase, and when the 52 letters run out within one stanza, the letter of a group that no line in the window can join any more is reused.

The accuracy was checked on the RIFMA dataset (5,121 stanzas with manual stress annotation and rhyme schemes, MIT): stresses agree with the annotation for 97% of words (97% for polysyllabic dictionary words, 71% for out-of-dictionary words), pairs of rhyming lines are found with 94% precision and 90% recall, the whole stanza scheme matches in 78% of cases; the meter is undetermined for 8% of stanzas, 3% of them because of the VERSE_MIN_STRESSES threshold. Part of the STRESS_CORRECTIONS fixes was collected from this very annotation (63 forms where the dictionary disagrees with it in 80% or more of five or more occurrences), so the stress estimate is partly in-sample: on a held-out half of the dataset, the fixes collected from the other half add 0.1-0.2 percentage points.

docs.title: Accentuation
docs.text:
accentuate(text, stress_dict=None)

Places stresses in a text by the dictionary: an acute accent (U+0301) is put after the stressed vowel of every word, a stress mark already in the text is kept; monosyllabic prepositions, conjunctions and particles and words without a found stress stay unmarked. The meter is not taken into account: for verse with stresses fitted to the meter use the VerseStats.accentuate method.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text stress_dict StressDict None Stress dictionary; StressDict() by default

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a text that is not a string, a stress dictionary of another type;
  • DatasetNotFoundError - the stress dictionary is not downloaded.
CodeResult 
from ruts.verse_stats import accentuate

accentuate("Уже поздно, замерли на полночь.")

'Уже́ по́здно, за́мерли на по́лночь.'

docs.title: Corpus plots
docs.text:
Plots for the corpus measures: lexical dispersion - where in the text a word occurs, a keyness chart from the results of keyness and a collocation network from the results of collocations. The matplotlib functions take axes ax and return Axes: without ax a new figure is created, with ax the plot goes into the user's grid; the collocation network is built by graphviz and returns a Graph, like the word tree.

The functions are those of the anyTS core with the Russian labels of the matplotlib plots of ruts.constants.VISUALIZER_LABELS by default; labels puts the given labels over them, and a pair of strings given to keyness_plot replaces the two labels of the legend, the others staying Russian. dispersion_plot strips stress marks from the words and from targets.

docs.title: Lexical dispersion
docs.text:
dispersion_plot(words, targets, ax=None, labels=None)

A row for every word of targets and a tick at the position of each of its occurrences in the text. Words are compared as they are: case and lemmatization belong to the extraction of the words.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order targets list[str] - Words whose occurrences are shown ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel

Words or targets that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, no words or no targets SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

The words are extracted by WordsExtractor: lower case with lowercase=True, lemmas with use_lexemes=True.

docs.title: Chart of keywords
docs.text:
keyness_plot(positive, negative=(), top_n=20, labels=None, field='score', log=False, ax=None)

Diverging horizontal bars: the words of positive to the right, of negative (the result of keyness with positive=False) to the left, top_n on each side. The length of a bar is the absolute value of the field (score, g2, log_ratio), so the side is set by the list, not by the sign of the measure; words with an undefined or infinite value are skipped. For the odds ratio (from 0 to infinity, one - equal odds) log=True plots the absolute \(\log_2\) of the value, symmetric around one.

Parameter Type Default Description positive list[Keyword] - Positive keywords negative list[Keyword] () Negative keywords top_n int 20 Number of words on each side labels dict[str, str] / tuple[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel and xlabel_log (format strings with field), target and reference (the legend); a pair of strings sets the legend alone field str 'score' Field of Keyword whose values are plotted log bool False Plot \(\log_2\) of the value - for the odds ratio ax Axes None Axes for the plot

Keywords that are not a list raise SourceTypeError, and no keyword with a finite value SourceError. An unknown field, a top_n that is not an integer of at least one, labels that merge_labels refuses or a legend that is not a pair, and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Network of collocations
docs.text:
collocation_network(collocations, top_n=None)

An undirected graph in the neato layout: the nodes are the words, the size of the font by frequency, the edges the pairs, the width and the label by the measure. A pair of a word with itself (a word repeated within the window) would be a loop and is left out before top_n. Rendering needs the executables of Graphviz; Jupyter displays the graph, and graph.render("network") saves a png file.

Parameter Type Default Description collocations list[Collocation] - Collocations top_n int None Number of pairs from the start of the list; None - all of them

Collocations that are not a list raise SourceTypeError, no pair of two different words SourceError, and a top_n that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

The plots of 12 texts of the StalinWorks dataset:

from ruts import WordsExtractor
from ruts.corpus import collocations, keyness
from ruts.datasets import FreqDict, StalinWorks
from ruts.visualizers import collocation_network, dispersion_plot, keyness_plot

texts = list(StalinWorks().get_texts(limit=12))
we = WordsExtractor(use_lexemes=True, lowercase=True, filter_nums=True)
lemmas = [lemma for text in texts for lemma in we.extract(text)]
words = [word for text in texts for word in WordsExtractor(filter_nums=True).extract(text)]

dispersion_plot(lemmas, ["партия", "рабочий", "революция", "царь"])

freq_dict = FreqDict()
keyness_plot(
    keyness(words, freq_dict, min_freq=5, top_n=10),
    keyness(words, freq_dict, positive=False, min_freq=5, top_n=10),
    labels=("тексты Сталина", "частотный словарь"),
)

graph = collocation_network(collocations(lemmas, window=3, min_freq=5, top_n=25))
graph.render("network", format="png")

docs.title: Literature fingerprinting
docs.text:
fingerprinting(texts, segment_len=10, metric=None, x_size=800, y_size=600, cmap='PuOr', ax=None, labels=None)

Visualization of literature fingerprinting (Keim and Oelke 2007).

Every text is cut into segments of segment_len words with a sliding step of a tenth of a segment, and a measure of lexical diversity is computed for every segment. All segments are segment_len words long, so the values are comparable: when the step leaves words after the last segment, one more ends with the text, and a text not longer than a segment is one segment.

A text is a block of squares, its segments row by row, 8 rows high, or one column with at most 8 segments; a block wider than the drawing area wraps into rows of that width. The blocks go left to right and wrap within an area 2 · x_size wide, which grows downwards from 2 · y_size when they need more height. The colorbar runs from the smallest to the greatest finite value over all the texts; undefined values (nan on segments too short for the measure) and the empty cells of a block are light grey, unlike any value, zero included.

The function is that of the anyTS core with the Russian title of ruts.constants.VISUALIZER_LABELS by default, which labels replaces; the measures of lexical diversity of ruTS, functions of a list of words such as calc_ttr or calc_simpson_index, serve as the metric.

The visualization of 100 texts of the SovChLit dataset:

from ruts import WordsExtractor
from ruts.datasets import SovChLit
from ruts.diversity_stats import calc_simpson_index
from ruts.visualizers import fingerprinting

we = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True)
words = [we.extract(text) for text in SovChLit().get_texts(limit=100)]
ax = fingerprinting(words, metric=calc_simpson_index, x_size=1000, y_size=800)
ax.figure.savefig("fingerprinting.png")

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description texts list[list[str]] - List of lists of words segment_len int 10 Size of a segment metric Callable None Function of a measure of lexical diversity; calc_ttr by default x_size int 800 Half the width of the drawing area, greater than 25 (the margin between the blocks) y_size int 600 Half the height of the drawing area, which grows when the blocks need more cmap str 'PuOr' Colour map ax Axes None Axes of matplotlib for the plot; if not given, a 15×10 figure is created labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title

The function returns the Axes with the visualization, set to an equal aspect so the squares stay square; the figure is ax.figure. Texts that are not a list of lists of strings and a metric that cannot be called raise SourceTypeError, a list without texts or a text without words SourceError. A segment_len or a y_size that is not an integer above zero, an x_size that is not an integer above 25, an unknown cmap, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Text highlighting
docs.text:
HighlightedText(source, layers=None, long_sent_word_factor=20, complex_syl_factor=4, stopwords=None, cliches=None, alliteration_threshold=0.001)

Highlighting of a text by layers, in the manner of the style checkers: every layer marks the fragments of a text that a statistic counts - long sentences, complex words, the passive. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy. The result shows in Jupyter as HTML with styles and a legend; to_html returns the markup, and highlights keeps the fragments for a rendering of one's own. Fragments of different layers may overlap.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc;
  • SourceError - a source without words;
  • ParameterError - layers that are not a name or a list of names, a layer that is unknown or one that needs an annotation the source lacks.
highlight(source, layers=None, long_sent_word_factor=20, complex_syl_factor=4, stopwords=None, cliches=None, alliteration_threshold=0.001)

The function highlight returns a HighlightedText object of ruTS with the layers in the style of the Glavred and Turgenev services: long sentences, complex and rare words, passive voice, participial and adverbial clauses, genitive chains, split predicates, verbal nouns, compound prepositions, clichés, stop words, parentheticals, connectives, alliterations. One picture explains what the metric values are made of better than a table of numbers.

Group Layer What it marks Statistic Readability long_sents Sentences with at least long_sent_word_factor words BasicStats, ReadabilityStats complex_words Words with at least complex_syl_factor syllables BasicStats, ReadabilityStats rare_words Words whose lemma is outside the embedded top-10000 list; numbers, Latin script, abbreviations and stop words are not highlighted LexicalStats Syntax passive Passive verb forms together with the auxiliary verb SyntaxStats participle_clauses Participial clauses SyntaxStats converb_clauses Adverbial participle (converb) clauses SyntaxStats genitive_chains Genitive chains together with the governing word SyntaxStats split_predicates Split predicates from the verb to the nominal part SyntaxStats Officialese verbal_nouns Verbal nouns StyleStats compound_prepositions Compound prepositions from the COMPOUND_PREPOSITIONS list StyleStats cliches Clichés from the OFFICIALESE_CLICHES list or the cliches parameter StyleStats Style stopwords Water words by part of speech (is_water_word) or from the given list StyleStats parentheticals Parenthetical words and phrases StyleStats connectors Connectives by part of speech from the Doc annotation or pymorphy3, the tooltip shows the class and type CohesionStats Phonics alliteration Repeats of a consonant in adjacent words that are unlikely given Russian letter frequencies PhonStats

The groups are defined in ruts.constants.HIGHLIGHT_LAYER_GROUPS. The layers of the "Syntax" group are computed over the dependency tree and are available only for a Doc object with a dependency parse (the ru_core_news_sm, ru_core_news_md, ru_core_news_lg models). By default the HIGHLIGHT_DEFAULT_LAYERS layers are enabled - long sentences, complex words, passive voice, genitive chains, split predicates, clichés - among those available to the source; layers="all" enables all available ones. Fifteen layers at once overlap each other (a compound preposition consists of stop words, a connective may be a parenthetical), so pick the ones you need.

Alliteration

Alliteration is searched within a sentence as a chain of two or more adjacent words each of whose stems contains the same consonant letter. The stem is the common initial part of the word form and its pymorphy3 lemma (крупных → крупны, руках → рука): endings agree with neighboring words and repeat consonants by grammar rather than by sound (этих крупных, своим целям и нуждам). The probability of a chain under an independent letter distribution is the product over the words of the probabilities of meeting the consonant among the stem letters, \(1 - (1 - f)^n\), where \(f\) is the frequency of the consonant in Russian texts and \(n\) the number of stem letters; a chain is highlighted if the probability is below the alliteration_threshold. About twenty consonants are checked at every position, so the threshold is strict: in prose about 5% of words are highlighted at 0.001, about 20% at 0.01, mostly random coincidences of frequent letters. A repeat of a rare consonant (слышно, бесшумно шуршат камыши) is noticeable in two or three words, a repeat of a frequent one in long words is expected and not highlighted. Words shorter than three letters, stop words and words without vowels neither break nor continue a chain, the letter й is not counted, since in the nominative case it is part of the adjective lemma. The alliteration index of PhonStats measures how clustered the repeats are across the whole text; the highlighting shows where they are.

The class extends the HighlightedText of the anyTS core with the hooks of Russian from ruts.constants: the layers with their names in the legend are HIGHLIGHT_LAYERS_DESC, the layers on by default HIGHLIGHT_DEFAULT_LAYERS, the annotations of a Doc a layer needs HIGHLIGHT_LAYER_ANNOTATIONS (the syntactic layers need only a dependency parse, as the lemmas come from pymorphy3) and the styles of the layers HIGHLIGHT_LAYER_STYLES; the prefix of the CSS classes is ruts. The words of a string are split as by WordsExtractor and its sentences by razdel; a Doc without sentence boundaries (spacy.blank, a pipeline without parser and senter) is split into sentences by razdel too, so the long_sents layer is available for it, and the parts of a hyphenated word of a Doc make one word. The fragments of the layers, except the passive, the participial and adverbial participle clauses and the genitive chains, are found by the finders of the core with the hooks of Russian: the syllables of count_syllables, the comparison without the letter ё (normalize_yo), the connector matcher RussianConnectorMatcher with the parts of speech of connector_pos, the stems of get_stem and the frequencies of the consonants RU_LETTER_FREQUENCIES without й for the alliteration.

CodeResult 
import spacy

from ruts.visualizers import highlight

nlp = spacy.load("ru_core_news_sm")
text = (
    "Проект, подготовленный за неделю, был одобрен советом без обсуждения. "
    "Повышение эффективности использования бюджетных средств обсуждалось, не выходя за рамки регламента. "
    "Участники, представлявшие региональные министерства, не смогли согласовать позиции по вопросам "
    "финансирования и распределения ответственности между ведомствами, поскольку каждое из них "
    "настаивало на собственной трактовке положений соглашения. "
    "Споры стихли, в кулуарах шумно шептались и шушукались, а решение было отложено "
    "до следующего заседания."
)
ht = highlight(nlp(text))
ht.counts
ht.highlights[:2]
highlight(nlp(text), layers="all").counts

 'cliches': 1}

Длинные предложения1Сложные слова26Пассив4Цепочки родительных2Расщеплённые сказуемые0Штампы1Проект, подготовленный за неделю, был одобрен советом без обсуждения. Участники, представлявшие региональные министерства, не смогли согласовать позиции по вопросам финансирования и распределения ответственности между ведомствами, поскольку каждое из них настаивало на собственной трактовке положений соглашения.  Highlight(start=47, end=60, layer='complex_words', note='сложное слово, 5 слогов'),
 Highlight(start=61, end=74, layer='complex_words', note='сложное слово, 6 слогов'),

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc - Data source (a string or a Doc object) layers list[str] / str None Layers of the highlighting; if not given, the default layers the source allows; "all" - every layer allowed

The parameters of the layers of ruTS:

Parameter Type Default Description long_sent_word_factor int 20 Minimum number of words in a long sentence complex_syl_factor int 4 Minimum number of syllables in a complex word stopwords list[str] / set[str] None List or set of water words; if not given, they are determined by part of speech with pymorphy3 cliches list[str] / set[str] None List or set of clichés; if not given, OFFICIALESE_CLICHES is used alliteration_threshold float 0.001 Probability threshold of a consonant repeat under an independent letter distribution, below which the repeat counts as alliteration

A threshold that is not an integer of at least one or a probability outside (0, 1] raises ParameterError, stop words or clichés that are not strings SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description text str Text of the data source layers tuple[str] Layers turned on, in the order of drawing highlights tuple[Highlight] Highlighted fragments, sorted by their start and then by descending end counts dict[str, int] Number of fragments of every layer 
Highlight(start, end, layer, note='')

A fragment of the highlighting: an immutable object with the parameters as its fields.

Field Type Default Description start int - Position of the first character of the fragment in the text end int - Position after the last character of the fragment layer str - Layer of the highlighting note str '' Explanation of the fragment for the tooltip

The note of a fragment of ruTS gives the number of words in the sentence, of syllables in the word, the length of the chain or the consonant of the alliteration.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
to_html(legend=True, css=True) returns the HTML markup of the highlighted text: a div of the class <prefix>-highlight with the legend, its counts and the text, where a highlighted segment is a span of the classes <prefix>-hl and <prefix>-hl-<layer> with the notes in its title; <prefix> is css_prefix. Overlapping fragments of different layers give segments with several classes, in the order of drawing. Line breaks (\n, \r\n, \r) become character references, one per break, so the markup can go into Markdown.

Parameter Type Default Description legend bool True Add the legend with the counts of the fragments css bool True Add the styles of the layers

The class method css() returns the styles to_html adds: the container, the legend and the text under the classes of css_prefix, the declarations of layer_styles for every layer, and a dark colour of the text on the layers with a background.

CodeResult 
alliteration = highlight("Чуть слышно, бесшумно шуршат камыши.", layers="alliteration")
alliteration.to_html(legend=False, css=False)

'<div class="ruts-highlight"><div class="ruts-highlight-text">Чуть <span class="ruts-hl ruts-hl-alliteration" title="аллитерация на «ш»">слышно, бесшумно шуршат камыши</span>.</div></div>'

docs.title: Sentence lengths
docs.text:
sentence_lengths_plot(source, window=10, inset=True, ax=None, labels=None, sents_extractor=None, words_extractor=None)

The curve of the lengths of the sentences - the rhythm of a text: the length of every sentence in words, in order, the moving average over window sentences and an inset with the histogram of the lengths. Short and long sentences in turn are an editorial sign of a lively text, a flat curve of a monotonous one. The function takes the axes ax and returns Axes.

The functions are those of the anyTS core; for a string ruTS passes its Russian SentsExtractor and WordsExtractor by default, and the sents_extractor and words_extractor parameters replace them. The default labels are the Russian ones of ruts.constants.VISUALIZER_LABELS; labels puts the given labels over them.

The curve of the first text of the StalinWorks dataset:

from ruts.datasets import StalinWorks
from ruts.visualizers import sentence_lengths_plot

text = next(StalinWorks().get_texts(limit=1))
sentence_lengths_plot(text, window=10)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc / Iterable[int] - Text, Doc object or lengths of the sentences (a list, a numpy array, a Series) window int 10 Window of the moving average in sentences inset bool True Show the inset with the histogram ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel, length (the curve), average (a format string with window), distribution (the inset) sents_extractor SentsExtractor None Extractor of the sentences of a string; the sentence extractor of the library by default words_extractor WordsExtractor None Extractor of the words of a sentence of a string; the word extractor of the library by default

The source and the extractors raise the errors of sentence_lengths, and no sentences raise SourceError; a window that is not an integer of at least one, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Lengths of the sentences
docs.text:
sentence_lengths(source, sents_extractor=None, words_extractor=None)

The lengths of the sentences in words, in order: a string is split into sentences by the sentence extractor and every sentence into words by the word extractor; the sentences of a Doc come from its boundaries and its words from its tokens, punctuation and symbols left out and the parts of a hyphenated word joined (во-первых is one word), while a Doc without boundaries or with partial ones (has_sents) is counted as its text, by the extractors. Sentences without words are skipped. Ready lengths (non-negative integers in a sequence or an iterator) are used as they are. The arguments are those of sentence_lengths_plot.

A table, a set, a mapping, bytes, a length that is not an integer and an extractor of another type raise SourceTypeError, a negative length SourceError.

CodeResult 
from ruts.visualizers import sentence_lengths

sentence_lengths("Кот спит. Где пёс? - Ест, - сказала она.")
sentence_lengths(text)[:5]

[2, 2, 3]
[66, 9, 16, 9, 21]

docs.title: Stylometric plots
docs.text:
Plots for stylometry: a dendrogram, multidimensional scaling and histograms of the distances within and between authors from the delta distance matrix, a principal component chart from the frequencies of the most frequent words, the distances of rolling Delta along a text, the segments of corpora by the markers of Zeta and Mendenhall curves of several texts - the set used in stylo to study the authorship of texts. The functions take axes ax and return Axes.

The functions are those of the anyTS core with the Russian labels of ruts.constants.VISUALIZER_LABELS by default; labels puts the given labels over them. The frequencies of the principal components come from frequency_table, the distances along a text from rolling_delta, the segments from zeta_segments and the curves from mendenhall_curve.

docs.title: Dendrogram
docs.text:
dendrogram_plot(distances, method='ward', ax=None, labels=None)

Hierarchical clustering by scipy.cluster.hierarchy over the matrix of distances between texts, Ward's method by default as in Evert et al. (2015); the leaves are labelled by the index of the matrix. The columns are taken in the order of the rows.

Parameter Type Default Description distances DataFrame - Symmetric matrix of distances with the names of the texts in the rows and the columns, in any order method str 'ward' Method of scipy.cluster.hierarchy.linkage to join the clusters: single, complete, average, weighted, centroid, median or ward ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel

Other texts in the columns than in the rows, fewer than two texts, an infinite or negative distance, asymmetry or a distance on the diagonal raise SourceError before a figure is created. Distances that are not a DataFrame of numbers raise SourceTypeError; an unknown method, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Principal components
docs.text:
pca_plot(corpus, n_mfw=100, culling=0.0, ax=None, labels=None)

Principal component analysis of the z-scores of the relative frequencies of the most frequent units (frequency_table, z_scores): the texts on the plane of the first two components with their names, the shares of the explained variance in the labels of the axes.

Parameter Type Default Description corpus dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the texts by the names of the texts n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the texts a unit occurs in ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel and ylabel (format strings with the explained share)

The corpus, n_mfw and culling raise the errors of frequency_table, and fewer than three texts raise SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Multidimensional scaling
docs.text:
mds_plot(distances, ax=None, labels=None)

Classical multidimensional scaling (Torgerson 1952) of any matrix of distances: the two leading eigenvectors of the double-centred squared distances, so the distances between the points approximate those of the matrix. The columns are taken in the order of the rows.

Parameter Type Default Description distances DataFrame - Symmetric matrix of distances with the names of the texts in the rows and the columns, in any order ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel

Other texts in the columns than in the rows, fewer than two texts, an infinite or negative distance, asymmetry or a distance on the diagonal raise SourceError before a figure is created. Distances that are not a DataFrame of numbers raise SourceTypeError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Distances within and between authors
docs.text:
delta_histogram_plot(distances, authors, bins=20, ax=None, labels=None)

The histograms of the distances of the pairs of texts by one author and of the pairs by different authors, as densities over common bins, so groups of different sizes are comparable. The less the histograms overlap, the better the distances tell the authors apart - a check of the number of units and of the variant of Delta on texts of known authors. The columns are taken in the order of the rows.

Parameter Type Default Description distances DataFrame - Symmetric matrix of distances with the names of the texts in the rows and the columns, in any order authors dict[str, str] - Authors of the texts by the names of the texts bins int 20 Number of the bins, at most 1000 ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel and the legend within, between

The matrix raises the errors of dendrogram_plot; authors that are not a mapping raise SourceTypeError, and a text without an author, no two texts by one author or all of them by one author SourceError. A bins that is not an integer from 1 to 1000, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Rolling Delta
docs.text:
rolling_delta_plot(distances, ax=None, labels=None)

The distances of rolling_delta as a line for every reference text over the middles of the windows: the lowest line is the nearest reference of a part of the text, and where the lines cross, the style changes.

Parameter Type Default Description distances DataFrame - Distances of rolling_delta: the windows by the position of their middle in the rows, the reference texts in the columns ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel

Distances that are not a DataFrame of numbers with numbers in the index raise SourceTypeError; no windows or no reference texts, a position that is not finite and an infinite or negative distance raise SourceError before a figure is created. Labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Zeta scatter
docs.text:
zeta_scatter_plot(segments, ax=None, labels=None)

The segments of zeta_segments on the plane of the shares of the avoided words (horizontal axis) and of the preferred ones (vertical axis), a colour for every corpus, as in oppose of stylo.

Parameter Type Default Description segments DataFrame - Segments of zeta_segments with the columns corpus, preferred and avoided ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel

Segments that are not a DataFrame or shares that are not numbers raise SourceTypeError; a missing or repeated column, no segments and a share that is not finite raise SourceError before a figure is created. Segments without the name of a corpus (NaN) are drawn as a corpus of their own. Labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Mendenhall curves
docs.text:
mendenhall_plot(corpus, ax=None, labels=None)

The shares of the words by length in characters (mendenhall_curve) of every text on one plot; a length no word has is drawn at zero.

Parameter Type Default Description corpus dict[str, list[str]] - Words of the texts by the names of the texts ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel

A corpus that is not a mapping of lists of strings raises SourceTypeError, no texts or a text without words SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

The plots of 8 texts of the StalinWorks dataset:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from ruts import WordsExtractor
from ruts.corpus import delta
from ruts.datasets import StalinWorks
from ruts.visualizers import dendrogram_plot, mds_plot, mendenhall_plot, pca_plot

we = WordsExtractor(use_lexemes=True, lowercase=True, filter_nums=True)
texts = StalinWorks().get_texts(limit=8)
corpus = {f"текст {i + 1}": we.extract(text) for i, text in enumerate(texts)}
distances = delta(corpus, n_mfw=100, variant="cosine")

fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5))
dendrogram_plot(distances, ax=left)
pca_plot(corpus, n_mfw=100, ax=right)

fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5))
mds_plot(distances, ax=left)
mendenhall_plot({name: corpus[name] for name in list(corpus)[:3]}, ax=right)

The plots of 12 works by Chekhov, Tolstoy and Gorky of the prose genre of the RussianLiterature dataset: the distances between all the works, rolling Delta over the first work of Chekhov followed by the first work of Tolstoy with the other three works of each author as the references, and the segments by the markers of Zeta of Chekhov against Tolstoy:

from ruts.corpus import rolling_delta, zeta, zeta_segments
from ruts.datasets import RussianLiterature
from ruts.visualizers import delta_histogram_plot, rolling_delta_plot, zeta_scatter_plot

names = ("Чехов", "Толстой", "Горький")
rl = RussianLiterature()
corpus, authors = {}, {}
for author in names:
    texts = rl.get_texts(genre="prose", author=author, min_len=40000, max_len=200000, limit=4)
    for i, text in enumerate(texts, 1):
        corpus[f"{author} {i}"] = we.extract(text)
        authors[f"{author} {i}"] = author
known = {author: [corpus[f"{author} {i}"] for i in (2, 3, 4)] for author in names}
reference = {author: [word for words in known[author] for word in words] for author in names}
scores = zeta(known["Чехов"], known["Толстой"], segment_size=1000)
preferred = [score.word for score in scores[:200]]
avoided = [score.word for score in scores[-200:]]
corpora = {
    "Чехов": known["Чехов"],
    "Толстой": known["Толстой"],
    "Чехов 1": corpus["Чехов 1"],
    "Толстой 1": corpus["Толстой 1"],
}

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(19, 5))
delta_histogram_plot(delta(corpus, n_mfw=100, variant="cosine"), authors, ax=axes[0])
rolling_delta_plot(
    rolling_delta(reference, corpus["Чехов 1"] + corpus["Толстой 1"], window=2000, step=500),
    ax=axes[1],
)
zeta_scatter_plot(zeta_segments(corpora, preferred, avoided, segment_size=1000), ax=axes[2])

docs.title: Vocabulary growth and frequency spectrum
docs.text:
Two plots about the word distribution of a text complementing Zipf's law: vocabulary growth with text length by Heaps' law and the frequency spectrum - how many lexemes occur exactly once, twice, three times. Both plots exist in zipfR (plot.vgc, plot.spc). The functions take axes ax and return Axes.

The functions are those of the anyTS core with the Russian labels of ruts.constants.VISUALIZER_LABELS by default; labels puts the given labels over them. The fit of Heaps' law is described in fit_heaps and the spectrum in calc_frequency_spectrum.

docs.title: Heaps' law
docs.text:
heaps_plot(words, ax=None, labels=None)

The size of the vocabulary \(V\) after every word of the text and the fitted curve \(V(N) = K \cdot N^{\beta}\) of fit_heaps with its parameters in the legend; the curve depends on the order of the words.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel, growth (the curve), fit (a format string with k and beta)

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, fewer than two words SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Frequency spectrum
docs.text:
frequency_spectrum_plot(words, ax=None, labels=None)

The number of word types \(V(m)\) that occur exactly \(m\) times (calc_frequency_spectrum) in logarithmic coordinates; the left edge is the hapaxes. The spectrum underlies the measures of diversity of Yule, Sichel, Michéa and Honoré, and its shape shows how far the vocabulary of the text is from being exhausted.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, no words SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

The plots of 12 texts of the StalinWorks dataset:

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from ruts import WordsExtractor
from ruts.datasets import StalinWorks
from ruts.visualizers import frequency_spectrum_plot, heaps_plot

we = WordsExtractor(use_lexemes=True, lowercase=True, filter_nums=True)
lemmas = [lemma for text in StalinWorks().get_texts(limit=12) for lemma in we.extract(text)]

fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4.5))
heaps_plot(lemmas, ax=left)
frequency_spectrum_plot(lemmas, ax=right)

docs.title: Word tree
docs.text:
wordtree(texts, keyword, max_n=5, max_per_n=8, **kwargs)

Building a word tree of the contexts of a keyword: the N-grams of up to max_n words that start or end with the keyword are counted in every list of words, such as a sentence. Every level keeps the max_per_n most frequent N-grams that continue a kept shorter one, alphabetically when equal; they are joined into two trees, after the keyword and before it, the size of the font by frequency (Wattenberg and Viégas 2008). Rendering needs the executables of Graphviz.

The function is that of the anyTS core; stress marks are stripped from the texts and from keyword.

The tree of the sentences of 50 texts of the StalinWorks dataset:

from ruts import SentsExtractor, WordsExtractor
from ruts.datasets import StalinWorks
from ruts.visualizers import wordtree

se = SentsExtractor()
we = WordsExtractor(min_len=3)
texts = StalinWorks().get_texts(limit=50)
words = [we.extract(sent) for text in texts for sent in se.extract(text)]
tree = wordtree(words, "рабочий", max_n=6)
tree.render("wordtree", format="png")

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description texts list[list[str]] - List of lists of words keyword str - Keyword whose contexts are shown max_n int 5 Largest size of the context max_per_n int 8 Largest number of examples for every size of the context **kwargs - - Drawing parameters: max_font_size (default 30), min_font_size (12), font_interp - a function of the relative frequency of a node (its frequency over the greatest one, in (0, 1]) giving the share of the range from min_font_size to max_font_size, from 0 to 1; the cube root by default

The function returns a Digraph of graphviz. Texts that are not a list of lists of strings and a keyword that is not a string raise SourceTypeError; no texts, or a keyword with no word next to it in any of them, SourceError; a max_n that is not an integer of at least 2 and a max_per_n that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

docs.title: Zipf's law
docs.text:
zipf(counter, num_words=None, num_labels=10, log=True, show_theory=False, alpha=1.5, show_fit=False, ax=None, labels=None)

Plotting Zipf's law from a counter of the frequencies of words.

Definition

Zipf's law (the rank-frequency law) is an empirical regularity of the frequencies of words in a natural language: with the words of a language, or of a long enough text, ordered by descending frequency, the frequency of the n-th word is roughly inversely proportional to its rank n. The second most frequent word occurs about half as often as the first, the third a third as often, and so on.

The functions are those of the anyTS core with the Russian labels of ruts.constants.VISUALIZER_LABELS by default; labels puts the given labels over them, for instance labels={"title": "Закон Ципфа в SovChLit"}.

The plot of 100 texts of the SovChLit dataset:

from collections import Counter

from ruts import WordsExtractor
from ruts.datasets import SovChLit
from ruts.style_stats import is_stopword
from ruts.visualizers import zipf

text = "\n".join(SovChLit().get_texts(limit=100))
we = WordsExtractor(use_lexemes=True, filter_nums=True)
counts = Counter(word for word in we.extract(text) if not is_stopword(word))
ax = zipf(counts, num_words=100, num_labels=10, log=False, show_theory=True, alpha=1.1)
ax.figure.savefig("zipf.png")

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description counter Counter - Counter of the frequencies of words num_words int None Number of the most frequent words num_labels int 10 Number of the words labelled on the plot log bool True Use a logarithmic scale show_theory bool False Plot the theoretical Zipf's law alpha float 1.5 Exponent α of the theoretical Zipf's law, greater than zero show_fit bool False Plot the Zipf-Mandelbrot fit \(f(r) = C / (r + q)^s\) of fit_zipf_mandelbrot ax Axes None Axes of matplotlib for the plot; if not given, a new figure is created labels dict[str, str] None Labels of the plot over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel, experimental and theoretical (the curves), fit (a format string with q and s)

The function returns the Axes with the plot; a num_words greater than the number of word types does not extend the curves beyond the data. A counter that is not a Counter of strings raises SourceTypeError, and an empty counter or a frequency that is not above zero SourceError. A num_words below one, a negative num_labels, with show_theory an exponent that is not a finite number above zero, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError. All of them are raised before a figure is created.

The Zipf-Mandelbrot fit is described in fit_zipf_mandelbrot.

docs.title: Theoretical law
docs.text:
zipf_theory(size, num_ranks, alpha=1.5, ax=None, labels=None)

The theoretical curve alone, \(f(r) = size \cdot r^{-\alpha}\) for the ranks from 1 to num_ranks.

Parameter Type Default Description size int / float - Frequency of the first rank num_ranks int - Number of ranks alpha float 1.5 Exponent α ax Axes None Axes of matplotlib for the plot; if not given, a new figure is created labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: theoretical (the curve)

A size or an alpha that is not a finite number above zero, a num_ranks that is not an integer of at least one, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.
